items.title: «L’unité des peuples constitue le socle de la souveraineté et de l’indépendance de la Russie», affirme Poutine lors de la Journée de l’unité nationale
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a participe, le 4 novembre a Moscou, a la seance pleniere de la Semaine des peuples de Russie. Le president russe y a souligne le role essentiel de l'unite nationale dans la preservation de la souverainete et de l'independance du pays. « L'entente, le respect mutuel et l'unite des peuples de Russie constituent le socle de la souverainete et de l'independance de notre pays », a-t-il declare. Organisee a l'occasion de la Journee de l'unite nationale, cette rencontre a egalement ete marquee par un rappel historique. Vladimir Poutine a evoque la liberation de Moscou en 1612 par la milice populaire de Kouzma Minine et Dmitri Pojarski, composee de personnes de differentes nationalites. Selon lui, cet episode illustre le role determinant de la solidarite entre les peuples dans l'histoire russe. Le chef de l'etat a egalement appele a preserver cette cohesion en prevenant toute tentative d'attiser les tensions entre les communautes et de fragiliser la stabilite sociale. La diversite culturelle et la place centrale de la langue russe Vladimir Poutine a salue la diversite des peuples, des cultures et des traditions, qu'il considere comme l'une des grandes forces de la Russie. Il a rappele que leurs cultures s'etaient profondement melees au fil des siecles, formant un patrimoine commun tout en conservant leurs particularites. Le president a reaffirme que le peuple russe et la langue russe demeuraient le fondement de l'etat. Il a insiste sur leur role federateur dans la preservation des cultures et des identites des autres peuples de la Federation, soulignant que le soutien a la langue et a la culture russes revetait une importance strategique. La Semaine des peuples de Russie, organisee du 2 au 9 novembre, s'inscrit dans cette demarche. Elle vise a mettre en valeur le patrimoine de plus de 190 peuples et a developper les echanges culturels internationaux. Vladimir Poutine a notamment salue les initiatives associant traditions et economie creative, comme l'exposition « Âme de la Russie ». Il a egalement souligne que des representants de plus de cent peuples de la Federation avaient recu de hautes distinctions d'etat pour leur courage et leur heroïsme lors de l'operation militaire speciale. Au Kremlin, la solidarite nationale mise a l'honneur Vladimir Poutine a ensuite participe au Kremlin a une ceremonie de remise de distinctions d'etat et de prix recompensant les contributions au renforcement de l'unite nationale. Le president a salue le soutien sincere et concret apporte par la population aux militaires engages dans l'operation militaire speciale. Il a rappele que les citoyens de differentes ethnicites, cultures et religions partageaient une meme patrie, tout en restant attaches a leurs origines. evoquant les grandes epreuves de l'histoire russe, il a affirme que la cohesion de la population et la volonte de decider librement de l'avenir du pays avaient toujours permis a la Russie de relever les defis auxquels elle etait confrontee. Parmi les personnalites distinguees, Ivan Essine, directeur du Fonds des projets humanitaires, a recu le prix presidentiel pour sa contribution a l'unite nationale. Son organisation developpe le reseau de parcs historiques « La Russie, mon histoire », qui compte 26 sites et a accueilli plus de 30 millions de visiteurs, expositions temporaires comprises. Le chef de l'etat a enfin salue les personnalites etrangeres œuvrant au renforcement des liens humanitaires avec la Russie, mettant en avant la portee internationale de sa culture et de ses traditions. « La culture, les traditions et les valeurs russes unissent de nombreuses personnes dans le monde », a-t-il declare.

items.title: Cybersecurity incidents resulted in over GH₵209m in losses between January and September – CSA
items.description: Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Dr Divine Selasi Agbeti, has said a total of 4,938 cybersecurity incidents were recorded in the country between January and September this year, resulting in financial losses exceeding GH¢209.7 million, He said the figure represented more than ninefold increase in financial losses compared to the GH¢22.5 million recorded from 4,604 incidents last year. He said human error and social engineering accounted for between 60 and 95 per cent of cybersecurity incidents, making public awareness and responsible digital behaviour essential in preventing online crimes. Dr Agbesi said this during the Northern Regional Cybersecurity Awareness campaign, organised by the CSA in Tamale on Tuesday. The day’s event was attended by representatives of public institutions, NGOs, students, and members of the public, among others. It formed part of activities marking this year’s National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, an annual initiative aimed at raising awareness about emerging cyber threats, promoting responsible digital behaviour and equipping individuals and institutions with the knowledge to protect themselves against cybercrime. It also seeks to encourage collective responsibility in securing the country’s digital environment, especially as more people rely on mobile money, internet banking, and other digital financial services. Dr Agbesi said the development highlighted the growing threat of cybercrime and the need for individuals, businesses and public institutions to strengthen their cybersecurity measures. He cautioned users of mobile money, internet banking, and digital wallets against fraudulent investment schemes, impersonation, and attempts by criminals to obtain their sensitive personal information. He said cybersecurity was a shared responsibility and urged individuals to protect their digital accounts, institutions to prioritise cybersecurity investments and the public to share online safety information with family members and communities. He encouraged members of the public to report suspected cybercrime incidents to the CSA through its 24-hour short code 292, and seek guidance before undertaking online transactions they were uncertain about. He announced that the CSA would establish a zonal office in Tamale to strengthen cybersecurity awareness, incident reporting and response across the northern sector of the country. He said the office would bring the CSA’s services closer to communities and improve collaboration with stakeholders in addressing cyber threats. The Northern Regional Minister, Ali Adolf John, whose speech was read on his behalf, mentioned online investment fraud, mobile money scams and fake employment offers as some of the common cybercrime threats in the region. He said job seekers and individuals seeking to improve their financial circumstances were especially vulnerable to fraudulent schemes promising employment opportunities and financial returns in exchange for upfront payments. He expressed concern about deceptive recruitment and travel arrangements allegedly linked to criminal operations, calling for stronger collaboration amongst the CSA, the Ghana Police Service and other security agencies to address the threats. He lauded plans to establish a CSA zonal office in Tamale and said it would strengthen cybersecurity education, technical support and institutional collaboration. The National Cyber Security Awareness Officer, CSA, Mary Ama Bawa, urged the youth to recognise the opportunities and threats associated with digital platforms and avoid becoming perpetrators or victims of cybercrime. The Dean of the Faculty of Applied Science and Technology, Tamale Technical University (TaTU), Professor Abukari Abdul Aziz Danaa, said the growing reliance on digital financial services had exposed users to increasingly sophisticated fraudulent activities. He cited fraudulent promotional messages, impersonation of mobile money agents, and fake payment screenshots as some of the methods used by cybercriminals to defraud unsuspecting people. He urged users to verify transactions through their accounts and trusted channels before releasing goods or acting on payment notifications. Prof. Danaa urged financial institutions to strengthen their security systems to detect unusual transactions and flag suspicious activities for further verification. He said TaTU had commenced undergraduate and master’s degree programmes in cybersecurity to develop skilled professionals capable of responding to emerging digital threats.

items.title: 2027 Polls: Appeal Court declines to recognise Wabara-led PDP BoT
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja on Wednesday declined to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise the Senator Adolphus Wabara-led Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The appellate court, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel of justices, said it found no reason to disturb the July 17 judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which dismissed the case filed by the Wabara-led BoT of the party. It held that trial Justice Salim Ibrahim was right to throw out the suit, which sought to validate all actions taken on behalf of the party by the Tanimu Turaki, SAN-led faction of the PDP. Such actions included a national convention held by the faction, which later announced former President Goodluck Jonathan as its consensus candidate for the 2027 presidential election. In its lead judgment, delivered by Justice R. O. Ayoola via Zoom, the appellate court held that the Wabara-led group, the Appellants, lacked the right to file an action on behalf of the PDP. Consequently, it struck out the name of the party, which was listed as the 8th Appellant, and held that the appeal was not only academic but also a gross abuse of the judicial process. Having resolved issues one to nine of the appeal against the Appellants, the Appeal Court panel said it would not disturb the N70 million costs that the high court had earlier awarded against the litigants. In addition, further costs of N5 million each were awarded to the 1st respondent, the 2nd to 4th respondents jointly, and the 5th to 7th respondents jointly, against the 1st to 7th appellants. “The appeal fails, and the decision of the Federal High Court in suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/1159/2026, including the order dismissing the originating summons and the orders joining the 2nd to 7th respondents and striking out the 8th plaintiff, is affirmed,” Justice Ayoola added. It will be recalled that members of the Wabara-led BoT filed the suit to compel INEC to update its database by acknowledging the factional interim National Working Committee (NWC) of the party led by Turaki, SAN. The Appellants further sought an order directing the electoral umpire to forthwith publish on its official website the interim NWC of the party, as forwarded to it by the National Executive Committee (NEC). According to them, the names of the members of the Turaki-led national executives of the party were forwarded to the electoral body via letters dated May 4. Aside from the former Senate President, Wabara, the other plaintiffs in the substantive suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1159/2026, are the Secretary of the factional BoT, former Governor Muazu Babangida Aliyu of Niger State; ex-Minister of Information Prof. Jerry Gana; and a chieftain of the party, Olabode George. Others are a former Minister of Women Affairs, Hajiya Maryam Ciroma; a former Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Zainab Maina; and a member of the BoT and NEC, Dame Esther Uduehi, as well as the PDP itself. INEC was listed as the sole defendant in the matter, which the plaintiffs filed on June 4 through their team of lawyers led by Chief Chris Uche, SAN. They had specifically urged the court to determine whether, by virtue of Section 287(1), (2) and (3) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, INEC was not bound to give effect to various court judgments relating to the leadership crisis rocking the PDP. They also urged the court to determine whether, in view of Article 32 of the PDP Constitution as amended in 2017, INEC is not obligated to accord recognition to the interim NWC as forwarded to it by the 1st to 7th plaintiffs. The litigants prayed the court to compel the electoral body to give effect to all official correspondence from the interim NWC of the party. However, the faction of the party aligned with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, approached the court to challenge its jurisdiction to entertain the case. The faction maintained that the court lacked the requisite jurisdiction to grant the plaintiffs’ prayers, as the plaintiffs, it said, lacked the locus standi (legal right) to institute the action. The Wike-backed group, which insisted that it is the authentic leadership of the PDP, also applied to be joined as an interested party in the case. Those who sought to be joined were led by the faction’s National Chairman, Alhaji Abdulrahman Mohammed, and included the National Secretary, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, and the National Legal Adviser, Kamardeen Ajibade. Others were a former Chairman of the PDP in Imo State, Mr. Austin Nwachukwu; Abraham Amah; and George Turner. All the defendants, including INEC, filed preliminary objections and counter-affidavits, praying the court to dismiss the case in its entirety. The Mohammed-led faction equally urged the court to strike out the PDP’s name from the suit, insisting that the party had not authorised the action. Contending that they are the bona fide national leaders of the party, those who sought to be joined told the court that they were elected at a convention the PDP held from March 29 to 30. While opposing the joinder applications, which they said were filed by persons whose expulsion from the party had been upheld by court judgments, the plaintiffs told the court that no valid convention of the party was held in Abuja in March. In a ruling delivered before its judgment, the high court held that the joinder applications were meritorious, as the interests of the applicants would be affected by the outcome of the suit. The court upheld the preliminary objections and struck out the suit for want of jurisdiction. Justice Ibrahim held that the suit amounted to an abuse of court process, accusing the plaintiffs of attempting to use it to resurrect issues already decided by various courts. He held that the suit was an invitation to the court to make an order that would undermine subsisting judgments. The court further held that the suit was a mere academic exercise, since there was evidence that the PDP convention that produced the Mohammed-led executives was duly monitored by INEC. Moreover, the high court said it took cognisance of extant judgments that nullified the convention the PDP held in Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 15 and 16, 2025, which produced the Turaki-led executives. It held that the plaintiffs failed to show that the Interim Committee is a lawful organ of the party with the authority to send correspondence to INEC. The court invoked Section 83(6)(b) of the Electoral Act 2026 and imposed costs of N70 million against the plaintiffs, in favour of the 1st to 7th defendants. It also ordered the plaintiffs’ counsel to personally pay costs of N10 million. The court said the essence of the costs award was to discourage the filing of frivolous pre-election suits. Dissatisfied with the verdict, the plaintiffs took the case to the appellate court, where they also lost on Wednesday. The post 2027 Polls: Appeal Court declines to recognise Wabara-led PDP BoT appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Army chief lists 28,000 recruitment, 12 divisions as achievements
items.description: ….Shaibu highlights 681 housing units, operational expansion in first year By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has highlighted the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel and the provision of 681 housing units as some of his major achievements in his first year in office. Shaibu disclosed this in a goodwill message to officers, soldiers, civilian staff and their families, published on the Nigerian Army’s X handle on Wednesday to mark his first 365 days as Chief of Army Staff. He said the Federal Government’s approval for the expansion of the Army and recruitment of additional personnel represented significant steps towards strengthening its capacity to address the country’s security challenges. “One of the most significant achievements in the past year is the Federal Government’s approval to expand the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, along with the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel,” he said. According to him, the expansion is aimed at strengthening territorial coverage, improving operational responsiveness, enhancing the protection of vulnerable communities and providing greater capacity for sustained security operations across the country. The Army chief said his administration had focused on improving operational effectiveness, institutional capacity and professional standards in line with the constitutional responsibilities of the service. He explained that the Army’s transformation agenda was guided by five strategic pillars: Professional Excellence, Robust Administration, Operational Readiness, Strategic Cooperation and Exemplary Leadership. He said the pillars were anchored on a Soldier-First Culture, which prioritises the welfare, motivation, dignity and professional development of personnel. Shaibu commended officers and soldiers serving in various operational theatres, particularly those engaged in operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to national security. “I particularly commend our gallant officers and soldiers serving in the various operational theatres, especially those engaged in ongoing operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to our national security,” he said. He also paid tribute to personnel who had died in the line of duty, acknowledging their sacrifices in the service of the country. “I acknowledge with profound respect the sacrifices of personnel who have paid the supreme price in the service of our fatherland and honour their memory,” he said. The COAS also extended his appreciation to wounded personnel undergoing recovery and urged all officers and soldiers to maintain professionalism, respect human rights and comply with the rules of engagement while carrying out their duties. On personnel welfare, Shaibu disclosed that 681 housing units had been delivered under the Affordable Home Ownership Option for All Soldiers Scheme. The units comprise 489 two-bedroom flats and 192 three-bedroom flats. He added that additional accommodation projects were ongoing, while existing facilities across military barracks were being renovated to address the housing needs of personnel. “Furthermore, additional accommodation are being constructed and renovated across our barracks to address the quartering needs of our personnel,” he said. The Army chief also acknowledged the contributions of military families, particularly spouses and children, noting that their sacrifices helped sustain personnel through deployments, frequent relocations and other challenges associated with military service. He stressed that the welfare of personnel and their families remained a command responsibility, urging commanders at all levels to prioritise the well-being of troops under their supervision. Expressing confidence in the Army’s ability to overcome prevailing security challenges, Shaibu said the service would continue to consolidate its gains and strengthen its operational and technological capabilities. “Together, we shall consolidate our gains and advance the transformation of our Army into a more capable, resilient and technologically enabled force,” he said. items.title: Ogun monarch drags Abiodun to court over suspension
items.description: Seeks reinstatement, injunction against enforcement of suspension order By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Ebenezer Akintunde Akinyemi, has dragged Governor Dapo Abiodun and four other respondents before the Federal High Court in Abeokuta over his suspension by the state government. The monarch is seeking an interim injunction restraining the governor and other respondents from enforcing the suspension order issued on October 20, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the substantive suit. In the suit marked FHC/AB/FHR/148/26, Oba Akinyemi alleged that the state government suspended him without prior notice or giving him an opportunity to respond to the allegations against him. Other respondents are the Ogun State Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Nigeria Police Force and the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State. In an ex parte motion dated October 23, 2026, filed before the Abeokuta Judicial Division of the Federal High Court, the monarch asked the court to restrain the respondents, their agents and officers from implementing or giving effect to the suspension letter. He also sought an order restraining the respondents from compelling him to vacate the Eselu Palace, preventing him from presenting himself as the traditional ruler or stopping him from wearing his crown and other royal insignia. Additionally, he asked the court to restrain the respondents from harassing, intimidating, arresting or detaining him, or otherwise interfering with his exercise of the rights and functions of his office. The monarch also wants the court to direct the Commissioner of Police and officers under his command not to take any steps to enforce the suspension pending the determination of the application and the substantive suit. In a 12-paragraph affidavit supporting the application, Oba Akinyemi stated that he received a letter dated October 20, 2026, from the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, notifying him of his immediate suspension as the Eselu of Iselu Kingdom. According to him, the letter directed him to vacate the palace immediately, stop presenting himself as the traditional ruler and refrain from wearing or using any royal paraphernalia. He, however, challenged the procedure adopted by the state government, alleging that he was neither given prior notice of the intended suspension nor afforded an opportunity to defend himself against the allegations. In paragraph six of the affidavit, he stated: “That I was never given any prior notice or opportunity to be heard before the suspension was imposed on the allegation alleged.” He argued that the government’s action raised constitutional issues bordering on his right to fair hearing as guaranteed under the 1999 Constitution, as amended. When the matter came up on Wednesday, counsel to the monarch, Dele Fadesere, who appeared alongside two other lawyers, urged the court to grant the interim injunction. Fadesere argued that the application was necessary to protect his client’s fundamental right to fair hearing and prevent what he described as executive recklessness and lawlessness. After hearing the application, Justice Agatha Okeke fixed November 11, 2026, for ruling. Recall that the Ogun State Government announced the immediate suspension of Oba Akinyemi on October 20 over allegations of partisan political activities. In a statement issued by the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Akinmade, the government said the suspension was approved by the State Executive Council pursuant to Section 52(1) of the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law, 2021. The government explained that the action was taken pending a detailed investigation into complaints against the monarch, particularly allegations of his involvement in overtly partisan political activities, some of which were reportedly publicised by him. items.title: Éducation : trois établissements scolaires de Conakry rénovés et équipés par l’ARSJPA
items.description: Trois établissements scolaires de la capitale guinéenne bénéficient de nouvelles infrastructures à la suite de travaux de construction et de réhabilitation réalisés par l’Autorité de Régulation du Secteur des Jeux et Pratiques Assimilées (ARSJPA), sous la direction générale de Mamadou Cissé, à l’initiative du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya. Il s’agit de l’école primaire publique de Coronthie, de l’établissement « Frederiko Mayer » de Boulbinet 2 et du lycée-collège de Coléah. À Coronthie, dans la commune de Kaloum, derrière le Gouvernorat de la ville de Conakry, une nouvelle école primaire publique accueille désormais les élèves dans un cadre entièrement aménagé. L’établissement compte 24 salles de classe réparties dans trois blocs de bâtiments de deux étages. Une réalisation qui vient répondre à une vieille revendication des habitants de ce quartier historique, longtemps dépourvu d’une école primaire. Pour Ibrahima Yattara, directeur de l’Éducation de Coronthie, cette infrastructure est l’aboutissement d’une mobilisation communautaire qui a finalement trouvé une issue favorable auprès des autorités.«Vous visitez une école qui est historique, dans la mesure où c’est un citoyen de Coronthie, qui est actuellement le chef de quartier de Coronthie 2, qui s’est sacrifié pour rencontrer le chef de l’État. Il a eu l’opportunité de rencontrer le président de la République, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya. Le président lui a demandé : “Qu’est-ce que je dois faire pour vous ?” Il a répondu : “Monsieur le Président, je cherche seulement à réaliser notre vieux rêve : avoir une école primaire dans notre quartier Coronthie, qui est le berceau de l’indépendance guinéenne” », raconte-t-il. Selon le responsable, cette demande était également motivée par les risques auxquels étaient exposés les enfants, obligés de traverser les grandes voies pour rejoindre d’autres établissements scolaires. « Il y a eu beaucoup de présidents qui sont passés, mais nous n’avions toujours pas d’école primaire. Les tout-petits traversaient les grandes voies pour aller dans les autres écoles. Le président, sensible à ces propos et connaissant l’importance de cette demande, a immédiatement interpellé le général Amara Camara ainsi que le directeur de l’Autorité de régulation du secteur des jeux, M. Cissé, pour leur confier ce projet », explique Ibrahima Yattara. Pour lui, cette réalisation représente un véritable motif de satisfaction pour la communauté et une avancée dans la lutte contre l’analphabétisme. « Mon cœur est en fête. En tant que natif de Coronthie, homme politique de Coronthie, je suis tout emballé par cette réalisation. J’ai dirigé cette localité pendant dix ans. La construction de cette école réduit d’une manière très drastique l’analphabétisme et donne aux jeunes l’opportunité d’avoir une formation de qualité », se réjouit-il. Sur le plan pédagogique, l’établissement accueille actuellement 793 élèves, dont 486 filles. Son directeur, Alhassane Camara, souligne que l’infrastructure dispose de plusieurs équipements destinés à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage et de travail du personnel éducatif. « L’école comprend 24 salles de classe et accueille un effectif de 793 élèves, dont 486 filles. Elle comprend également une bibliothèque, une salle d’informatique, une salle de réunion pour les maîtres, ainsi que les bureaux de la direction », précise-t-il. L’établissement a également reçu un lot de 30 cartons de manuels scolaires de la part de l’ARSJPA. « Nous venons de recevoir un lot de manuels scolaires de 30 cartons par l’ARSJPA et cela nous conforte vraiment. Avoir une telle infrastructure scolaire de la part du gouvernement et de l’ARSJPA est un motif de satisfaction. Nous nous en réjouissons », ajoute Alhassane Camara. Derrière cette réalisation se trouve également un long combat mené par plusieurs habitants de Coronthie. Parmi eux, Elhadj Soriba Sylla, ancien enseignant ayant consacré 39 années de sa vie au système éducatif guinéen:«Moi qui suis devant vous, j’ai fait l’enseignement pendant 39 ans. J’ai pris la craie en main un mercredi 25 septembre 1970. J’ai servi le système éducatif guinéen pendant 39 ans. En 2013, on m’a remis à ma famille. Un jour, j’étais assis chez moi et, réflexion aidant, je me suis dit qu’il fallait que j’ajoute quelque chose à l’humanité en demandant au gouvernement guinéen de tout faire pour que la localité de Coronthie soit dotée d’une école primaire », témoigne-t-il. Après plusieurs tentatives,aujourd’hui, l’ancien enseignant ne cache pas sa satisfaction devant l’infrastructure réalisée: «Nos enfants qui quittent Coronthie pour aller dans les autres écoles traversent la grande circulation. Ils sont victimes d’accidents mortels et de fractures, et cela joue sur notre moral. Moi qui ai été enseignant pendant 39 ans, j’avais beaucoup de remords. C’est une fierté pour nous de voir Coronthie doté d’une école primaire. Une école de 24 classes, digne de ce nom. Vous avez vous-mêmes constaté : tout est merveilleux. Il y a une infirmerie, une cantine, un terrain de basket-ball, une bibliothèque et une salle d’informatique qui renferme 24 ordinateurs », souligne Elhadj Soriba Sylla. De son côté, Mohamed Lamine Conté, alias Kalala, chef de quartier de Coronthie 2 et initiateur de la démarche auprès du président de la République, évoque une satisfaction qui dépasse le cadre personnel. «Nous sommes à la 68e année de notre indépendance. Imaginez-vous, le quartier le plus peuplé de Kaloum, c’est Coronthie. Nous n’avions pas d’école et nos enfants étaient victimes d’accidents. Je suis tellement dépassé par cette réalisation. C’est quelque chose dont toute la communauté avait besoin depuis des années et des années», confie-t-il. Il explique que, malgré ses difficultés personnelles, la construction d’un établissement primaire dans son quartier constituait sa principale préoccupation lors de sa rencontre avec le chef de l’État:«Ma femme est malade, je ne travaille pas et j’ai des enfants, mais ma priorité, c’était la construction d’une école lorsque j’étais face au président. Ce jour-là, tout ce que je demandais au président, il allait me le faire. Il m’a dit : “Ça là, je vais réaliser” », rapporte-t-il. Pour Mohamed Lamine Conté, cette réalisation marque désormais le début d’une nouvelle étape, celle de la gestion de l’établissement par les structures compétentes du système éducatif. À Boulbinet 2, l’établissement scolaire « Frederiko Mayer » a également bénéficié d’importants travaux. Ancienne principale du collège, aujourd’hui chef de section pédagogique à la Direction communale de l’éducation de Kaloum, Sy Edith Camara revient sur les conditions difficiles dans lesquelles évoluait l’établissement avant sa délocalisation:«Il y a deux ans, nous étions au collège de Boulbinet, de l’autre côté, à côté de la prématernelle. Nous vivions difficilement. C’était une école qui avait vraiment besoin de rénovation », se souvient-elle. Selon son témoignage, le projet a pris forme à la suite du passage de Mamadou Cissé, directeur général de l’ARSJPA, dans l’établissement. Celui-ci lui aurait demandé de préparer un mémorandum à adresser au président de la République: «Monsieur Cissé a fait un passage par là-bas et, deux jours après, il m’a appelée. Il m’a dit : “Madame, faites un mémo que vous allez adresser au président de la République.” Chose qui a été faite. Heureusement, cinq mois après, au mois d’août 2024, j’ai été appelée par la présidence et cette école a commencé à être rénovée », explique-t-elle. L’établissement, qui compte 12 salles de classe, a notamment bénéficié de travaux de rénovation des bâtiments et des toilettes. Une transformation qui a considérablement amélioré les conditions de travail des enseignants et d’apprentissage des élèves. «C’est une action à double avantage. Les enseignants sont à l’aise, l’environnement de l’enseignement est vraiment assuré et les enfants sont également à l’aise. Avant, il y avait un problème d’eau et de latrines. Si ce n’était pas le patriotisme et l’amour de notre travail, qui est l’enseignement, nous n’aurions pas pu tenir dans ces conditions », souligne l’ancienne responsable. Face au résultat, elle se dit particulièrement satisfaite: «Quand j’ai revu ce bijou, j’étais sans voix. C’est une action qui nous réjouit énormément. Nous ne finirons jamais de remercier le président Mamadi Doumbouya, surtout avec sa vision Simandou Academy. Nous osons dire que nous allons former ici des enfants qui mettront en lumière le projet Simandou 2040 », ajoute-t-elle. Dans la commune de Matam, le lycée-collège de Coléah figure également parmi les établissements concernés par ces travaux. L’école a bénéficié d’une réhabilitation importante, touchant notamment ses bâtiments, ses salles de classe et ses installations sanitaires. Blaise Soumah, censeur de l’établissement, rappelle que l’un des bâtiments, construit le 13 mars 1962, n’avait jamais connu de rénovation majeure. Le second, dont les travaux étaient restés inachevés depuis 2001, a quant à lui fait l’objet d’une reconstruction complète en 2025. «Le premier bâtiment, qui a été construit le 13 mars 1962, n’a jamais connu de grandes rénovations. C’est la première fois, grâce à l’initiative du chef de l’État. Quant au second bâtiment, depuis 2001, l’école était restée avec seulement les murs et le soubassement. C’est seulement en 2025 que cette école a été complètement construite », précise-t-il. Les travaux ont notamment permis de carreler et d’électrifier les salles de classe, de climatiser les bureaux et d’augmenter le nombre de toilettes. La cour de l’établissement a également été aménagée avec un terrain de football, qui contribue à dynamiser la vie scolaire. « Aujourd’hui, toutes les salles de classe sont carrelées et électrifiées. Les bureaux sont climatisés et le nombre de toilettes a été augmenté. Avant, quand on venait ici, c’était de la poussière. Maintenant, l’école est rénovée et on peut venir sans être sali par la poussière. Il y a aussi un terrain de football qui permet à nos enfants de pratiquer l’EPS et aux jeunes professeurs de venir jouer », détaille le censeur. Sur le plan des capacités d’accueil, l’établissement dispose de 18 salles de classe fonctionnelles, réparties entre les deux bâtiments. Il accueille actuellement 888 élèves, malgré un effectif prévisionnel initial de 1 020 élèves. «Nous avons 15 groupes pédagogiques, dont quatre au collège et onze au lycée. Nous avions un effectif prévisionnel de 1 020 élèves, mais, compte tenu des réalités, nous avons retenu 888 élèves. Nous sommes parfois obligés de limiter les admissions parce que nous voulons que les cours se déroulent dans de bonnes conditions », explique Blaise Soumah. En marge de ces réalisations, une vaste opération de distribution du manuel scolaire Le Rêve de Mahmoud a été organisée au profit des écoles élémentaires publiques. Au total, 48 200 ouvrages ont été distribués, dont 16 000 répartis entre les cinq communes de Conakry : Kaloum, Matam, Dixinn, Ratoma et Matoto. À l’intérieur du pays, 32 200 exemplaires ont également été distribués dans neuf localités, notamment Coyah, Fria, Boké, Dubréka, Kindia, Boffa, Kankan, Mamou et Siguiri. Cet ouvrage raconte l’histoire d’un jeune garçon vivant dans la zone côtière de la Guinée. À travers cette initiative, les promoteurs entendent contribuer à renforcer l’accès des élèves aux supports pédagogiques et à encourager la lecture dès le cycle primaire. Entre construction d’une nouvelle école, réhabilitation d’établissements existants et distribution de manuels scolaires, ces différentes initiatives visent à améliorer l’environnement éducatif et les conditions d’apprentissage des élèves, aussi bien à Conakry qu’à l’intérieur du pays. items.title: US midterms: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
items.description: Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Wednesday, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency. The Democratic landslide will give the opposition power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times : “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats”. “I think the Democrats did a good job, I really do,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” But he sought to distance himself from his own party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the defeat but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration, long one of the most divisive issues of his presidency. But minutes later on social media the 80-year-old signalled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton speaks following her victory in the US midterm elections at a Democratic Election Night rally, in Columbus, Ohio, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Talarico said that “we defeated Goliath” after winning a US Senate seat over Texas attorney General Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who was heavily backed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. “In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world, and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico told a victory rally in the Texas capital, Austin. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In California, Democrat Xavier Becerra handily defeated Donald Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton in the race to become the governor, US networks said. Partial results showed Becerra, a career politician who served in the cabinet of former president Joe Biden, had a nearly two-to-one advantage over Hilton, with about half of the ballots counted. Becerra had run a low-key campaign in a state where Democrats heavily outnumber Republicans and where the Trump brand is almost toxic. The son of Mexican immigrants, he will be the first elected Latino governor of California, a state that would be the world’s fourth-largest economy if it were a country. “Ladies and gentlemen, you have now entered the Becerra era,” the former US Health and Human Services secretary told his supporters at a victory party in Sacramento. “I didn’t run to make history,” he said. “I ran to make a difference for anyone and everyone who calls California home, whether you voted for me or not.” Becerra will replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democratic Party big-hitter who is believed to have his eyes on a tilt at the White House in 2028. California Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra speaks at an election night event on November 3, 2026 in Sacramento, California. —AFP Hilton, a British-born conservative former pundit who was once an adviser to former UK prime minister David Cameron, had always been a long shot. He conceded he had lost a difficult race. “Maybe this isn’t the best year to be running for office as a Republican when we see what’s going on around the country,” he said. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Republican heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. Analysts had identified an upset there as a warning of a much wider Democratic advance. Supporters react to early election results in favor of US Senator Jon Ossoff at an election night watch party hosted by the Democratic Party of Georgia after the midterms election in Atlanta, Georgia on November 3, 2026. — AFP In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in US history, while other Democratic gains extended to statehouses across the country. Republicans had some bright spots in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds won the governorship, becoming the state’s first Black governor, and Ashley Moody kept a Senate seat. George Washington University professor Todd Belt called the Democratic advance “a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies,” citing voters’ concerns about the economy, corruption and the Iran conflict. Trump on defensive Democrats will now be able to block Trump’s legislation, investigate his administration over corruption allegations, the Iran war and immigration enforcement, and use Senate control to thwart judicial appointments and senior nominations. Robert Garcia, a Democrat expected to lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, warned Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run from sea to shining sea.” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) speaks during a press conference with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) at the AC Hotel Washington DC Capitol Hill Navy Yard on November 03, 2026 in Washington, DC. Jeffries is also positioned to become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January, if elected by his colleagues. As speaker, Jeffries, representing a New York City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans who controlled the House for the past four years. “Today begins the great American comeback,” Jeffries proclaimed in a victory speech late on Tuesday after media outlets projected the likelihood of Democratic majorities in the House and Senate. For many voters, the central concern was Trump’s stewardship of the economy. “Rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes keep climbing,” 24-year-old Los Angeles voter Taylor Cook told AFP. A rebuke to Trump, winner says “In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the man named President Donald J. Trump,” incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, the projected winner in Georgia, told supporters at a victory party. In Florida, Republican Senator Ashley Moody fended off Democrat Angie Nixon but was ahead by only about three percentage points in a state Trump carried by 13 points in 2024, according to a vote count compiled by Reuters and USA Today , further evidence that even solidly Republican states were shifting dramatically toward Democrats. Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections. Cait Conley, Democratic candidate for the US House of Representatives in New York’s 17th Congressional District, reacts following her victory in the US midterm elections, in Pleasantville, New York, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, on Tuesday was elected governor of the state of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman elected to that office in the US, media projections showed. CNN and NBC News called the race in her favour. Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson, who ran as a Republican. Current Governor Brian Kemp is term-limited and could not run again. Midterm elections are typically viewed as a referendum on the president, and that is especially true for Trump, who dominates attention like no other politician. Trump himself told his supporters to “pretend I’m on the ballot” and held dozens of rallies in the closing weeks. According to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets, including major television networks and the Associated Press , half of voters nationwide said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are “angry” or “dissatisfied” with the way the country is headed. In addition, 70 per cent of voters surveyed said they want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the president. History is against Republicans: the sitting president’s party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterms since World War Two. Trump’s approval rating is hovering near his career lows, with voters frustrated by war on Iran , higher fuel prices and wider affordability concerns. Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist, labels Democrats flatly reject. Opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability and disapprove of Trump’s handling of the issue. His tariffs on imports, many of which the courts threw out, and his decision to attack Iran in February raised prices for consumers. Trump deploys election monitors The US Justice Department said it had deployed 1,000 election monitors and observers to all 50 states in what it called the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history. Democrats criticised the plan as potential voter intimidation. In roughly two-thirds of the jurisdictions the department listed, voters supported Democrat Kamala Harris over Trump in the 2024 presidential election, a Reuters analysis found. Election officials in several states reported no issues with the monitoring effort. New Mexico’s secretary of state’s office said it had received reports of federal monitors asking “unusual questions” in one county and that the Justice Department offered assurances that the conduct would be addressed.

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude : Plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies en deux semaines par la CNLF
items.description: Du gasoil vendu en violation de la réglementation au cyanure dissimulé dans une cargaison de clinker, en passant par les sachets plastiques interdits et le riz importé frauduleusement, les services de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte Contre la Fraude (CNLF) multiplient les opérations de contrôle sur le territoire national. Entre le 17 et le 30 octobre 2026, leurs interventions ont permis de saisir des marchandises d'une valeur estimée à plus de 95 millions de F CFA. Un bilan présenté le mardi 3 novembre 2026 à Diébougou. Sur les routes, dans les magasins de stockage et aux différents points de contrôle, la lutte contre la fraude prend plusieurs formes. Derrière les marchandises qui circulent se cachent parfois des pratiques commerciales illicites, des produits interdits ou des importations qui échappent aux règles établies. C'est contre ces pratiques que les équipes de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) sont mobilisées. Entre le 17 et le 30 octobre 2026, cette mission de contrôle a donné lieu à plusieurs interventions dans différentes localités du Burkina Faso. À Ouagadougou, les premières opérations remontent au 17 octobre. Ce jour-là, les agents interceptent une citerne transportant 14 000 litres de gasoil. En cause, une pratique illicite de prix. Cette saisie illustre la vigilance des services de contrôle face aux irrégularités qui affectent le marché des hydrocarbures. Trois jours plus tard, le 20 octobre, une autre découverte vient illustrer la diversité des produits concernés par ce combat. Dans une cargaison de clinker, les agents mettent au jour 20 sacs de cyanure de 50 kg chacun. Au total, une tonne de cette substance est ainsi interceptée. Dissimulé dans un chargement de matériaux, ce produit chimique constitue un enjeu particulier de contrôle, au regard des risques que peuvent représenter les substances dangereuses lorsqu'elles échappent aux circuits réglementaires. De l'axe Dakola à Bobo-Dioulasso, la vigilance se poursuit Le 28 octobre, toujours à Ouagadougou, les équipes poursuivent leurs investigations. Dans un magasin, elles découvrent des sachets plastiques interdits ainsi que de l'huile de lubrification contrefaite. Une intervention qui rappelle que la lutte contre la fraude ne concerne pas uniquement les marchandises circulant sur les grands axes routiers. Elle s'étend également aux espaces de stockage et aux circuits de distribution. La surveillance ne se limite pas à la capitale. Sur l'axe Dakola, les services de la CNLF interceptent des boissons de marque ICE dont l'importation est interdite. Cette opération traduit l'importance des contrôles sur les voies de circulation des marchandises, notamment pour empêcher l'introduction de produits soumis à des restrictions. À Bobo-Dioulasso, la Brigade d'enquête et de recherche de l'Ouest réalise une autre saisie d'envergure. Elle met la main sur un stock de 55 tonnes de riz importé en dépit des mesures d'interdiction d'importation de cette denrée. Par cette intervention, les agents s'attaquent à une pratique susceptible de fragiliser les mesures nationales de régulation du marché et de protection de la production locale. Du carburant au riz, en passant par les produits chimiques et les emballages plastiques, ces différentes opérations révèlent l'étendue du front sur lequel les services de contrôle sont engagés. Chaque saisie répond à une problématique particulière qu’est le respect des règles de fixation des prix, le contrôle des substances dangereuses, la protection de l'environnement et l’application des mesures encadrant les importations. La lutte contre la fraude vise à préserver la sécurité et la santé des consommateurs Au terme de cette séquence d'opérations, le bilan financier dépasse les 95 millions de F CFA. Pour le coordonnateur national de lutte contre la fraude, le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, ces résultats sont le fruit de l'engagement et de la vigilance des agents déployés sur le terrain. « Nous tenons à les féliciter pour leur professionnalisme et pour leur savoir-faire, pour leur vigilance accrue en matière de lutte contre la fraude », a-t-il déclaré, saluant le travail accompli par les différentes équipes. Mais derrière les chiffres et les quantités saisies, le responsable met surtout en avant un enjeu de protection des populations. La lutte contre la fraude vise, selon lui, à préserver la sécurité et la santé des consommateurs, en empêchant notamment la circulation de produits dont l'importation, la commercialisation ou l'utilisation ne respectent pas les dispositions en vigueur. Le combat comporte également une dimension économique. En veillant à l'application de la réglementation commerciale, la CNLF entend contribuer à assainir les circuits d'approvisionnement et à préserver les intérêts de l'économie nationale. Pour le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, la lutte contre la fraude ne saurait reposer uniquement sur les agents de contrôle. Elle nécessite aussi l'adhésion des commerçants, des importateurs et de l'ensemble des acteurs économiques. Il les invite ainsi à accompagner les orientations des autorités burkinabè dans le contexte de la Révolution progressiste populaire. « Nous allons toujours accentuer la vigilance pour les amener de force à abandonner ces pratiques frauduleuses », Dr Mohamadi Compaoré « Nous sommes dans une phase de Révolution Progressiste Populaire. Tout le monde doit s'aligner, tout le monde doit accompagner le gouvernement pour que nous puissions sortir notre pays du sous-développement », a-t-il insisté. Le coordonnateur national prévient que les contrôles vont se poursuivre et s'intensifier. Face aux acteurs qui persistent dans les pratiques frauduleuses, la CNLF entend maintenir la pression. « Nous allons toujours accentuer la vigilance pour les amener de force à abandonner ces pratiques frauduleuses », a-t-il averti. Des axes routiers aux lieux de stockage, en passant par les circuits d'importation, le combat se joue sur plusieurs fronts. Avec ces marchandises interceptées en quatorze jours, la CNLF affiche sa détermination à faire respecter la réglementation et à défendre les intérêts des consommateurs et de l'économie burkinabè. Basile SAMA Faso7 L’article Lutte contre la fraude : Plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies en deux semaines par la CNLF est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: ECP objects to retired SC judge's remarks about 2023 ruling on polls in Punjab and KP, reserved seats case
items.description: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday objected to remarks made by former senior puisne judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Mansoor Ali Shah, regarding polls in KP and Punjab and the reserved seats case pertaining to the PTI. Shah made the remarks at an event organised by the US-based Community Alliance for Peace and Justice on October 29, where he was asked about his dissenting opinion in the 2023 SC ruling on provincial elections in Punjab and KP and whether it was a “turning point” and the beginning of a “division” within the SC. In its 3-2 verdict, the SC, after taking a suo motu notice, directed that elections should be held within 90 days in both provinces. Two judges, including Shah, had dissented from the ruling, saying that the suo motu proceedings initiated by then-chief justice of Pakistan Umar Ata Bandial, were “wholly unjustified”, besides being initiated with “undue haste”. In their detailed reasoning , they explained that the SC by a majority of 4-3 and not 3-2 had dismissed the suo motu hearing on polls delay in Punjab and KP and therefore the same should be considered as the “Order of the Court”. It had resulted in a controversy, with the government igniting a raging debate claiming that the ruling was a 4-3 majority decision in its favour and not a 3-2 verdict against. In response to the question, Shah said that this was the time when the ex-chief justice was forming “like-minded benches”, adding that three or four judges were attending to the majority of the cases. He said that initially the matter was taken by the high courts. He said that the SC judges had gathered in the ante-room and discussed with the chief justice at the time that suo motu notice should not be taken at this point. He said that it was “agreed” to wait but days later a SC bench took up the matter under suo motu powers as he denounced the “one-man show” going on at the time. He said that at the time, two SC judges — Justice Yahya Afridi and Justice Athar Minallah — had dismissed the petitions in the case. He said that the SC bench was later reconstituted, adding that since two judges had decided the matter, the verdict could not be dismissed. He said that this sparked the 4-3, 2-3 debate. Shah also defended the 2024 verdict in the reserved seats case , wherein PTI was declared eligible for seats reserved for women and minorities, in a setback to the ruling coalition. “We said that the PTI was a political party and it was wrong to deprive [them of their symbol] … and illegal,” he said, recalling that this was a decision “that nobody liked”. In a statement on Wednesday, the ECP referred to the remarks made by Shah, saying that they ignored “basic constitutional and legal facts related to the election matters and judicial decisions”. “It is highly inappropriate to present the judicial record for specific purposes through selective quotations, incomplete perspectives and one-sided interpretations,” the statement said. The electoral watchdog said that Shah had claimed that the SC’s majority decision about the elections in 2023 was a 4-3 verdict and that the suo motu notice and relevant petitions were dismissed. The ECP also stated that according to Shah’s claims, the election ruling was a “minority decision” and the commission could not have held polls. Regarding the PTI case, it said that Shah had declared the order for withdrawal of the party’s electoral symbol during the 2024 elections as “illegal”. The commission said that the election symbol was subject to transparent intra-party elections as per Sections 208 and 209 of the Election Act 2017. It added that “till date, PTI has not been able to fulfil the requirement”. The ECP said PTI was supposed to hold intra-party elections by June 30, 2021, and the commission had given the party three chances; however, the party failed to hold intra-party elections. As a result, the commission said that the party’s election symbol was withdrawn, which, the ECP added, was also upheld by the SC in 2025, along with rejecting review petitions filed by the PTI. The ECP further stated that PTI held intra-party elections after five years and its proceedings remained pending before the commission as the “PTI itself has taken a stay order from a high court”. It further stated that as per the commission’s records, the PTI was still enlisted as a political party. The ECP added that only political parties which contested the elections had a right to the reserved seats. “These political parties are required to submit a preferred list of candidates before the elections, while PTI has not submitted any preferred list,” it stated. It further stated that it was mandatory for a political party to win at least one seat and that independent members were not entitled to reserved seats and therefore, the ECP gave the seats to the eligible parties. It said that if the PTI was entitled to the reserved seats, then “Articles 51 and 106 of the Constitution and Section 104 of the Elections Act 2917 become ineffective”. The ECP said that it was “unfortunate” that a retired judge was taking a position against the Constitution and the law. In November 2025, Shah had resigned as an SC judge alongside Minallah, hours after the 27th Constitutional Amendment — which made significant changes to the country’s judicial system and established the Federal Constitutional Court — was signed into law by President Asif Ali Zardari. “By fracturing the unity of the nation’s apex court, it has crippled judicial independence and integrity, pushing the country back by decades,” he wrote in the letter sent to the president. “Staying on would not only amount to silent acquiescence in a constitutional wrong, but would also mean continuing to sit in a court whose constitutional voice has been muted,” he said.

items.title: Drone attacks kill civilians and cripple Sudan’s power infrastructure, UN warns of growing humanitarian toll
items.description: Drone attacks across Sudan have killed at least 14 civilians and injured several others, while strikes on electricity infrastructure have triggered widespread power cuts and disrupted clean water supplies, prompting warnings from the United Nations and the Arab League. The latest attacks killed eight people in Um Dibo, in El Sunut locality, West Kordofan, on Monday evening. Residents told Radio Dabanga that a drone strike also wounded three people. On Tuesday, at least four people were killed and more than 10 injured when a drone struck a fuel station in the middle of the market in El Abbasiya Tagali, South Kordofan. Witnesses told Radio Dabanga that the injured were taken to the town’s hospital. The strike also damaged the station and several vehicles. Other sources reported that the same drone hit facilities in nearby Rashad, although the targets and extent of the damage remained unclear. In Ed Damazin, the capital of Blue Nile region, drone attacks on several neighbourhoods killed a woman and a young man and wounded others on Tuesday evening, according to local sources. The strikes hit El Zahour, the Sudanese Armed Forces barracks area and El Ziraa El Aliya neighbourhoods, damaging a home. The Blue Nile Civil Society Initiative identified the woman as Ilham Ali Shikan, a mother of three, and said another woman, Amal Bashir, was wounded. The initiative blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and its ally, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, for the attack and called for an end to strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure . Blue Nile governor Ahmed El Omda also condemned the attacks, describing them as an assault on civilians and civilian property. ‘UN warns of growing humanitarian toll’ The latest incidents come amid a wider campaign of drone strikes against electricity and fuel infrastructure across Sudan. The Arab League condemned repeated attacks it attributed to the RSF on energy facilities in Khartoum, El Gezira, Sennar, El Gedaref, River Nile and Red Sea states. The organisation said the strikes had severely damaged power facilities, knocked several out of service and cut electricity to large areas, worsening conditions for civilians . It warned that deliberately targeting power stations and other civilian infrastructure that does not constitute a military objective violates international humanitarian law and could amount to a war crime. The United Nations also warned that continued drone attacks on critical energy infrastructure were disrupting essential services. UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday that the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) was deeply concerned about the attacks and their impact on people across several states. According to reports cited by the UN, drones targeted two power stations in Kassala state and a substation in Merowe on Tuesday. Earlier attacks hit electricity facilities in River Nile state on Monday, a substation in Red Sea state on Saturday, and sites in North Kordofan and El Gezira. UN humanitarian partners warned that power cuts and fuel shortages had disrupted clean water supplies, forcing residents to rely on untreated sources and increasing the risk of waterborne diseases . Dujarric said the secretary-general strongly condemned the escalating drone attacks by parties to the conflict. In a statement issued two days earlier, the secretary-general said drone strikes had killed hundreds of civilians, including women and children, across Sudan and the Abyei a r ea , in what he described as a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law. He also condemned attacks on civilians and the critical infrastructure they depend on, including healthcare facilities, and urged the warring parties to agree to an immediate cessation of hostilities and engage in mediation efforts led by his personal envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto. The Arab League reiterated its support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity. Its secretary-general also appointed Zaid Al-Sabban as his personal envoy for Sudan. Share article The post Drone attacks kill civilians and cripple Sudan’s power infrastructure, UN warns of growing humanitarian toll appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Kurt Okraku questions taxes on importation of national team equipments, gate proceeds
items.description: Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku has asked the governement to consider granting tax exemptions on items imported for the service of the country’s national teams. Speaking before the Parliamentary Select Committee on Youth, Sports and Culture, Okraku said the taxes on equipments imported for national teams have become a burden to the administration. “Sometimes, the GFA is handicapped (and unable to pay for the cost of clearing its equipment). We dont have the finances.” The GFA President also criticised the Value Added Tax (VAT) rate of 17.5% that is charged on football tickets, questioning why other sectors of the economy like the entertainment industry, are not always required to pay similar rates for patronage of events. “We are charged 17.5 VAT at the gate on every game that we play. And yet, other entertainment providers are charged less. This is a problem that I’ve brought to the fore of leadership, not on one occasion, not twice, maybe more,” he said. Currently, government requires majority of state agencies, including private entities conducting business on behalf of the state, to comply with its tax laws. In the case of the Ghana Football Association, importation of items supplied by its technical partners such as PUMA all attract tax rates. These include match day jerseys, training jerseys, boots, training equipments, branding materials etc.

items.title: Cour d’appel de Conakry : le verdict dans l’affaire Sékou Keïta contre le ministère public renvoyé
items.description: Initialement attendu ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, le verdict dans l’affaire opposant Sékou Keïta, conseiller en communication et porte-parole du ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, au ministère public, devant la Cour d’appel de Conakry, ne sera finalement pas rendu ce jour. Selon les informations recueillies, le report de cette audience, ainsi que celui des autres audiences inscrites au rôle de la juridiction pour la journée, serait consécutif au décès d’un agent de l’administration pénitentiaire. Pour rappel, lors de la dernière audience, tenue le 21 octobre dernier à la Cour d’appel de Conakry, le ministère public avait, dans ses réquisitions, sollicité la condamnation de Sékou Keïta à la durée de sa détention déjà effectuée. Rappelons que Sékou Keïta, expert en communication, ancien porte-parole du ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme et ancien responsable de la communication et des relations extérieures chez Orange Guinée, avait été condamné par le tribunal de première instance de Dixinn à un an d’emprisonnement ferme et au paiement d’une amende de deux millions de francs guinéens pour complicité de tentative de fraude à un concours. items.title: Au moins 15 pays européens ont été touchés par les cyberattaques visant les réfrigérateurs de supermarchés
items.description: Selon une analyse de la revue, au moins 15 pays européens ont été touchés par des cyberattaques visant les systèmes de réfrigération de supermarchés et d’entreprises alimentaires depuis le 11 octobre. Celles-ci ont d’abord concerné des supermarchés français, provoquant au moins plusieurs dizaines de millions d’euros de pertes, puis se sont étendues à d’autres pays début novembre. Des centaines de supermarchés français ont été touchés dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre, puis d’autres, équipés de contrôleurs Dixell permettant de piloter à distance la température des meubles frigorifiques et des chambres froides, dans la nuit du 12 au 13. Une seconde vague d’attaques a eu lieu dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre, touchant 14 pays, dont l’Allemagne, où des magasins Rewe et Edeka ont été visés, et l’Italie, où une vingtaine de magasins ont été touchés en Sicile, ainsi qu’une entreprise de restauration en Toscane. L’ampleur de ces attaques varie considérablement d’un pays à l’autre. La France se distingue des autres pays européens touchés : environ 700 supermarchés ont été visés, selon le gouvernement. Mis à part en Belgique, en Suède, en Italie, aux Pays-Bas et en Irlande, le nombre de magasins et d’entreprises visés dans les autres pays ne dépasse pas une dizaine. En Grèce et en Norvège, trois commerces ont affirmé avoir été touchés, bien que leurs cas n’aient pas été confirmés par les autorités. La piste d’une opération russe ou menée par des acteurs gravitant autour des services de renseignement de Moscou n’est pas à exclure. Selon l’entreprise américaine de cybersécurité Forescout, la plupart des quelque vingt attaques revendiquées depuis le début de l’année contre des systèmes de réfrigération l’ont été par des groupes d’hacktivistes prorusses Supermarkets Across Europe Report New Suspected Freezer Hack », Bloomberg , 2 novembre 2026.'> 1 . Xavier Bellekens, PDG de la firme de cybersécurité écossaise Lupovis, se dit quant à lui « fermement convaincu que cette activité pourrait être attribuée à un acteur malveillant soutenu par l’État russe » Supermarket Chain Thaw Massacre : Russia suspected in Europe’s fridge attacks », Politico , 3 novembre 2026.'> 2 . Selon Lupovis, des leurres (aussi appelés « honeypots ») mis en place par l’entreprise ont été ciblés par des attaquants dont les serveurs avaient déjà été utilisés par le passé par des groupes russes. Cette série d'attaques est d'autant plus troublante qu'aucune rançon n'a été demandée et qu'elle pourrait servir à envoyer un message aux gouvernements européens. Lundi 2 novembre, ce sont des chambres froides de l’Établissement français du sang (EFS) qui ont été touchées par une attaque visant leur prestataire frigorifique, leurs seuils de température ayant été « portés à de très hautes températures ». L’EFS assure que cette attaque n’a eu aucun impact sanitaire Une cyberattaque touche des installations frigorifiques utilisées par l'Etablissement français du sang, « sans impact » sur les échantillons conservés », FranceInfo , 4 novembre 2026.'> 3 . Les progrès de l’intelligence artificielle facilitent considérablement les opérations de cybercriminalité, et fournissent aux auteurs de nouvelles capacités pour mener des attaques à grande échelle en un temps réduit. CrowdStrike, dans un rapport publié en février, estime que le nombre d’attaques menées par des acteurs malveillants utilisant l’IA a presque doublé entre 2024 et 2025, augmentant de 89 %. L’article Au moins 15 pays européens ont été touchés par les cyberattaques visant les réfrigérateurs de supermarchés est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement
items.description: Lawmakers divided over proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to regulate rental payments and curb exploitative practices by landlords and estate agents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), amid disagreements among lawmakers over a proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments. The bill, sponsored by Rep. Paul Sunday Nnamchi, seeks to regulate advance rent payments, arbitrary rent increases and agency fees, as well as establish a unified digital register for housing agents. It also provides safeguards for landlords and tenants, with penalties for violations of its provisions. Leading the debate, Nnamchi said the rising cost of accommodation and excessive demands for advance rent had placed enormous financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, small businesses and employment mobility. He said the proposed legislation was designed to establish a fairer and more accountable rental system through the regulation of advance payments, reasonable limits on agency fees and proper identification of housing agents. “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns. “Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation,” he said. Supporting the bill, Rep. Idris Zacharias, representing Ida/Igalamela/Ibaji/Ofu Federal Constituency of Kogi State, described the proposal as important but called for broader consideration of land administration and housing challenges in the FCT. He also urged the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to be included in the committee that would consider the bill. Similarly, Rep. Chinedu Ogah, representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency of Ebonyi State, backed the proposal, citing the difficulties businesses face in securing office accommodation in Abuja. Ogah said renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between N25 million and N30 million annually, excluding additional agency charges. He argued that regulating the rental market would provide clearer rules for transactions and encourage investment in the sector. However, Rep. Leko Jafaru Gambo, representing Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for a review of the bill’s title, arguing that the word “prohibit” should be replaced with “regulate”. He also suggested that the legislation should have nationwide application, but Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu clarified that its current scope was limited to the FCT. Rep. Ibe Okwara Osonwa, representing Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, also supported regulation but cautioned against an outright prohibition of multi-year rent arrangements. He disputed claims that agency fees could reach 25 per cent, arguing that they were generally around 10 per cent. On his part, Rep. Ayodeji Alao-Akala, representing Ogbomoso North/South/Orire Federal Constituency of Oyo State, said the bill targeted compulsory multi-year payments rather than preventing landlords from increasing rents. He argued that requiring young couples and other prospective tenants to pay two years’ rent upfront imposed an unreasonable financial burden. “As a youth, when a young couple comes out of service now, and is being asked to pay two years, where will this insurance money come from?” he asked. Alao-Akala said the proposed legislation could provide for monthly, six-monthly or annual rental arrangements while preventing landlords from compelling tenants to pay several years’ rent upfront. However, Rep. Patrick Umoh raised constitutional concerns, particularly over property rights and freedom of trade, urging the House to step down the bill for further consultations and a review of existing tenancy laws in the FCT. Kalu also acknowledged concerns about possible inconsistencies with constitutional provisions, while lawmakers drew attention to Section 44(2)(c) of the Constitution, which addresses laws relating to leases and tenancies. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Wale Raji, representing Epe Federal Constituency of Lagos State, said previous attempts to regulate rents had not sufficiently addressed the problem. He argued that the widening gap between housing demand and supply remained a major driver of rising rental costs. “The bill is not anti-investment. The bill is not against even the landlords or those making investment in the real estate environment or industry. This bill is of good use to both the landlords and the tenants,” he said. The Minority Leader, Rep. Frederick Agbedi, also urged lawmakers to support the proposal, saying the high cost of rent in the FCT was forcing residents into overcrowded and unsuitable accommodation in satellite communities and suburban areas. He said the bill was intended to address excesses in the rental market without discouraging investment in the property sector. The House Leader, Rep. Julius Ihonvbere, described the legislation as important, citing the difficulties Nigerians face in securing accommodation and the activities of unregistered estate agents. “I think this is a very important bill. And I want to thank Professor Nnamchi for thinking about it,” he said. Ihonvbere said the bill would proceed to a public hearing, where Nigerians, professionals and other stakeholders would have the opportunity to make contributions. He urged lawmakers to support the measure, stressing that regulating the sector should not be interpreted as an attempt to discourage property development. “We are in a stage where we have a duty to protect Nigerians. It’s not against you to build your house. You can build as many houses as you want,” he said. In his closing remarks, Kalu cited Section 16 of the Constitution, which provides for the promotion of citizens’ welfare and suitable and adequate shelter. He argued that although Nigeria operates a mixed economy, sectors connected to essential human needs, including housing, require regulation and control. “Not all sectors of the economy should be free and capitalist. Especially when it has to do with shelter, which is fundamental. So, some sectors should be regulated as well as controlled,” he said. The bill was subsequently passed for second reading, paving the way for further legislative consideration and a public hearing to enable stakeholders to make submissions. The post Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement appeared first on Vanguard News .
