items.title: 2027: No coalition needed in Ondo, APC elders declare
items.description: Target one million votes for Tinubu, 80% turnout By Dayo Johnson, Akure The PBAT Mandate Elders Forum (PMF), Ondo State chapter, has declared that there is no need for a coalition arrangement in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the All Progressives Congress (APC) is strong enough to win all elective positions. The Forum also set a target of at least one million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, alongside an 80 per cent voter turnout in the state. The position was made known at a meeting of the Forum in Akure, the state capital, where its chairman, Hon. Demola Ijabiyi, said the APC’s dominance in the state made any arrangement requiring it to surrender candidates or constituencies unnecessary. Ijabiyi said the Forum recognised the importance of cooperation among political parties with shared political objectives but maintained that such arrangements must reflect the political realities of individual states. “In Ondo State, the APC is the dominant political party, controlling government at both the state and local government levels,” he said. He said the Forum welcomed support from other political parties for Tinubu’s re-election but would not accept any arrangement that required APC candidates to step down. “Support for the President need not depend on displacing APC candidates. We have confidence in our candidates and their prospects of victory,” he said. According to him, coalition arrangements are more appropriate in states where political parties have limited electoral strength and need to combine forces to overcome their weaknesses. He explained that parties could support stronger candidates in constituencies where they lacked sufficient electoral strength in exchange for reciprocal support elsewhere. “But we don’t have that kind of circumstance in Ondo State. There is no constituency that we cannot win. There is no constituency that we do not want to contest. We are going to win all. That is the bottom line,” he said. The Forum chairman also cited the declining political strength of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which he described as the major opposition party in the state in the past, as another reason the APC should not surrender its electoral interests. On mobilisation, Ijabiyi said the Forum was working towards extending its structures to every ward and polling unit to mobilise voters and secure victory for Tinubu and all APC candidates. He said Ondo State’s more than two million registered voters ahead of the 2027 governorship election presented a significant electoral opportunity, adding that the challenge was to translate the figure into actual voter participation. “We have therefore set a voter turnout target of at least 80 per cent. The PMF will work towards this through sustained mobilisation and voter education. Alongside this, we must earn sufficient support to deliver at least one million votes for the President,” he said. Ijabiyi directed the Forum’s chapters to develop practical grassroots mobilisation plans, assign responsibilities and provide regular reports on their activities. He said meetings and political endorsements must translate into measurable engagement with voters in communities across the state. The chairman also urged APC National and State Assembly candidates to intensify their campaigns, identify areas of weak mobilisation and work with local party leaders to strengthen support at the polling-unit level. He said candidates should engage voters directly, explain their legislative priorities and demonstrate how their election would advance the interests of their constituencies. Ijabiyi further urged the candidates to promote Tinubu’s re-election and support the campaigns of other APC candidates, stressing that victory would depend on effective coordination among party structures and support groups. The Forum reaffirmed its commitment to Tinubu’s re-election and the victory of all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. It also pledged to collaborate with the party leadership, candidates, the Campaign Council and other support groups to mobilise support for the President ahead of his planned reception in the state on November 11. items.title: 37e Tour du Faso/6e étape : Le triplé pour Yacine Hamza
items.description: Le premier à l’arrivée de la 6e étape courue ce mercredi 4 novembre entre Saponé et Léo (140,49 km) a été l’Algérien Yacine Hamza qui signe sa troisième victoire d’étape sur le 37e Tour du Faso. Il a bouclé la distance en 3h09’56’’. Le Sud-africain Gustav Basson conserve le maillot jaune. Et de trois pour Yacine Hamza. Le sprinter algérien a fait parler une fois de plus sa puissance à l’arrivée de la 6e étape ce 4 novembre à Léo. Il a « déposé » sur la ligne finale le Néerlandais Cas Hermans (2e) et l’Algérien Mohamed Nadib Assal au bout d’un alléchant sprint groupé à 44, 380 km/h. Partis à 8h 37 avec trois coureurs de moins que la veille, ils étaient 70 en lice pour ce sixième jour de compétition. Le peloton est resté calme jusqu’au premier point chaud de la journée, jugé à Rakaye au km 34,22. Un sprint intermédiaire remporté par Tiémoko Diamouténé du Mali devant Marouan Kharbouchi du Maroc et Wogué Ivan Njonkoué du Cameroun. C’est seulement après 48 km parcourus que les Burkinabè Paul Daumont et Barthélémy Yaméogo ainsi que le Néerlandais Jannes Van Weele donnent la première véritable animation à la course. Elle restera le seul fait majeur avant l’explication finale. En effet, les trois hommes vont réussir à creuser un écart avec le peloton qui a prospéré jusqu’à 2’30’’ à l’entrée de Sapouy. Ils vont ainsi se partager les différentes bonifications du second sprint intermédiaire au km 72,51km. Paul Daumont le premier suivi de Jannes Van Weele (2e), Barthélemy Yaméogo (3e). Le rythme imprimé par les ‘fuyards’’ va les porter jusqu’à 3’20’’ plus avant sur le groupe maillot jaune au moment d’aborder le village de Taré. La réplique des poursuivants après Nébou à 35 km de l’arrivée va cependant avoir raison de l’effort des hommes de tête. Leur avance va progressivement fondre et ils seront repris un par un. D’abord le Néerlandais victime de crevaison. Paul Daumont sentant le monde à ses talons tente une ultime accélération sur plus de 10km seul en tête mais il sera rattrapé à 5km de l’arrivée par le groupe. Les intentions des Algériens sont désormais claires : la victoire d’étape. Ils se positionnent pour cet objectif et la suite leur donnera raison avec deux places sur le podium. Le premier Burkinabè de l’étape est Saturnin Yaméogo arrivé 10e. Au classement général, aucun changement à noter. Le Sud-africain conserve le maillot jaune avec 41 secondes d’avance sur le Burkinabè Soumaïla Ilboudo. La tunique des points chauds demeure également la propriété du Marocain Youssef Bdadou. Celle du meilleur jeune est restée aussi sur les épaules de Soumaïla Ilboudo du Burkina, tout comme le maillot vert détenu par le vainqueur de l’étape Yacine Hamza de l’Algérie. La 7e étape prévu demain entre Ouagadougou et Pô est longue de 144,02 km. Voro KORAHIRE

items.title: Cyberattaques en France : des chambres froides du don du sang ciblées
items.description: Du sang et du plasma, destines a la transfusion, ont failli etre perdus en raison d'une cyberattaque, a revele le 3 novembre Le Canard enchaîne . Selon l'hebdomadaire, l'intrusion dans les serveurs de Coolworld – un prestataire de l'etablissement francais du sang (EFS), – a eu lieu dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre. Les pirates ont alors regle la temperature des chambres froides, devant etre maintenus a -30 °C, sur 110 °C. « a cette temperature-la, ca devient du boudin ! », a lâche un chirurgien au journal satirique. Ces 110 °C n'auraient pas ete atteints, « un technicien de permanence a constate dans la nuit […] une remontee en temperature dans les chambres froides », a precise l'EFS aupres du Palmipede. « Il y a zero consequence operatoire, car la situation a ete reperee », a de son cote assure le ministere francais de la Sante. « Des produits sanguins », avant leur livraison dans des etablissements de sante, ainsi que « des echantillons destines a nos biotheques » sont conserves dans ces chambres froides a fait savoir l'EFS dans un communique publie le 3 novembre sur son site, confirmant un « incident de cybersecurite » ayant entraîne une « alteration des parametres » des equipements. « Il ne s'agit pas d'attaque extremement poussee », a estime sur BFMTV Benoit Grunemwald, expert en cybersecurite chez ESET, « parce que lorsque vous avez des systemes de frigo mis a disposition sur internet sans aucune protection, tout a chacun peut faire des operations de destabilisation via ces frigos ». L'affaire survient alors qu'en France, ainsi que dans d'autres pays, des chaînes de supermarches et de distribution alimentaire rapportent depuis plusieurs semaines des intrusions informatiques dans leurs systemes de refrigeration, declenchant a distance le degivrage force des installations et causant plusieurs millions d'euros de pertes de denrees alimentaires.

items.title: FDSI : Ismaël Condé exprime sa reconnaissance au Président Mamadi Doumbouya après sa prise de fonction
items.description: Officiellement installé dans ses fonctions de Directeur général du Fonds de Développement Social et de l’Indigence (FDSI), Ismaël Condé a exprimé sa profonde gratitude au Président de la République, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya, pour la confiance placée en sa personne. Il entend inscrire son action dans une dynamique de renforcement de la solidarité nationale et de l’inclusion sociale. À la suite de sa prise de fonction officielle, le nouveau Directeur général du Fonds de Développement Social et de l’Indigence (FDSI), Ismaël Condé, a tenu à adresser ses remerciements au Président de la République, Chef de l’État, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya, pour sa nomination à la tête de cette institution stratégique. Conscient de l’importance de la mission qui lui est désormais confiée, Ismaël Condé considère cette nomination comme un honneur, mais surtout comme une responsabilité majeure au service de la nation et des populations guinéennes. Fort de plusieurs années d’expérience dans l’administration publique et le développement local, notamment à la tête de la commune de Matam, il affirme aborder cette nouvelle étape avec humilité, détermination et un sens élevé du devoir. À la tête du FDSI, sa priorité sera de contribuer au renforcement de la solidarité nationale, à la promotion de l’inclusion sociale et à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des personnes les plus vulnérables. Le nouveau Directeur général inscrit également son engagement dans la vision de transformation portée par le Chef de l’État, notamment à travers le programme Simandou 2040. Une ambition nationale qui, selon lui, doit permettre de faire du développement de la Guinée une dynamique collective, dont les retombées profiteront à toutes les couches de la population. Ismaël Condé prend ainsi l’engagement d’exercer ses nouvelles fonctions avec loyauté, intégrité, rigueur et dévouement. Il entend traduire la confiance présidentielle en actions concrètes, en résultats mesurables et en un engagement constant au service des citoyens. « Au Président de la République, merci pour la confiance. Je saurai m’en montrer digne par le travail, les résultats et l’engagement au service de la Guinée », a-t-il déclaré. Cette prise de fonction ouvre ainsi une nouvelle étape dans le parcours d’Ismaël Condé, avec pour ambition de faire de la solidarité et de la protection des populations vulnérables des leviers essentiels du développement national. AS FAR/Raja Casablanca : un Classico à enjeux
items.description: Reporté lors de la première journée de la Botola Pro D1 Inwi, le choc entre l’AS FAR et le Raja Casablanca se dispute ce mercredi au stade Olympique de Rabat. Une affiche toujours très attendue entre deux grandes formations du football national, avec un enjeu sportif important pour les deux équipes. Au classement, l’AS FAR occupe la sixième place avec 8 points en quatre matchs, tandis que le Raja pointe au treizième rang avec 6 unités en cinq rencontres. Un écart qui reflète les débuts plus convaincants des Militaires, toujours invaincus depuis le début du championnat. Avec deux victoires et deux matchs nuls, l’équipe militaire affiche une certaine régularité. Son parcours lui permet de rester au contact du groupe de tête et d'aborder ce rendez-vous avec une confiance mesurée. Une victoire mercredi lui offrirait l'occasion de gagner des places et de se rapprocher du podium. En face, le Raja Casablanca traverse un début de saison plus compliqué. Avec une victoire, trois nuls et une défaite, les Verts peinent à trouver leur rythme. Leur classement est en décalage avec les ambitions d'un club habitué à jouer les premiers rôles. Le déplacement à Rabat représente ainsi une occasion de réagir et de relancer une dynamique encore hésitante. Les deux formations auront donc des objectifs bien distincts. L'AS FAR cherchera à confirmer sa bonne entame et à profiter de l'avantage du terrain, alors que le Raja devra afficher davantage de caractère et d'efficacité pour repartir avec un résultat positif. Dans ce genre de confrontation, le classement ne suffit toutefois pas à déterminer le favori. La rivalité entre les deux clubs, la pression du résultat et l'importance du rendez-vous pourraient redistribuer les cartes. La bataille du milieu de terrain et la capacité à concrétiser les occasions seront notamment déterminantes. Pour les Militaires, l'enjeu sera de poursuivre leur série sans défaite. Pour les Rajaouis, il s'agira de frapper un grand coup et de montrer que leur saison peut encore prendre une autre tournure. Un Classico sous pression, où les trois points auront une saveur particulière pour chacun des deux camps. items.title: 38 detained in Karachi as police baton-charge protesters headed towards CM House
items.description: KARACHI: Thirty-eight people were detained on Wednesday as police used tear gas and baton-charged protesting teachers headed towards Chief Minister House from Karachi Press Club (KPC). Hundreds of teachers had gathered outside the press club on the call of the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association. They were headed towards CM House to present their demands that pertained to the service structure and called for delegating powers for transfers and postings to district officers. The protesters chanted slogans and attempted to move towards the CM House. However, when they arrived near Fawara Chowk, police baton-charged them and used tear gas shells to push them back toward the press club. Adjoining roads near the KPC were closed to traffic, according to a traffic police spokesperson. South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that a teachers’ organisation had announced a protest at the KPC, with a march planned toward the CM House. He said prior to the protest, the administration made concerted efforts to resolve the matter through negotiations and engaged officials from the education department to facilitate meaningful dialogue. The official said the protest leadership was categorically told that entry into the Red Zone — a term used to denote the area surrounding Governor House and Chief Minister House — would not be permitted. Nevertheless, the administration was directed to exhaust all available resources and make every effort to ensure a peaceful resolution through dialogue, he said. Raza alleged that around 3:15pm, the protesters turned “violent, abandoned the course of negotiations and forcibly started advancing towards the CM House.” He claimed that the protesting teachers “breached police barricades and resorted to pelting police personnel with stones, causing injuries to one official.” “Upon reaching and crossing Kabir Masjid on Governor House Road, the situation escalated, compelling police to resort to shelling to disperse the violent mob and restore order,” said the South police chief. He said during the operation, 38 protesters, including the president of the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association, Ghulam Rasool Mahar, and the general secretary, Aijaz Ali Chandio, were taken into custody. Raza insisted that police took drastic action as the teachers tried to enter the Red Zone. Meanwhile, Rafiq Nizamani, the vice president of the teachers’ association, told Dawn that in 2021, the Sindh government had chalked out an “education policy” under which it was decided that teachers would not be promoted and they would remain in the same pay scale. He said they launched a protest against this “arbitrary” decision as others were being promoted, but not them. He said that at the time, the government had assured them that their demands would be addressed, but this did not happen. He said apart from the service structure, their other demands pertained to delegating the powers of posting primary teachers to district government officials. He said that they wanted recruitment and the transfer/posting of teachers to be delegated to district officials. According to Nizamani, as the protesters moved from KPC towards CM House, police resorted to tear gas and a baton charge. He claimed that two teachers were also injured. Nizamani said that they had decided to set up a protest camp outside the KPC for the fulfilment of their demands. He admitted that the education officials had approached them for talks, but said they considered it “delaying tactics” in view of their past unfulfilled promises and decided to hold a protest march.

items.title: Trade Minister urges Ghanaian artisans to leverage SIAO 2026 for business growth
items.description: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has urged Ghanaian artisans and businesses to take advantage of the 18th International Arts and Handicraft Trade Show of Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026) to expand their businesses and explore opportunities in the regional market. She said Ghana’s participation in the exhibition as Guest Country of Honour presents an important opportunity to showcase the country’s creative industry, strengthen trade relations with Burkina Faso and promote intra-African trade. The Minister’s message was delivered by Ghana’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Kenneth Akibate, in a keynote address at the Ghana Day Celebration on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, in Ouagadougou. Mrs Ofosu-Adjare reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to deepening economic cooperation with Burkina Faso, noting that the exhibition reflects the longstanding friendship between the two countries and their shared ambition to promote local industries, industrialisation and economic opportunities for their people. She also expressed Ghana’s appreciation to the Government and people of Burkina Faso, as well as the organisers of SIAO 2026, for the warm reception and opportunity to showcase the country’s cultural heritage, creativity and economic potential. Meanwhile, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), Rashid Raymond Kramer, disclosed that Ghana would soon establish a trade house in Ouagadougou. He said the facility would, among other things, help facilitate trade between Ghana and Burkina Faso, providing further opportunities for businesses in both countries to access each other’s markets.

items.title: Mines : Appian mise sur les valeurs sûres d’Afrique
items.description: Le fonds britannique de capital-investissement minier Appian Capital Advisory range le Royaume, avec la Namibie et le Botswana, parmi les juridictions africaines les plus sûres pour ses investissements. Il prévoit de mobiliser environ 2 milliards de dollars sur le continent au cours des 12 à 24 prochains mois. Le Maroc fait partie des destinations minières que le fonds londonien Appian Capital Advisory juge les plus fiables en Afrique. Son fondateur et PDG, Michael Scherb, l’a indiqué dans des propos recueillis par Reuters, en classant le Royaume, la Namibie et le Botswana dans la catégorie des juridictions de premier rang. Ce message intervient alors que la société s’apprête à engager de nouveaux capitaux. Appian compte déployer entre 5 et 7 milliards de dollars à l’échelle mondiale au cours des 12 à 24 prochains mois. Environ 2 milliards sont destinés à l’Afrique, où le fonds détient actuellement trois investissements actifs. Spécialisé dans le financement de projets miniers, il intervient dans l’or, le cuivre, le zinc, les terres rares et d’autres minerais critiques. Ce volontarisme s’accompagne toutefois d’une mise en garde. Pour Michael Scherb, l’incertitude réglementaire pousse une partie des capitaux vers l’Amérique latine. « La géologie ne change pas, mais la politique des gouvernements, si », a-t-il lancé à Reuters. Les États africains ont en effet resserré leur emprise sur le secteur ces dernières années, en révisant leurs codes miniers, en relevant les redevances et en exigeant une participation locale plus importante, afin de capter une part plus large de la richesse tirée de leur sous-sol. Appian en a fait l’expérience sur le terrain. Le fonds s’est retiré de trois projets africains, dont ceux du Burkina Faso, au lendemain d’un coup d’État, et de la Tanzanie, en pleine crise électorale. Il compte désormais quatre investissements actifs en Amérique latine, principalement au Brésil. Cette région n’est pourtant pas exempte de tensions, le nationalisme des ressources s’y étant manifesté au Chili, au Pérou et au Mexique, mais ses régimes fiscaux et ses procédures d’octroi de permis y sont globalement restés plus stables. Le dirigeant insiste sur le coût d’un tel désengagement. S’il est onéreux pour un investisseur de quitter un pays, il l’est aussi pour l’État concerné, puisque le capital va simplement s’investir ailleurs. Il estime que les pays africains pourraient attirer une part nettement plus importante des investissements miniers mondiaux en simplifiant l’obtention des permis et en rendant leurs politiques plus prévisibles. « Les capitaux sont là », affirme-t-il, la question étant de savoir quels pays offriront la stabilité nécessaire pour les attirer. Au-delà des trois marchés qu’il cite en tête, Appian étudie des opportunités au Ghana, en Côte d’Ivoire, en Mauritanie et au Sénégal. Le fonds reste par ailleurs résolument optimiste sur le cuivre. Son patron s’attend à ce que l’offre mondiale peine à suivre une demande tirée par l’électrification, l’intelligence artificielle, les centres de données et l’extension des réseaux électriques. items.title: Police warn politicians against destroying campaign materials
items.description: …IGP orders commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political thugs and other individuals against the destruction or defacement of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Force said offenders would be arrested and prosecuted, warning that political differences or loyalty to a particular party did not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s campaign materials. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying the police had observed with concern growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of campaign materials across the country. The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately. “For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws, including Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law, which defines the offence of mischief. “Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely. “The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law. “No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed.” The police said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, had directed commissioners of police in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to take proactive measures to prevent such incidents. He also directed them to investigate reported cases and ensure that anyone found culpable was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. The statement added that political sponsors and individuals who recruited, encouraged or facilitated the destruction of campaign materials would also be held accountable where evidence established their involvement. The Force urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rights of others. It warned that political intolerance, intimidation and criminal conduct must not be allowed to undermine the democratic process. “The Nigeria Police Force will not allow political thugs and troublemakers to turn the nation’s political environment into a theatre of lawlessness. Those who choose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. “Be warned. Respect the law. Let democracy thrive,” the statement added. items.title: Police confirm death of girl allegedly pushed from two-storey building
items.description: … Suspect to face murder charge By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — The Imo State Police Command has confirmed the death of 17-year-old Chiamaka Chukwuokore, who was allegedly pushed from a two-storey building in Owerri. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Mr Henry Okoye, confirmed the development in a statement yesterday, disclosing that the 26-year-old suspect, Ifeanyi Chukwu Joseph, would now face a murder allegation following the victim’s death. Okoye said the incident occurred on November 1, 2026, along Mbonu Ejike Street, Ikeneagbu, Owerri. He said the suspect remained in police custody as investigations continued to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. “Following the victim’s death, the suspect is now facing a murder allegation. He remains in police custody as investigations continue to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that justice is served,” he said. The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, commiserated with the family of the deceased and assured that a thorough investigation was ongoing. The Command also urged members of the public to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified information and allow the police to carry out their duties professionally. Vanguard recalls that in an earlier statement following the incident, Okoye said the victim sustained serious injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital, where she was receiving treatment in critical condition. He also disclosed that an angry mob had attempted to lynch the suspect but police operatives intervened and rescued him before taking him into custody. items.title: 'We did it!': Democrat El-Sayed hails US Senate win, becomes first Muslim elected to upper chamber of Congress
items.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s US Senate race over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, US networks said early on Wednesday, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said in a speech attended by hundreds of supporters who screamed and hugged each other at his election headquarters in Detroit. “I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.” El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curve ball in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour. The Michigan medical administrator rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to win a key US Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters. El-Sayed held a nearly six-point lead on Rogers when networks called the race. Party-goer entrepreneur Trunetta Roach, 75, who attended El-Sayed’s victory party in downtown Detroit wearing US flag-design diamante high-heels, said: “We are sick and tired of being sick and tired. And I’m so proud of all the work. It was boots on the ground. We were always out, but we were never outworked.” “I’m feeling elated. The kids are all right. I was concerned about them. They didn’t seem very engaged, but I was wrong. They showed up.” ‘Swear me in’ Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans. But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s fractured, for-profit health care system. “You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system. During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo. The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969. “Everybody in politics is so trash. So to see ethical Muslims be at the forefront representing us and showing everybody what we’re actually about … it means everything,” said micro-influencer Maryam Bozai, 28. At the victory party, crowds gathered around TVs tuned to left-leaning cable news channel MS NOW , cheering jubilantly each time the Democrat’s trademark blue flashed on screen to announce another race won by the party. “Tsunami! Tsunami!” chanted Ondine Fortune, 64, a Democratic Party media planner. El-Sayed supporters rubbed shoulders with left-leaning influencers and union activists, a group that lent El-Sayed their formidable campaign infrastructure to reach Michigan’s large organised labour community. Eboni Taylor, a vice-president at Higher Heights which promotes Black women seeking office, said El-Sayed had “gone places where I just would not expect to see him.” “What’s most remarkable is that he’s showing up in places that are not the usual prescription for the Democratic Party. He’s going wherever the people want him to be,” Taylor said between social media livestreams and celebratory dancing. El-Sayed faced Islamophobic attacks and mockery for his Arabic name from US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. But El-Sayed may yet have the last laugh. Addressing the vice president, El-Sayed said in his victory speech, “you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January”. Dr Arif Alvi congratulates El-Sayed Pakistan’s former president Dr Arif Alvi congratulated El-Sayed on his victory in a post on X and said it “resonates far beyond one election”. “It is a reminder that democracy matters: that the people’s mandate is sacred, that every vote counts, and that the will of the people cannot be wished away, manipulated or denied with guns,” he said, wishing El-Sayed success in his role. Alvi added that “being Muslim should never make anyone a target of hatred, prejudice or intimidation. No one should have to face the vile excesses of Islamophobia.” He noted that the “people’s voice will prevail”, expressing his hope that the lesson would reach beyond US shores.

items.title: Les forces américaines se retirent d’une base aérienne stratégique au sud de la Somalie
items.description: Les troupes americaines presentes sur la base aerienne de Baledogle en Somalie se sont retirees du poste avance strategique, servant de plaque tournante pour les operations antiterroristes dans la Corne de l'Afrique, indique le site d'information militaire Stars and Stripes , le 3 novembre, citant des rapports de presse de medias somaliens publies la veille. La base constituait un centre pour recueillir des renseignements et pour soutenir les efforts de lutte contre les elements du mouvement terroriste somalien Al-Shabab, lie a Al-Qaïda. L'AFRICOM s'abstient de commenter directement le retrait Le commandement americain pour l'Afrique (AFRICOM) n'a pas souhaite commenter directement le depart des troupes du site somalien. « Dans un souci de securite operationnelle, nous ne communiquons pas les details des operations en cours », a declare le porte-parole de l'AFRICOM le 2 novembre, mais a tout de meme precise que le commandement « repositionne ses forces afin d'optimiser les operations antiterroristes en cours ». L'AFRICOM n'a divulgue aucune information sur le nombre de militaires deployes sur la base, ni sur les effectifs concernes par le retrait signale et le lieu de leur redeploiement La presence des troupes americaines en Somalie changerait-elle de nature ? D'apres Stars and Stripes, le retrait de Baledogle pourrait marquer un tournant notable de la presence americaine dans la region. En mai 2025, les Forces operationnelles interarmees combinees Corne de l'Afrique (CJTF-HOA) ont investi dans des infrastructures militaires a Baledogle, avec notamment la construction d'un centre medical et l'amelioration des logements et de la securite. Les investissements devaient soutenir une presence durable et developper l'aerodrome « en tant que site perenne », selon la CJTF-HOA. Si la mission americaine sur le sol somalien a connu certaines fluctuations au fil des annees, avec le retrait de 700 soldats du pays au terme du premier mandat du president Donald Trump en 2020, la decision a cependant ete annulee des 2022 par son successeur Joe Biden, qui a retabli la presence permanente dans la region pour soutenir les efforts et ameliorer les capacites de lutte contre Al-Shabab. Dans une autre perspective, le mouvement Al-Shabab avait affirme que le retrait americain de la base de Baledogle « a ete influence par notre escalade », a rapporte le service de surveillance des menaces liees au djihad et au terrorisme (JTTM) du Middle East Media Research Institute (MEMRI), le 2 novembre.

items.title: Ghanaian engineer Johannes Amo-Aye wins Africa Prize award for hybrid wind and solar innovation
items.description: Ghanaian engineer Johannes Amo-Aye has won the £5,000 One-to-Watch Award at the 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation for developing a hybrid wind and solar energy system designed to provide reliable electricity to off-grid communities. His innovation, the Fusion Wind Turbine, combines wind and solar power to provide electricity to underserved communities, particularly rural health facilities that rely on expensive diesel generators during power outages. The award, decided by an audience vote, was presented at a ceremony held at NH Johannesburg Sandton in South Africa. Amo-Aye’s recognition comes as the continent continues to grapple with electricity access challenges, with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without reliable electricity. In Ghana, the technology is intended to address power supply challenges in rural health centres, where outages can disrupt medical services, compromise vaccine refrigeration and affect the delivery of emergency care. How the technology works Developed by MINAGIE Energy, the Fusion Wind Turbine combines a Darrieus H-type vertical-axis wind turbine with a solar arch fitted with bifacial panels. The wind turbine uses a gearless direct-drive generator incorporating magnetic levitation technology, which the developers say reduces friction, noise and maintenance requirements. The solar panels complement wind generation to provide electricity across different weather conditions and times of the day. According to the development team, approximately 90 per cent of the system’s components are designed and manufactured in Ghana, with only specialised components such as rare-earth magnets, weather stations and hybrid controllers imported. The system is designed to operate without lubricants or oil, with routine maintenance largely involving system checks and cleaning of the solar panels. Amo-Aye developed the technology after growing up in an Accra suburb where frequent power outages exposed the limitations of conventional electricity supply. Working with co-founder and public health expert Elizabeth Onireti, he sought to develop an energy solution that would address the needs of rural communities while reducing dependence on diesel generators. Two rural health centres benefiting MINAGIE Energy says the Fusion Wind Turbine has so far been installed at two rural health centres in Ghana’s Eastern Region, serving an estimated catchment population of about 850 people. The company says the installations have replaced diesel generators, saving approximately $500 monthly in fuel costs while providing electricity for lighting and refrigeration. Amo-Aye has cited an incident in 2024 involving a midwife who had to deliver a baby during a community-wide power outage using mobile phone torches. He said poor lighting contributed to warning signs being missed and the baby subsequently dying. According to him, the same mother later returned to deliver another child in a well-lit ward with functioning equipment, illustrating the difference reliable electricity can make to healthcare delivery. The project has also received support from UNICEF Ghana’s UNICEF Scale-Up Fund. Expansion plans MINAGIE Energy is now looking to expand deployment of the technology across rural Ghana. The company plans to install 25 turbines and train 25 technicians in 2026, followed by an expansion to 60 turbines and five operational hubs in 2027. By 2028, it hopes to have deployed more than 100 turbines and established 10 hubs, while also introducing carbon credit monetisation. Amo-Aye says affordability remains a major obstacle to expansion because of the high upfront cost of the equipment and the financial support communities may need to transition from diesel-powered systems. While Amo-Aye received the audience-voted One-to-Watch Award, the main £50,000 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation went to Nigerien innovator Mamane Kabirou Ousseini for his medical monitoring platform, Likita Care. The platform combines connected medical devices, clinical software and local digital manufacturing to support patient cardiac and prenatal monitoring. Its embedded artificial intelligence module helps interpret vital signs in real time, while a central dashboard allows healthcare workers to monitor multiple patients. More than 70 monitoring units have been produced and deployed across five medical centres in Niger, following testing involving more than 100 patients and more than 4,000 data points. Ousseini plans to use the prize money to commercialise the platform in Niger and prepare for expansion into other West African markets. Three other innovators received £10,000 each as runners-up: South Africa’s Dyllon Randall for Pee-Cycling, a urine-to-fertiliser recovery system, and Kenya’s Alice Muhuhu for MoyoECG, a portable heart monitoring device, and Naom Monari for Renal Roads, a mobile dialysis clinic. The four finalists were selected from a cohort of 16 entrepreneurs who completed an eight-month training and mentoring programme organised by the Royal Academy of Engineering. The Africa Prize is delivered by the Royal Academy of Engineering and part-funded by the UK Government’s International Science Partnerships Fund.

items.title: The Socializing That’s Replacing Friend Time
items.description: What is your favorite way to spend an evening? Perhaps, hearing this question, you’d picture a big, steaming plate of spaghetti from a beloved neighborhood restaurant. Maybe you’d imagine going dancing with friends, shimmying off the stress of a long week. Or you’d belt along with a crowd of perfect strangers at a concert, play Frisbee in the park, or stroll aimlessly with a cone of sprinkled soft serve. Yet last year, when more than 2,000 survey participants answered this open-ended query, many of them described a very different kind of scene: a night at home, cozied up with family. When researchers analyzed the long answers, they found that 43 percent of respondents mentioned time with family or a romantic partner—the most common activity, tied with watching a TV show. For Jeffrey A. Hall, a University of Kansas communication professor and a co-leader of the project, this was heartening. He knew, of course, that the average American is staying in more now compared with past decades, and hanging with friends less. But he was reminded: Time at home is not necessarily time alone. He read description after description of people relaxing together, catching up on their days, curling up for a movie, or cooking a good meal. Honestly, he thought that all sounded pretty nice. Granted, these were depictions of an ideal evening; the survey didn’t measure how people were actually spending their hours. But some studies suggest that, although alone time is increasing in the United States, family time may be as well. Over the past handful of decades, on average, parents have started spending more time with young kids; romantic partners have become more intertwined; more grown children are maintaining close relationships with their parents; and more grandparents are actively involved in caring for their grandkids. And many Americans seem to love the idea of kinship. In a 2023 Pew poll , nine out of 10 participants named “spending time with family” to be either very important or the most important priority for them—far outranking every other category, including religious faith, physical activity, nature, career, and community. Socializing at home, in sweatpants rather than heels, is socializing nonetheless. In some ways, Americans are living through a golden age of family time. But many of them are also losing a different kind of connection—one that’s important in its own right. For early Americans, family tended to be the nucleus of social life. Relatives commonly worked together , on farms or in small businesses, and helped one another raise children. But with industrialization, more people were able to separate socializing from labor—and to travel beyond their village, meet new people, and actively choose their companions. Some historians argue that “pure friendship”—the kind of relationship opted into solely for its own sake—largely didn’t exist until then. It was a modern invention. Today’s family-forward age is, obviously, very different from that of the 18th century. The average family is much smaller, with fewer siblings or cousins who might feel like peers; time together might be less chaotic and labor-intensive, more quiet and cushy. (If tilling soil was once the quintessential shared activity, now the standard looks more like streaming Netflix and ordering in.) And yet, in a certain sense, Americans today also seem to be homebound together by a kind of necessity. When participants said they were unsatisfied with how frequently they saw friends, Hall and his colleagues asked what was getting in the way. Nearly 40 percent said, “I don’t have enough money.” A third said they were too busy or tired, and a third reported not having enough time. (Respondents could pick more than one answer.) Hall’s sense is that two realities can be true at once: A lot of people love being with their family members. They might also feel like other kinds of socializing are slipping out of reach. This shift could be happening for a number of reasons. One is the skyrocketing cost of living. The price of housing, in particular, has been rising for years; if your home is taking up a major share of your budget, you might want to take full advantage of it—and cut back on other expenses. Affluent Americans tend to have bigger houses and more land than they used to, the Princeton University sociologist Patrick Sharkey told me, making staying at home extra tempting (and the home itself extra expensive). Working-class Americans, meanwhile, might be spending so much on rent that they can’t afford to meet friends at restaurants or bars. More and more low-wage workers have unreliable schedules too, which makes planning outings difficult. When public resources (parks, playgrounds, transit systems) aren’t well used, they may get less investment, which can lead to neglect—which, in turn, can make those resources less accessible or appealing. Sharkey calls this “the privatization of our daily lives and the disinvestment in collective life.” Many people also have to spend time with family—for caregiving purposes. More American adults are providing care for their aging relatives, some at the same time that they’re still caring for younger children. And parents today tend to do a lot of hanging out with their kids, rather than letting them run around independently. Moms do the bulk of that child care, but fathers and grandparents are pitching in more than in the past. To be clear, they’re not all gritting their teeth; multiple studies have found that parents and children describe time together as positive for their well-being, Melissa Milkie, a University of Toronto sociologist, told me. Still, with only so many hours in a day, friendship can get sidelined. An occasional night out with friends, for a parent, might feel untenable when a babysitter costs $30 an hour. Even getting out with the kids is hard. Let’s say you live in New York, and you and your partner want to go with your two children to see a movie in a theater. You could pay about $20 a ticket for a total of $80, not counting the price of the subway or a couple of tubs of popcorn. Or you could stay home, tear open a bag of chips, and pay $3 to stream a movie together. Hall’s study suggests that many people are embracing that kind of snug evening—that their values may be changing along with their schedules and finances. Much of the time, in coverage about Americans staying home, the portrait feels both apocalyptic (everyone is ceaselessly doomscrolling, glassy-eyed and alone) and judgy (people can’t be bothered to nurture their friendships). A different conclusion could be that people are resilient. “We make sense of the social conditions that we find ourselves in,” Hall said. His team found that both family and friend time were associated with higher life satisfaction and less loneliness. Facing real constraints on your routine, you can idealize the life you actually lead. That said, plenty of people don’t have loved ones at home. A society that reveres the nuclear family is one that might fail to look after many of its members: those who live far from their relatives, or who have lost them or never felt accepted by them, or who don’t have a partner or kids, by choice or by chance. Unmarried people report feeling lonely at much higher rates, on average, than married ones do. And an analysis of time-use data from 1965 to 2018 found that solitary leisure time had increased by 118 minutes a day for unmarried people who lived alone—but by only 40 minutes for everyone else. Even for people who do live with family, decentering friendship—and the outside world—has real consequences. Milkie’s research suggests that for many people, shared time in the home involves a lot of parallel play: sitting in the same room but doing your own thing. Studies have found that people tend to enjoy that type of side-by-side, passive companionship more than total solitude. Yet she and Hall both told me that this kind of engagement isn’t likely to boost well-being as much as actually sharing an activity. Hall’s participants had painted such lovely portraits of their restful dream evenings, but the reality of home life isn’t necessarily so rosy. In a 2024 study , Sharkey analyzed people’s participation in work, school, dining, leisure, sports, and religious or spiritual life from 2003 to 2022. He found that over that period, people spent roughly the same amount of time on those activities—but the share of time they spent doing them at home significantly increased. (This shift began long before COVID.) When those activities occurred at home, they were associated with lower levels of happiness and perceived by the individuals as less meaningful. That remained true, though less so, even when family or friends were around. Breaking out of that private sphere can get harder and harder the less you do it. Examining the habits of individuals, psychologists have long observed a pattern, Hall said: When people get accustomed to loneliness, they may start declining social engagements. They aren’t just less motivated; they actually begin to discount the value of that connection. “Maybe they say to somebody who might invite them, I’m just not feeling up to it right now ,” he told me. “Or maybe they’d say yes, and then the time comes and they go, You know, I just don’t think I can stand it. ” He’s worried that the same could happen on a much broader level. If friendship starts losing cultural cachet, more Americans may deprioritize it. Family might help make up for some of that lost connection. But it’s not a perfect substitute for the particular joys of friendship. The French philosopher Geoffroy de Lagasnerie spends every evening with his two best friends, including holidays; he’s written a book about structuring his life and identity around those relationships. But he doesn’t love when people refer to such bonds as “chosen family.” The implication is that friendships are inherently more casual—that they can be elevated only when put in a bracket that’s taken more seriously. In fact, he said, the two categories are qualitatively different. He thinks the nuclear unit can cause people to turn inward—to embrace an ideology of “my home, my family, my land.” When you go out to meet friends, on the other hand, you’re in a position of receptivity: potentially hearing new ideas, having new experiences, maybe connecting with people who are quite different from you. I don’t know if the line between friends and family is always quite so stark. But there may be something to the idea that friendship requires openness: to other people, and also to a distinct kind of growth. After all, friends have no legal contract or blood tie binding them; they simply commit to experiencing the world together. “Pure friendship” is based on the tenuous ties of affection and curiosity, and it depends on overcoming solipsism. That’s why it’s so special—and also why, when it’s not protected, it’s so easily lost.

Grand Lomé : Une nouvelle opération de libération des emprises publiques annoncée
items.description: Lomé, 4 nov. (ATOP) – Le comité ad hoc de lutte contre l’occupation anarchique du domaine public dans le Grand Lomé a annoncé dans un communiqué, le mardi 3 novembre, de nouvelles opérations de libération des emprises des voies publiques. Les occupants irréguliers sont invités à libérer les espaces concernés au plus tard le vendredi 20 novembre, sous peine de voir leurs installations dégagées à leurs frais. Cette annonce intervient dans un contexte marqué par la persistance de l’occupation irrégulière des espaces publics, malgré les opérations de désencombrement menées en février 2023. Selon le comité, cette situation compromet la sécurité des usagers, entrave la fluidité de la circulation et complique l’intervention des services de secours. Ces mesures concernent notamment, les étalages commerciaux, les baraques et points de vente non réglementés, les conteneurs installés à des fins commerciales, ainsi que les dépôts de gravats, de sable et de matériaux de construction sur les trottoirs. Le stationnement anarchique des véhicules, les dépôts d’ordures et les affichages publicitaires non réglementés figurent également parmi les pratiques interdites. A travers cette initiative, le comité entend contribuer à l’assainissement urbain, à l’amélioration de la circulation et à l’embellissement de la capitale. Il souligne également que le dégagement des emprises facilitera l’accès des services de secours et réduira certains risques, notamment les accidents et les inondations liés à l’obstruction des caniveaux. Les modalités de cette opération et les dispositions envisagées pour sa mise en œuvre seront au centre d’une conférence de presse prévue ce mercredi 4 novembre à Lomé. ATOP/MG/SED

items.title: Binah : SIBEC-Togo sensibilise sur la charge mentale et le bien-être des hommes et des garçons
items.description: Pagouda, 4 nov. (ATOP)- La journée internationale de l’homme a été célébrée le mardi 3 novembre à Kétao, chef-lieu de la commune Binah 2. Célébrée chaque année le 19 novembre, cette journée est placée sous le thème : « Charge mentale, bien-être des hommes et des garçons ». L’évènement initié par l’Association solidarité internationale pour le bien-être communautaire (SIBEC-Togo) a bénéficié de l’appui de la coopération allemande, mise en œuvre par la GIZ à travers le projet « DeZon : Promotion de la participation, de l’égalité et de l’équité de genre au Togo », ainsi que du ministère des Solidarités, du Genre, de la Famille et de la Protection de l’Enfance (MSGFPE). La célébration va se dérouler dans quatre localités, notamment Kpélé, Lavié, Tové, Kétao et Pya. L’objectif est de promouvoir la santé et le bien-être des hommes à travers un dialogue communautaire inclusif. Il s’agit également de sensibiliser les hommes, les ménages, les leaders religieux, traditionnels et communautaires sur les enjeux liés à la charge mentale et au bien-être masculin. Cette journée constitue une occasion de revaloriser le rôle des hommes au sein de la société et de mettre en lumière les domaines dans lesquels les différences entre les hommes et les femmes peuvent être source de désavantages pour les hommes. Elle permet également de reconnaître les contributions positives des hommes à la vie communautaire, familiale et professionnelle, tout en attirant l’attention sur les défis auxquels ils sont confrontés. Le formateur, Dr Tchangaye Rodrigue, a entretenu les participants sur la charge mentale et le bien-être des hommes et des garçons. Il a notamment abordé les causes et les conséquences de la charge mentale, ainsi que les approches de solutions. Les échanges ont également porté sur la masculinité positive, la déconstruction des stéréotypes de genre et la nécessité de promouvoir une alliance entre les hommes et les femmes. Le directeur exécutif de l’ONG SIBEC-Togo, Abilimou Meyaba François, a souligné que cette journée vise à encourager le bien-être masculin, à cultiver l’écoute mutuelle et à poursuivre la construction d’un avenir meilleur pour la préfecture de la Binah et le Togo en général. Il a exhorté les hommes à être des acteurs de paix, des piliers d’amour au sein de leurs foyers et des modèles de bienveillance. « L’homme épanoui est celui qui chemine en parfaite harmonie avec sa conjointe, en tant que partenaire, pour bâtir un foyer stable et éduquer des enfants équilibrés », a-t-il conclu. Le maire de la commune Binah 2, Mme Welabalo Tchanta, a exprimé sa gratitude aux premières autorités togolaises pour les efforts consentis en faveur de la promotion de la journée internationale de l’homme. ATOP/AK/MD

items.title: State Police Bill to reach Tinubu for assent today — Reps
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The State Police Bill, seeking to decentralise policing responsibilities between the Federal and state governments, will be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday for assent. The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, disclosed this while presiding over plenary, following the approval of the proposed constitutional amendment by 29 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly. Kalu expressed excitement over the endorsement of the proposed police reform by more than two-thirds of the state legislatures, describing the development as a major step towards the establishment of state police in Nigeria. “The State Police Bill has received the backing of 29 State Assemblies. Later today, the Clerk to the National Assembly will transmit it to the President for assent,” he said. The approval by the state assemblies marks a significant milestone in efforts to amend the Constitution to allow states to establish and manage their own police forces alongside the Nigeria Police Force. The proposed reform is aimed at addressing concerns over Nigeria’s centralised policing structure, which critics argue limits the capacity of security agencies to respond effectively to local security challenges. Under the proposed arrangement, state governments would have greater responsibility for policing within their jurisdictions, while the Federal Government would retain its own police structure. The reform is expected to allow states to develop policing strategies tailored to their security needs, with the aim of strengthening intelligence gathering, community-based security and responses to crime. The transmission of the bill to the President marks the next stage in the constitutional amendment process, following its passage by the National Assembly and approval by the required number of state legislatures. The proposed establishment of state police has remained a major issue in Nigeria’s security reform debate, with supporters advocating decentralised policing as a means of improving security management across the country. items.title: Former convicts recount broken marriages, family rejection after prison as Crime Check Foundation calls for change
items.description: Former prisoners have shared painful accounts of broken marriages, abandoned families and rejection by loved ones following their release from prison, highlighting the difficulties many face in rebuilding their lives after serving their sentences. Some said their prison records had cost them their marriages, while others recounted how their families and society continued to treat them as criminals despite efforts to reform and reintegrate into their communities. The experiences were shared at the first-ever National Ex-Convicts Reintegration Conference organised by the Crime Check Foundation, which is calling for former prisoners to be recognised as returning citizens rather than labelled ex-convicts. Participants said the stigma attached to imprisonment had made it difficult for many of them to secure employment, restore broken relationships and find stable accommodation after their release. One former prisoner, who spoke about the impact of his prison history on his family life, said his wife had left him, leaving him to struggle to provide for himself and his children. “Life after prison has been extremely difficult. My wife left me because of my prison history. Today, I struggle to feed myself and my children. And I have no other place to sleep except seeking shelter in the slum. Sadly, my story is not unique,” he said. He explained that his experience reflected the difficulties faced by many others who had served prison sentences but continued to face rejection long after their release. “Many of my fellow ex-convicts have been abandoned by their spouses, rejected by their families, denied employment and stigmatised by society,” he added. The former prisoner said society often encouraged inmates to reform while in prison but failed to give them a fair chance when they returned home. He said that their past mistakes continued to define them, making it difficult to move forward even after serving their sentences. According to him, the rejection and lack of support sometimes pushed former prisoners back into difficult circumstances, undermining efforts to help them become responsible members of society. Another concern raised at the conference was the financial burden some returning prisoners face after their release, with many struggling to settle debts and meet basic needs. A participant described how former prisoners often returned to society with financial obligations but had little or no means of meeting them. He suggested that some were forced to find ways to repay what they owed, whether through money, labour or other forms of assistance, warning that failure to meet these obligations could expose them to further difficulties. “Most of the returning citizens come out with debt that they have to pay. It’s either you pay in the form of work, or you pay in kind. If you don’t pay, then you go back. Life is tough at times,” he said.

items.title: Ogou : Atakpamé abrite un colloque sur la résilience éducative en Afrique
items.description: Atakpamé, 4 nov. (ATOP) – L’Ecole normale supérieure (ENS) d’Atakpamé accueille du 4 au 6 novembre un colloque scientifique international consacré aux défis majeurs de l’éducation sur le continent africain. Placé sous le thème « Repenser la formation des enseignants en Afrique : innovations pédagogiques, numérique éducatif et production de savoirs pour des systèmes éducatifs résilients », cet événement est co-organisé par l’ENS d’Atakpamé, l’École normale supérieure de Porto-Novo, l’Institut national des sciences de l’éducation (INSE) de l’Université de Lomé, ainsi que l’Institut de formation en sciences pédagogiques et de l’administration universitaire (IFSPAU) de l’Université de Kara avec l’appui du ministère de l’Education nationale. Cette rencontre vise à promouvoir la recherche scientifique, le partage des connaissances et l’élaboration de solutions durables face aux mutations du secteur éducatif. Durant trois jours de travaux, les enseignants chercheurs du Togo, du Bénin et autres vont approfondir leurs discussions sur l’amélioration des méthodes pédagogiques, l’intégration du numérique et de la production endogène de savoirs pour consolider la résilience des institutions éducatives. Le ministre de l’Education Nationale, Mama Omorou, a indiqué que la réforme de la formation des enseignants ne saurait se limiter à des ajustements superficiels, mais doit s’inscrire dans une dynamique paradigmatique, politique et pragmatique. Il a rappelé que l’État accorde une priorité absolue à l’éducation, levier essentiel du développement national. Le ministre a également exhorté les chercheurs et les acteurs présents à formuler des recommandations concrètes et des doctrines d’action adaptées aux réalités du continent, afin de garantir l’émergence d’une école africaine inclusive, performante et tournée vers l’avenir. Le directeur général de l’ENS d’Atakpamé, Prof. Donyo Agbenoko, a souligné que ce colloque constitue un espace privilégié de dialogue, de partage d’expériences et de consolidation de la coopération inter universitaire pour relever ensemble les défis de la formation professorale. Les travaux se sont déroulés en présence du gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, général de brigade Dadja Maganawé, des acteurs de l’éducation, des autorités politiques, administratives et militaires. ATOP/KJ/KKT/AR

items.title: Army rewards soldier N500,000 for rejecting kidnap suspect’s bribe
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 3 Division of the Nigerian Army and Commander of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), Major General Maxwell Dangana, has rewarded a soldier, Private Utim Terwase, with N500,000 for rejecting an alleged bribe offered by a suspected notorious kidnapper. Military sources said Terwase apprehended the suspect following an attempted escape but rejected money allegedly offered in exchange for his release and subsequently handed him over to the appropriate authorities. Confirming the development, the spokesman for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, said the reward was presented on behalf of the GOC by the Commander of Sector 6, Colonel Philimon Malgwi. Oteh said Dangana, who spoke through Malgwi during the presentation, commended the soldier for demonstrating honesty, discipline and professionalism. He said: “The soldier’s conduct reflects the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty and commitment to duty expected of personnel of the Nigerian Army. “Rather than compromise his responsibility for personal gain, he upheld the values of honesty, accountability and selfless service by discharging his duties responsibly.” The GOC said the N500,000 reward was in recognition of the soldier’s integrity and commitment to duty, adding that the amount was equivalent to the bribe he reportedly rejected. “Operation Enduring Peace therefore considers Private Terwase’s action worthy of commendation and encourages all personnel to emulate his exemplary conduct,” he said. Dangana added that the recognition reinforced the operation’s commitment to promoting accountability, ethical conduct and professionalism among its personnel. He said the military would continue to encourage personnel to discharge their constitutional responsibilities with integrity, discipline and dedication. items.title: UNICEF commends Taraba over education reforms
items.description: … As state launches Learning Passport in 50 pilot schools By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has commended the Taraba State Government for its education reforms, particularly the introduction of free and compulsory basic and secondary education, abolition of illegal school fees and distribution of free learning materials. The commendation was given by UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Bauchi, Dr Nuzhat Rafique, during the official launch of the Nigeria Learning Passport (NLP) in Jalingo. Rafique, who was represented by the Education Officer, UNICEF Bauchi Field Office, Raphael Aiyedipe, said the state’s education policies had contributed to an increase in school enrolment from approximately 760,000 to more than one million pupils since the inception of the current administration. She also applauded the government for promoting inclusive education for children with special needs, while strengthening teacher recruitment and professional development. According to her, the rollout of the digital learning platform was made possible through partnerships with Microsoft, the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), Airtel, IHS Towers and TECNO. She explained that the programme was designed to address connectivity barriers, reduce the number of out-of-school children and ensure continuity of learning, particularly in vulnerable communities. In his address, Governor Agbu Kefas reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to making education accessible to every child in the state, describing it as a cornerstone of sustainable development and national progress. Kefas, who was represented by the Head of Service, Dr Hamidu Kara, said the Nigeria Learning Passport represented a major step towards ensuring that no child was left behind in the state’s educational development. “The Nigerian Learning Passport represents a bold step forward in our commitment to ensure that no child is left behind in their educational journey, especially in these challenging times,” he said. He explained that the digital platform would provide flexible, accessible and inclusive learning opportunities, particularly for children affected by crises or disruptions to conventional schooling. The governor added that the initiative aligned with his administration’s free education agenda and urged stakeholders, teachers and students to embrace and promote the platform. Also speaking, the Commissioner for Secondary, Technical and Vocational Education, Dr Augustina Godwin, announced that the pilot phase of the programme would commence in 50 schools across the state. She assured that the government would expand the initiative to more schools to enable additional students to benefit from the digital learning platform. items.title: Le nouveau préfet de Bas-Mono Col. Akagna Kodjo entre en fonction
items.description: Afagnagan, 4 nov. (ATOP) – Le nouveau préfet de Bas-Mono, Colonel Akagna Kodjo, a pris fonction le mardi 3 novembre à Afagnagan, lors d’une cérémonie de passation de service. La cérémonie a été présidée par le gouverneur de la région Maritime, Taïrou Bagbiègue. Elle a été marquée par la signature et l’échange des documents de passation de charge. Le gouverneur a félicité le Colonel Akagna pour sa nomination et rendu un hommage au préfet sortant pour les efforts consentis. Il a insisté sur la mission du préfet en matière du développement de la préfecture. Le gouverneur a invité la population à collaborer avec son nouveau préfet pour la réussite de sa mission. Le préfet Akagna a exprimé sa gratitude aux autorités du pays pour la confiance placée en sa personne. Il a remercié son prédécesseur pour le travail abattu tout en soulignant que « C’est au bout de l’ancienne corde que je tisserai la nouvelle ». Le Colonel Akagna a promis de travailler avec toutes les couches sociales afin de répondre aux aspirations des populations de Bas-Mono. « La priorité sera consacrée à la sécurité, car aucun développement ne peut se faire sans la quiétude de la population », a indiqué le nouveau préfet avant d’inviter l’ensemble des acteurs à l’accompagner dans sa mission pour le développement de la préfecture et la consolidation de la paix sociale. Le préfet sortant, Sogbo Kokou Amétépé, a témoigné sa reconnaissance au Président du Conseil pour la confiance. Il a dressé le bilan de son passage à la tête de la préfecture en termes de renforcement de l’autorité de l’Etat, de la consolidation de la paix et de la sécurité, de la promotion de la cohésion sociale, de l’amélioration de la gouvernance locale et de l’accompagnement des collectivités territoriales dans l’exercice de leur responsabilité. M. Sogbo a remercié les populations pour leur collaboration avant de réaffirmer sa disponibilité à accompagner son successeur dans la réussite de sa mission. La cérémonie a mobilisé des chefs de services déconcentrés de l’Etat, les maires des deux communes, des chefs traditionnels, des forces de sécurité, des religieux, des leaders communautaires et autres personnalités. items.title: State Police: 30 states approve bill, six yet to respond
items.description: Senate gives November 19 deadline for outstanding submissions By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The proposed establishment of state police in Nigeria has moved closer to becoming law, with 30 State Houses of Assembly approving the constitutional amendment, while six others are yet to formally transmit their decisions to the National Assembly. The Senate has given the outstanding states until November 19 to forward their resolutions, ahead of the transmission of the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), disclosed this on Wednesday, saying the 30 approvals had exceeded the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of the 36 state legislatures. He explained that the constitutional amendment process involved three stages: passage by the National Assembly, approval by at least two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly and presidential assent. According to him, the National Assembly had fulfilled its responsibility by passing the bill and transmitting it to all 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. Bamidele said: “Let me explain again, for the avoidance of doubt, three keywords are used in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended. The first word is passage, the second word is approval and the third word is assent. “The reason the writers of our Constitution, our forefathers, put all these specific words is to ensure that no part of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria can be easily amended without the buying in of all the critical stakeholders at all levels of governance.” He said the requirement was designed to ensure that major constitutional changes were not imposed without the participation of critical stakeholders across the federation. The Senate Leader stressed that the 30 approvals already received were above the constitutional threshold of 24 states, describing the development as evidence of considerable support for the proposed reform among elected representatives. “Two things that need to be emphasised here is that we needed two-thirds of the states at the very least for this to pass, and already two-thirds will be 24. So, as of yet, we already got 30 states, showing the popularity of this bill among Nigerians through the elected representatives in the State Houses of Assembly,” he said. The 30 states that have approved the proposal are Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara. The six states whose formal responses were still being awaited were Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue and Oyo. Bamidele, however, said the National Assembly was still expecting the outstanding submissions to enable it to conclude the process. He said the intention was to give all 36 state legislatures the opportunity to formally communicate their positions on the proposed constitutional amendment, whether in support or opposition. According to him, the Clerk to the National Assembly had written to the state assemblies on October 15, requesting their decisions within the stipulated period. “We believe that the remaining six states will still get back to the National Assembly before next week Monday, which is the deadline,” he added. Meanwhile, the Deputy President of the Senate and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Constitution Review, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), informed his colleagues that Kano State had sent its response and that the communication was expected to reach the National Assembly shortly. The proposed amendment is part of efforts to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture by providing a constitutional framework for individual states to establish their own police services. The proposal has remained a major issue in national discussions on how to address the country’s security challenges and whether policing responsibilities should remain concentrated at the federal level. With 30 states having approved the amendment, the proposal has crossed the required state-level threshold, leaving the outstanding formal responses and presidential assent as the next stages in the process.
