items.title: Tour du Faso 2026: Hamza Yacine s’offre une troisième victoire d’étape
items.description: L’Algérien Hamza Yacine poursuit sa belle moisson sur les routes du 37e Tour cycliste international du Faso. Le coureur, porteur du dossard 143, a remporté, ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, la 6e étape disputée entre Saponé et Léo, sur une distance de 140,49 km. Il signe ainsi son troisième succès d’étape dans cette édition. Hamza Yacine confirme sa domination dans cette compétition. Au terme d’une course longue de 140,49 km, le cycliste algérien a franchi la ligne d’arrivée en première position avec un temps de 3 h 09 min 56 s, soit une vitesse moyenne de 44,38 km/h. Il devance le Néerlandais Hermans Cas (dossard 24), qui occupe la deuxième place, tandis que son compatriote Mohamed Nadib Assal (dossard 141) complète le podium en troisième position. Avec cette nouvelle victoire, Hamza Yacine porte à trois son nombre de succès d’étape depuis le début de cette 37e édition du Tour du Faso. Une performance qui confirme son statut de l’un des hommes forts de cette compétition. Le classement de cette étape confirme ainsi la présence en force des coureurs algériens, qui s’offrent deux des trois places sur le podium à l’arrivée à Léo. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Tour du Faso 2026: Hamza Yacine s’offre une troisième victoire d’étape est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Midterms : Trump empêtré
items.description: Le Parti démocrate a remporté une victoire écrasante à l’occasion des élections de mi-mandat (midterms) qui se sont tenues ce mardi 3 novembre aux États-Unis. Ces élections sont particulièrement importantes, puisque les États-uniens renouvellent simultanément la Chambre des représentants (435 membres), une partie Sénat (100 membres au total), ainsi que les gouverneurs de leurs États (50 au total). On parle d’une véritable « vague bleue » qui déferle sur les États-Unis, symbole du mécontentement d'une partie de la population vis-à-vis de la politique de l’administration Trump, et particulièrement les conséquences économiques la guerre en Iran. La course électorale dans le Michigan a été particulièrement médiatisée. La victoire du candidat démocrate Abdul El-Sayed, premier sénateur musulman élu aux États-Unis, démontre que critiquer la politique d'Israël n’est plus un tabou. Plusieurs États historiquement républicains, comme le Texas ou le Kansas, ont également élu des sénateurs démocrates, pour la première fois depuis des décennies. Au-delà du signal symbolique que représente ce rejet de la politique de Trump, l'enjeu est aussi institutionnel : le Congrès demeure un contre-pouvoir fondamental à l’exécutif états-unien. Mais peut-on s’attendre à ce que cette vague bleue impacte réellement la politique extérieure états-unienne ? L’article Midterms : Trump empêtré est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Farmers fight Lands Commission, Newmont for delayed compensation over Ahafo North Mines Project
items.description: The Concerned Farmers Association of Afrispakrom, Terchire, Susuanso, and Adrobaa in the Tano North Municipality of the Ahafo region has called on the Land Valuation Division of the Lands Commission to immediately pay all outstanding compensation for lands, crops, and farm structures acquired for Newmont Ghana Gold Ltd’s Ahafo North mining project. Addressing a news conference in Terchire on Monday, the Association rejected claims by Newmont classifying farm structures in the area as “speculative” to halt compensation under Executive Instrument (E.I.) 273 of 2024. The group also raised urgent concerns over the ongoing plight of members affected by an earlier compulsory acquisition under E.I. 356 of 2023, who remain unpaid three years after state authorities took possession of their lands and destroyed their properties. The core of the dispute centers on the legal framework used to acquire the land and evaluate affected properties. In June 2026, the Lands Commission notified the Association that Newmont had submitted a petition alleging that structures belonging to 21 farmers should be denied compensation, relying on a 2017 cut-off date under the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). The Association maintains that Newmont’s petition relies on an inapplicable legal framework because state authorities abandoned negotiations under mining laws and instead compulsorily acquired the lands under the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036). Under Act 1036, improvements to land are deemed speculative only if erected after the formal publication of the State’s notice of acquisition, with no statutory reference to mining regulation cut-off dates. Furthermore, all contested structures were physically inspected, counted, and verified during a 2024 joint exercise supervised by a Ministerial Committee, with valuation records formally signed by representatives of the Land Valuation Division, affected farmers, and Newmont. Following this verification, the Valuation Technical Committee of the Lands Commission approved compensation figures on April 13, 2026, which the farmers’ legal team accepted on April 24, 2026. In addition to the delayed payments under E.I. 273 of 2024, the Association highlighted the complete non-payment of claims under E.I. 356 of 2023, issued on September 29, 2023. State authorities took possession of those lands in December 2023 and destroyed the properties of the affected farmers, leaving them without compensation or alternative livelihoods for nearly three years. “Newmont is the beneficiary of the acquisition. It is not the State. It must not take over the Lands Commission’s responsibility to determine, assess and pay compensation according to law. The Commission must exercise its own judgment, apply the law fairly and protect the rights of affected property owners”, John Mensah, Chairman of the farmers, stated. Joseph Adu Yaw, Secretary of the farmers’ Association, stressed that the farms were their only source of livelihood and that taking them away without paying compensation has left their families in hardship, adding that some of our members have died and some are very ill while waiting for payment. “The Commission must give us a clear written explanation of any outstanding issues and a definite timetable for payment,” he indicated. The Association is urging the Lands Commission to reject Newmont’s petition, execute its statutory duties independently, immediately disburse the approved compensation under E.I. 273, expedite outstanding payments for E.I. 356 victims, and issue a written schedule with a definite timetable for full settlement. JoyNews reached out to the management of Newmont for their response on the various issues raised. It declined to comment.

items.title: Voter Register: INEC to purge 1.5 million irregular registrants
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the Commission’s headquarters. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS), Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the Commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, are part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. The INEC chairman said the Commission has registered approximately 103 million voters. Young Nigerians aged 18 to 34 make up nearly 29 per cent of them. He added that the distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) is ongoing across the country. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) for public access to polling-unit results. The Commission is also planning a mock accreditation and election exercise to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of artificial intelligence and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. He therefore asked the UN for stronger collaboration on information integrity, countering electoral disinformation and public awareness. Other areas of prospective cooperation he outlined include conflict prevention, election security, early-warning mechanisms, stakeholder dialogue and peacebuilding. He also listed the protection of vulnerable groups, particularly women, youths and persons with disabilities. On security, Amupitan said INEC is working with relevant agencies to map areas vulnerable to electoral violence and other threats, so that preventive measures can be developed. Simão said the visit was meant to show UN support for INEC, noting that the Commission carries a significant responsibility in managing elections in a country confronted by terrorism and other security challenges. According to him, the UN will maintain a presence during the elections, not as observers since it has no mandate for election observation, but to encourage positive conduct and support an atmosphere conducive to peaceful participation. Simão said elections should not become another source of violence or instability for Nigeria, but should promote peace, democratic stability and national development. He added that peaceful and successful elections in Nigeria would carry implications beyond its borders, serving as an inspiration to other West African countries and contributing to regional stability and integration. “We are here, pleased to give you moral support, that you are not alone in facing this mammoth task,” he said. items.title: SEND Ghana warns unhealthy diets could raise a generation of diabetics, calls for mandatory food labels
items.description: SEND Ghana has warned that the growing consumption of ultra-processed foods among children could increase the country’s future burden of diabetes, hypertension and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs). The organisation says Ghana needs to introduce mandatory Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling (FOPWL) to help consumers identify foods high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats and make healthier choices. Project Officer at SEND Ghana, Baaba Sam, said many Ghanaians struggled to understand existing nutritional information on food products, leaving them unable to make informed decisions about what they consumed. Speaking at a workshop on Nutrient Profile Modelling (NPM), Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling and Healthy Food Policies in Ghana, organised by Vision for Accelerated Sustainable Development Ghana (VAST Ghana) in collaboration with SEND Ghana and GAND, Ms Sam explained that although Ghana had regulations requiring nutritional information on food products, the existing system had significant weaknesses, particularly regarding the visibility and understanding of the information. She said consumers could find nutritional information tables at the back of food packages, but many either ignored them or did not understand what the figures and technical terms meant. “Ghana has a regulation for food labelling, actually. So, when you take any product, and then you look at the back of the label, you see that there’s a nutrition content table over there,” she said. “But the issue with it is that it’s actually not compulsory, so people cannot decide whether or not they want to put it there. The other part is that consumers do not understand. So the ordinary Ghanaian does not understand, and we don’t even pay attention to it at all.” According to her, the information contains important details about the amount of sugar, fat and salt in products, among other ingredients, but its location and technical presentation make it less useful to ordinary consumers. She said the proposed Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling policy would address these challenges by making warning labels compulsory and easier to understand. Ms Sam said that the word ‘mandatory’ was important because food manufacturers would no longer have the option of deciding whether or not to display the warning labels. “So, it means that industry or individual food manufacturers do not pick and choose whether they want their labels to be there or not. The other part is that it is very easy for the average Ghanaian to understand,” she explained. She said the proposed labels would combine symbols and written warnings to ensure that even consumers with limited literacy could identify products containing excessive amounts of unhealthy ingredients. “The front-of-pack warning policy, or the FOPL, has two sides. One, it would have a symbol, and it would also have writing so that if the person, the consumer, is not educated, at least when you see the symbol, it gives you an idea of what the label is trying to warn you about,” she said. Ms Sam also raised concerns about the use of very small print on food packaging, saying it made it difficult for consumers to read and understand nutritional information. She argued that information intended to guide purchasing decisions served little purpose if consumers could not easily see or interpret it. She said the proposed front-of-pack labelling system would make warnings more visible, with bold and legible information that consumers could understand at a glance. “If it is small, then why is it there in the first place if people cannot read it?” she questioned. She also expressed concern about parents’ growing preference for packaged snacks and ultra-processed foods when choosing what their children eat. She said convenience often influenced parents’ decisions, with biscuits, sweets and sugary drinks becoming more common choices than fruits and vegetables. Ms Sam warned that introducing children to unhealthy food habits at an early age could have serious consequences for their health later in life. “It’s a huge problem. Parents, when we are deciding the kind of snacks to give our children, fruits don’t come to mind, or vegetables don’t come to mind. But the first thing we go for, actually, parents buy it in packs and put it down because it’s easy, it’s accessible, and all that,” she said. She cautioned that such habits could contribute to a generation facing a higher risk of diabetes and hypertension. “Forgetting that we are raising future diabetics and future hypertensives,” she said. Ms Sam said that diabetes, traditionally regarded by many as a condition associated mainly with older people, was increasingly being diagnosed among children. She referred to presentations at the workshop which highlighted cases of Type 2 diabetes among children, warning that the trend should concern parents and policymakers. “Now we are diagnosing children who are not Type 1 diabetics, but they are Type 2 diabetics. So, which means that gradually, because of the food we are giving them, we used to think that diabetes is a disease of the old. But right now, the terrain is changing, and it is becoming a problem,” she said. Ms Sam further warned that the rising prevalence of diet-related diseases could place additional pressure on government spending on healthcare. She said that a country’s economic development depended heavily on the health of its population and that allowing preventable illnesses to increase would have long-term financial consequences. “One of the things government should pay attention to is that the health of its people is what drives the economy,” she said. She explained that conditions such as diabetes and hypertension often require long-term treatment and management, placing a sustained burden on individuals, families and the healthcare system. According to her, government could end up spending increasing amounts of money managing chronic illnesses that could have been prevented or reduced through healthier diets and effective public health policies. “And so, if you now have to spend a lot of money, like government is doing now, to take care of your population, it’s a chronic disease that is not going. And so it’s like just managing the person to live,” she said. She added that an increase in the number of people living with diet-related conditions would require government to allocate more resources to healthcare, raising questions about the sustainability of public spending. Ms Sam also attributed the growing preference for unhealthy foods to the high levels of sugar, salt and fats used in many ultra-processed products. She said these ingredients could make such foods highly appealing, encouraging repeated consumption even when people were no longer hungry. Using everyday experiences to illustrate the problem, she said children often preferred sweets, biscuits and sugary drinks to proper meals, forcing parents to struggle to get them to eat healthier foods. She added that unhealthy eating habits were not limited to children, as adults also developed cravings for certain processed foods. “Sometimes you open the fridge. You are done eating. You know you are very full. If they give you another food, you know it. But the next thing you say is that they are there, and you wonder, I’m full, so why do I need this?” she said. “Some of the sugar, fats, and salts that they add to these ultra-processed foods are very, very addictive, and they give us a palatable tongue. And so you keep going in for it again and again and again. So it never satisfies you,” she added.

items.title: FG, Lagos seek stronger partnership on data protection
items.description: By Juliet Umeh The Federal Government and Lagos State have called for stronger collaboration among regulators, businesses and other stakeholders to safeguard personal information and build public trust in the digital economy. The call was made at the ongoing Data Protection Africa Summit in Lagos, organised by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). The NDPC National Commissioner, Dr Vincent Olatunji, said collaboration was essential given Nigeria’s population, the scale of business activities and the growing volume of personal data being processed. “It would be absolutely impossible for us to be able to do that without the support of our partners,” he said. Olatunji said the commission was working with organisations to ensure they understood their responsibilities as data controllers and processors. “There is no escape from it. Organisations must be accountable for how they handle personal information. “It has to be treated as a two-way thing,” he said, describing data protection as a shared responsibility between regulators and organisations that collect or process personal information. He said greater public awareness, capacity building and knowledge sharing were necessary to strengthen Nigeria’s data protection ecosystem. “Privacy and data protection are still new to a lot of people,” he said, adding that citizens needed to understand their rights and responsibilities. The NDPC chief also urged African countries to learn from one another, stressing the importance of knowledge exchange in addressing emerging data protection challenges. “Nobody knows it all. When we think we want to learn from others, that is how we learn from each other,” he said. Representing Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Lagos State Special Adviser on Technology, Innovation and Broadband, Engr Ganiyu Oseni, said data protection was central to building public trust in government institutions and digital services. “Every time a citizen provides personal information to access a government service, that citizen places confidence in the institution receiving it. We have a responsibility to justify that confidence,” he said. Oseni said Lagos State’s deployment of technology to improve public services, including residence and land registration, made it imperative for public institutions to protect information entrusted to them. “When properly implemented, it strengthens public confidence, supports responsible innovation and creates a more secure environment for investment and economic activities,” he said. Also speaking, the Executive Director of Africa Digital Rights’ Hub (ADRH), Ms Teki Akuetteh, called on African regulators to strengthen cooperation to facilitate cross-border business transactions and data transfers. She identified differences in data protection laws and their implementation across African countries as challenges to seamless cross-border data flows. “Across Africa, there is still that challenge of harmonisation of data protection laws,” she said, noting that differences between Nigerian and Ghanaian laws could affect the transfer of information and money. “Even when you have the same laws, there are different individuals and regulators that sit to implement them. One person’s interpretation may differ,” she added. Akuetteh said strategic partnerships would help build trust among regulators and promote common approaches to cross-border data transfers. “That is why it is very important to have these strategic partnerships as a way of bringing people together, building trust among regulators and agreeing on a simple way to facilitate cross-border data flows. “Everybody deserves the right to have their information protected,” she said. In his remarks, Oba Olufolarin Ogunsanwo, Tẹlade IV, urged traditional institutions and universities to promote privacy awareness in communities and on campuses. He described personal data as a valuable asset that required careful and accountable handling, urging stakeholders to take awareness campaigns to the grassroots and communicate them in local languages. “Personal data is a valuable asset that must be handled with the utmost care, integrity and accountability,” he said. “Digital privacy awareness must become a grassroots movement,” the traditional ruler added. items.title: Savanes/Lutte contre les VBG : Deux maisons de transit inaugurées à Dapaong
items.description: Dapaong, 4 nov. (ATOP) – Deux maisons de transit destinées à l’accueil et à la protection des victimes de Violences basées sur le genre (VBG), un bloc administratif et un forage ont été inaugurés le mardi 3 novembre à Dapaong. Ces infrastructures sont réalisées par le Réseau des femmes et développement (REFED), avec l’appui de l’association allemande TogoVerein, le Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD), le Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA) et la Communauté économique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO). Elles visent à renforcer la prise en charge et la protection des femmes et des filles victimes de violences dans la région des Savanes. Les deux maisons de transit offriront un cadre sécurisé aux survivantes de violences physiques, psychologiques, économiques et sexuelles. Elles permettront de leur assurer une prise en charge globale comprenant l’écoute, l’accompagnement psychosocial, l’orientation vers les services médicaux et juridiques ainsi que l’appui à leur réinsertion. Le ministre des Solidarités, du Genre, de la Famille et de la Protection de l’enfance, Mme Sankaredja-Sinandja Moni a salué la réalisation de ces infrastructures qui constituent, selon elle, un espace de protection, de réconfort et de reconstruction pour les femmes et les filles confrontées aux violences. Elle a invité les victimes à briser le silence et à solliciter de l’aide afin de préserver leurs dignités et droits. Mme Sankaredja a rappelé que c’est dans cette dynamique que le ministère des Solidarités a renforcé les dispositions nationales de prévention et de protection à travers les centres d’écoute « One stop centers », les mécanismes communautaires de veille et l’élaboration du protocole national de prise en charge holistique des victimes de VBG. Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh a félicité le REFED pour son engagement en faveur de la promotion des droits des femmes et de la lutte contre les VBG. Il a souligné l’importance des réalisations dans la mise en œuvre des engagements du Togo en matière de protection des femmes. La coordinatrice du REFED, Mme Kabissa-Lamboni Confort, a indiqué que l’inauguration s’inscrit dans le cadre du lancement des 16 jours d’activisme contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux filles. Elle a appelé à une mobilisation concertée des services sociaux, des forces de sécurité, de la justice ainsi que des leaders traditionnels et religieux pour prévenir et combattre durablement les VBG. Le REFED a été créé le 3 avril 2004 avec 26 associations. Il regroupe aujourd’hui plus de 500 associations et coopératives à travers le Togo. Les représentants des partenaires, des sénateurs et députés, les préfets et maires de la région, ainsi que des autorités administratives, militaires, traditionnelles et religieuses ont pris part à la cérémonie. ATOP/JK/BA

items.title: Subventions : « les députés devraient payer le pain à 50 dinars »
items.description: La lancinante question de la réforme de la politique des subventions en Algérie est revenue, une fois encore, à l’hémicycle de l’APN. La proposition a été portée, cette fois-ci, par la voix du député Fares Rahmani, qui a proposé d’orienter les subventions au profit des classes fragiles de la société. « Pour préserver l’argent public, nous plaidons pour des subventions ciblées. Il est injuste que tout le monde bénéficie de ces subventions. Par exemple, nous, en tant que députés, nous avons de bons salaires, nous ne devrions pas profiter des subventions. Quand on achète le pain, on ne devrait pas le payer 10 dinars, mais 40 ou 50 dinars », a proposé le député du Front El Moustakbel qui représente la communauté algérienne en Europe du Nord. « Il faut orienter les subventions au profit de ceux qui ont un pouvoir d’achat très faible. Il y a des citoyens qui ont 3 ou 4 enfants et qui touchent un salaire de 20.000 dinars. Ceux qui touchent un salaire mensuel de 100.000 et plus ne devraient pas bénéficier de ces subventions », a-t-il plaidé, mardi, lors des débats sur le projet de loi de finances de 2027 . Algérie : 18 milliards de dollars de subventions pour 2027 Ce dernier prévoit un budget de 2.414,15 milliards de dinars (18 milliards de dollars) pour les subventions en 2027. « Le projet de loi de finances 2027 accorde une importance centrale à la préservation du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens et à l’amélioration de leurs conditions de vie, en poursuivant le soutien aux transferts sociaux, dont les crédits atteignent 2.414,15 milliards DA, dont 717,7 milliards destinés à soutenir et à stabiliser les prix des produits de base de grande consommation. » La réforme de la politique de subventions des prix des produits alimentaires a été abordée par plusieurs économistes et hommes politiques en Algérie, et ce, depuis plusieurs années. Les gouvernements successifs ont souvent justifié le maintien de son caractère universel par l’absence de bases de données fiables sur les revenus des ménages. La loi de finances de 2022 a prévu le recours à des subventions ciblées, à travers la mise en place d’un « mécanisme de compensation monétaire » au profit des ménages. La mise en œuvre de ce dispositif a été ensuite reportée. Le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune a déclaré en février 2026, lors de sa rencontre périodique avec la presse, que « si on prive 20 familles de leurs droits en les classant là où elles ne devraient pas être, c’est remettre en cause la politique sociale de l’État ». L’État algérien subventionne les prix de plusieurs produits alimentaires, dont le pain, l’huile, le sucre et le café. L’article Subventions : « les députés devraient payer le pain à 50 dinars » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Lions de l’Atlas : Ayoub Oufkir, le nouveau talent appelé par Mohamed Ouahbi
items.description: À seulement 20 ans, Ayoub Oufkir franchit une nouvelle étape dans sa jeune carrière. Retenu pour la première fois avec l’équipe nationale A du Maroc par Mohamed Ouahbi, l’attaquant de l’AZ Alkmaar fait partie des nouvelles options offensives des Lions de l’Atlas pour la double confrontation face au Niger, les 13 et 17 novembre, dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Qui est Ayoub Oufkir? Né le 4 janvier 2006 à Rotterdam, Ayoub Oufkir a grandi et été formé aux Pays-Bas. Il rejoint les rangs du Sparta Rotterdam en 2013, à l’âge de sept ans, et y effectue l’essentiel de sa formation. Après avoir évolué dans les différentes catégories de jeunes, il intègre progressivement le groupe professionnel et signe son premier contrat en août 2024. Ses débuts en Eredivisie interviennent le 17 août 2024, face au FC Twente. Une première apparition remarquée puisqu’il délivre une passe décisive dès son entrée en scène. Il poursuit ensuite sa progression avec le club de Rotterdam, disputant 24 rencontres officielles et inscrivant quatre buts, pour quatre passes décisives. De Sparta Rotterdam à l’AZ Alkmaar En décembre 2025, l’AZ Alkmaar officialise son recrutement. Le jeune ailier s’engage jusqu’en juin 2030, avec une année supplémentaire en option, et rejoint la formation d’Alkmaar à partir de janvier 2026. Un transfert qui confirme l’intérêt suscité par son potentiel et lui permet de franchir un nouveau palier dans sa carrière. À l’AZ, Oufkir évolue principalement au poste d’ailier droit, même s’il peut également occuper le côté gauche. Gaucher, il se distingue notamment par sa vitesse, sa qualité de dribble et sa capacité à provoquer dans les un-contre-un. Un profil offensif qui lui permet d’apporter de la percussion et de la créativité sur les côtés. Au cours de la saison 2026-2027, le Marocain commence à trouver sa place dans l’effectif professionnel. Il a déjà inscrit deux buts en championnat avec l’AZ, selon les statistiques arrêtées à la fin du mois d’octobre. Il poursuit également son apprentissage avec les sélections de jeunes du club et les équipes néerlandaises. Un champion d’Europe avec les Pays-Bas Avant de recevoir sa première convocation avec le Maroc, Ayoub Oufkir s’était déjà illustré sous le maillot des sélections néerlandaises. Son premier grand fait d’armes remonte à juin 2025, lorsqu’il remporte le championnat d’Europe U19 avec les Pays-Bas. Titulaire lors de la finale remportée face à l’Espagne (1-0), il contribue au premier sacre européen de cette catégorie pour la sélection néerlandaise. Durant cette compétition disputée en Roumanie, il s’était notamment illustré en inscrivant un doublé face à l’Allemagne lors de la phase de groupes. Il avait également délivré une passe décisive en demi-finale contre le pays hôte. Ses performances lui ouvrent ensuite les portes des Espoirs néerlandais. Il se distingue notamment lors de la rencontre face à la Belgique, le 30 mars 2026, remportée par les Pays-Bas sur le score de 2-1, en inscrivant le deuxième but de son équipe. Son parcours avec les sélections néerlandaises n’a toutefois pas empêché son arrivée dans le groupe marocain. Sa première convocation avec les Lions de l’Atlas marque une étape importante dans son parcours international et témoigne de la volonté de Mohamed Ouahbi d’élargir ses options offensives. En faisant appel à Ayoub Oufkir, le sélectionneur marocain mise sur un joueur jeune, capable d’apporter de la vitesse, de la percussion et de nouvelles solutions dans les couloirs. Cette convocation s’inscrit également dans la volonté de Ouahbi de donner leur chance à des profils prometteurs, tout en préparant progressivement l’avenir de la sélection. The post Lions de l’Atlas : Ayoub Oufkir, le nouveau talent appelé par Mohamed Ouahbi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Executive accountability for results
items.description: Insight Organizational performance improves when executive leaders take clear ownership of results. Accountability must go beyond attending meetings, submitting reports, and completing assigned activities. It requires executives to accept responsibility for outcomes, explain performance gaps, and take corrective action. The CEO sets the standard by ensuring that responsibilities are clearly defined, expectations are understood, and performance is reviewed consistently. A high-performing executive team does not shift blame when targets are missed. It accepts responsibility, identifies solutions, and acts. Key Strategies: Establish clear performance expectations for every executive. Connect executive responsibilities to measurable organizational outcomes. Introduce consistent performance review and reporting arrangements. Encourage transparency when targets are missed, or risks emerge. Recognize strong performance and address persistent underperformance. CEO Leadership Actions. Ensure every executive understands their individual and collective performance responsibilities. Challenge explanations that lack evidence or practical corrective measures. Build a culture where commitments are taken seriously, and results are openly discussed. Actionable Tip At your next executive meeting, ask: “Which organizational result are you personally accountable for delivering, and what evidence will demonstrate that you have achieved it?” Why This Matters? Accountability strengthens trust, execution, and organizational discipline. When executives understand that leadership responsibility is measured by outcomes, they become more focused on delivering value rather than simply reporting activity. About the Author Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and serves on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: 5th Head of State Invitational Golf Tournament set for Saturday, November 21 in Accra
items.description: The fifth edition of the Head of State Invitational Golf Tournament is scheduled to be staged in Accra later this month. 140 amateur golfers, including international participants from Nigeria, Burundi and Kenya will compete in the event slated for Saturday, November 21, 2026, at the Achimota Golf Club in Accra. The tournament is held in honour of President John Dramani Mahama under the theme “Driving National Growth Through Leadership, Partnership and Golf.” The launch brought together distinguished sponsors, partners, club leadership and members of the media. Speaking at the launch of the event on Wednesday, November 4, the coordinator for the tournament, Francis Andoh, stressed that the event transcends the sport itself. “Our commitment extends beyond the course. “Through the Head of State Foundation, we seek to support community outreach and create opportunities for young people through golf. We invite our partners and participants to help turn this commitment into meaningful support for those who need it,” he said. The tournament is headlined by First National Bank, with BOST Energies as the Gold sponsor. Other valued sponsors include Samsung Ghana, The Luckiest, Myla Homes, National Petroleum Authority, Danny List Foundation, Aphro Ghana, Coca-Cola Ghana, Guinness Ghana, Pasonia, La Villa Aphro, Happy Box, TGTS, Ember Coco, Sunlodge, JD’s Fresh Juice, The Palms by Eagles, Gevans Natural Minerals Water and Nguvu Mining Limited. Speaking at the launch, Mike Aggrey, a member of the Board of Trustees of Achimota Golf Club and General Secretary of the African Golf Confederation, provided insights into the tournament’s history and impact. “The idea being that it will meet away from the bureaucracy of the ministries and the Jubilee House to a place such as a golf course where you can have a rapport without all the difficulties associated with the office environment,” he said. Reflecting on the impact of past editions, Aggrey recalled the 2018 event in Kumasi, which was attended by about 16 ministers of state and numerous industry leaders. “During that event, a lot of deals were struck because people were able to meet directly with ministers of state and put projects together and make proposals directly without going through secretariats,” he added.

items.title: Droits de la défense : Les motifs des convocations judiciaires désormais exigés !
items.description: Le ministre de la Justice, Me Moussa Sarr, demande aux services de police judiciaire de préciser systématiquement les motifs des convocations adressées aux personnes appelées à être entendues. Dans une circulaire datée du 3 novembre 2026, il invite les procureurs généraux près les cours d’appel à mettre fin à l’utilisation de la formule « affaire vous concernant ». Le garde des Sceaux relève que certaines unités de police et de gendarmerie, ainsi que d’autres services investis de missions de police judiciaire, se limitent à cette mention sans indiquer les raisons pour lesquelles l’intéressé est appelé à se présenter. Une pratique qui, selon lui, est contraire à la loyauté devant gouverner la conduite de la procédure et porte atteinte à la protection des droits de la défense. À cet égard, Me Moussa Sarr rappelle les garanties consacrées par l’article 9 de la Constitution et l’article 7 de la Charte africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples. Il souligne que leur effectivité suppose que la personne convoquée soit suffisamment informée de l’objet de son audition pour préparer ses éléments de défense, rassembler les pièces utiles et, si elle le souhaite, solliciter l’assistance d’un conseil. En conséquence, le ministre instruit les procureurs généraux de veiller à ce que les officiers et agents de police judiciaire mentionnent expressément, dans chaque convocation, la nature de l’affaire, l’infraction ou les faits sur lesquels la personne sera entendue. Lorsque la convocation est destinée à un témoin ou à une victime, cette qualité devra également être précisée. Le ministre de la Justice précise toutefois que cette exigence ne remet pas en cause le secret de l’enquête. Elle ne vise pas à révéler les éléments recueillis ou les indices, mais à fournir les informations strictement nécessaires à la préparation de la défense et au bon déroulement d’une éventuelle audition. La circulaire demande enfin aux procureurs généraux de veiller à son application stricte et de rendre compte de toute difficulté rencontrée. Salla GUEYE

items.title: Premier Nursing College seeks government support to expand campus, introduce degree programmes
items.description: Premier Nursing and Midwifery Training College has appealed to the government, traditional authorities and other stakeholders for financial and institutional support to expand its operations and enhance the training of nurses and midwives in Ghana. The private institution says support for the development of its new campus at Adadientem in the Ashanti Region is crucial to its plans to expand its facilities and introduce degree programmes in nursing. The principal of the college, Afia Serwaa Yegbe, made the appeal at the launch of the institution’s 25th Anniversary Homecoming and Graduation Celebration, held under the theme, “25 Years of Impactful Nursing and Midwifery Education.” Mrs Yegbe said the college was seeking adequate funding to develop the new campus and broaden its academic programmes to meet the changing demands of nursing and midwifery education. “We need funds; we have a new site at Adadientem where we want to get enough money to work on that so that we can expand our horizons. We want to start the degree nursing; if we stay with diploma, you will be left behind,” she pleaded. The anniversary launch brought together alumni, traditional leaders, academics and other stakeholders to celebrate the institution’s contribution to nursing and midwifery education over the past 25 years, while exploring ways to strengthen its future. Addressing concerns about private nursing education, students were encouraged to remain committed to their studies and disregard perceptions that private nursing institutions offer inferior training. They were reminded that several prominent health professionals serving in Ghana and abroad had received their training at the college. They were urged to pursue academic excellence and professional competence to earn recognition in the health sector. Registrar of the college, Nana Osei Kwadwo, allayed fears of unemployment associated with attending a private nursing institution, stressing that the college provides the requisite training for professional practice. “Impactful nursing and midwifery education is not without a challenge. We’re facing a lot of challenges; one of them is that, when you attend a private school, you won’t get employment. It’s the government that employs people; the Premier has what it takes to employ people,” he noted. On the financial difficulties confronting students, Nana Osei Kwadwo said many were struggling to pay their fees, as government allowances were insufficient to cover their educational expenses. He has therefore called on stakeholders to support students financially to support the successful completion of their academic endeavours. The college’s 25th anniversary highlights its contributions to nursing and midwifery education while renewing calls for partnerships and support to strengthen healthcare training and improve access to quality healthcare in Ghana. Chief of Nkwantakese in the Afigya Kwabre North District, Nana Boakye Yam Ababio, a former lecturer at the college, called on traditional authorities to support private nursing and midwifery training institutions. “If we have the means, people in our communities should be sponsored to be trained so that they will also come back to the communities to give back because we have the chips compound and we need the nurses, and so as traditional leaders, we can do something to help the training institutions so that Ghana will live up to expectations,” he pleaded.

items.title: Tennis great Rafael Nadal set to join Real Madrid board
items.description: Real Madrid are set to add a champion from another ⁠sporting arena to ⁠their boardroom as 22-time tennis Grand Slam winner Rafael Nadal’s appointment as a director is to be put to members for ⁠ratification, the club says. The board agreed to submit the appointment to the General Assembly of ⁠Delegated Members. Nadal is already an honorary member of the club. “It is a source of immense pride for Real Madrid and for all our supporters that a figure of his sporting and personal stature … is to join ‌our Board of Directors,” Real said in a statement on Wednesday. Tennis player Rafael Nadal and Real Madrid President Florentino Perez in the stands [Isabel Infantes/Reuters] The club highlighted Nadal’s sporting achievements, including 92 singles titles, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup triumphs with Spain and the world number one ranking. The club said his qualities beyond those honours – including humility, respect for opponents and commitment to charity – mirrored the club’s own. “All ⁠these values form part of Real Madrid’s identity, and ⁠Rafael Nadal has embodied and championed them throughout his sporting career,” said the statement announcing his appointment at a board meeting on Tuesday. Nadal welcomed the invitation. “I would like to thank President Florentino Perez and the Board for ⁠inviting me to join the Board of Directors of Real Madrid,” he wrote on social media. “I have ⁠accepted this invitation with great enthusiasm, keen to ⁠learn and to contribute as much as I can.” Nadal, who retired from tennis in November 2024, has long been touted as a potential successor to Perez, ‌although he has played down the prospect. Perez, 79, secured another four-year term in June after Real’s first contested presidential election in two decades.

items.title: Imperial General Assurance supports infrastructure upgrade at Ghana National Fire Service in Sekondi-Takoradi
items.description: Imperial General Assurance has donated bags of cement to the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) in the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis to support the Service’s ongoing infrastructure projects. The donation was made during a working visit led by the company’s Managing Director, Mr Harry Ofori-Attah, accompanied by the Regional Sales Manager and the Takoradi Branch team. The delegation was received at the Service’s Regional Headquarters by the Sekondi-Takoradi Metro Divisional Officer, Mr Michael Tetteh, and senior officers. The gesture forms part of the insurer’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) agenda, which seeks to support key public institutions and contribute to community welfare within its operational areas. Speaking at the presentation, Mr Ofori-Attah commended the Fire Service for its dedication, professionalism and bravery in protecting lives and property. He noted that the Service’s mandate closely aligns with the company’s core business of risk protection, stressing the importance of supporting institutions that play a critical role in public safety. “Our work as insurers is to provide financial protection after a loss, but your work is to prevent the loss and save lives in the first place. This donation is our small way of saying thank you and supporting you to improve your working environment,” he said. He added that the company recognises the vital role of firefighters in safeguarding communities and is pleased to contribute to efforts to improve their working environment. For his part, Mr Tetteh expressed gratitude for the donation, describing it as a welcome contribution to the Service’s infrastructure development efforts. He assured the delegation that the cement would be used judiciously for its intended purpose and called for stronger collaboration between the two institutions.

items.title: Yoto/Passation de service :M. Ahé Kokouvi Dodji prend les commandes de la préfecture
items.description: Tabligbo, 4 nov. (ATOP) – Nommé le 22 octobre dernier par décret présidentiel, M. Ahé Kokouvi Dodji a officiellement pris les rênes de la préfecture de Yoto, le mardi 3 novembre à Tabligbo. Il succède ainsi au Lt. Col Djossou Agossa, appelé à faire valoir ses compétences à la tête de la préfecture de l’Avé. Placée sous la présidence du gouverneur de la région Maritime, Bagbiègue Tairou, représentant le ministre de tutelle, la cérémonie de passation de charge a été marquée par les discours de circonstance, suivis de la signature et de l’échange de documents administratifs entre le gouverneur, le préfet sortant et le nouveau préfet. Le gouverneur a placé cette passation sous le signe de la continuité de l’action administrative au service du développement, de la paix sociale et du bien-être des populations. Il a rendu hommage au Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé avant d’exprimer sa gratitude au préfet sortant, Lt. Col Djossou Agossa, pour son courage et son engagement patriotique à la tête de la préfecture. Au préfet entrant, il a adressé ses félicitations, soulignant que sa nomination constitue une reconnaissance de son expérience et de ses compétences. Il lui a rappelé les tâches qui lui incombent notamment, la coordination des services déconcentrés de l’Etat, le contrôle de l’égalité des actes des communes et le maintien de la cohésion sociale. Le gouverneur a également insisté sur les valeurs de rigueur, d’impartialité, de loyauté et de collaboration avec les acteurs locaux. Il a invité la population de Yoto à réserver un accueil bienveillant au nouveau préfet et à lui apporter leur franche collaboration pour la réussite de sa mission au service du développement de la préfecture. Le préfet Ahé a exprimé sa gratitude au Président du Conseil pour la confiance placée en sa personne pour poursuivre la mise en œuvre des projets et programmes de développement dans la préfecture. Il a félicité le préfet sortant pour le travail abattu à la tête de la préfecture. M. Ahé a réaffirmé sa disponibilité à servir la préfecture avec détermination, précisant que son action reposera sur l’écoute, l’impartialité la diligence et l’efficacité. Il a appelé toutes les forces vives à unir leurs efforts pour relever les défis auxquels fait face la préfecture de Yoto. Le Lt. Col Djossou Agossa, préfet sortant a remercié toute la population pour la franche collaboration depuis son arrivée. Il a souhaité plein succès à son successeur et l’a exhorté à poursuivre les actions et les chantiers déjà engagés au cours de son passage à la tête de la préfecture. Les députés Djissénou Kodjo et Viagbo Jerry, les maires et conseillers municipaux des trois communes du ressort territorial de la préfecture, des autorités administratives, traditionnelles, religieuses et civiles, des cadres de la localité ainsi que des responsables des forces de défense et de sécurité ont pris part à la cérémonie. ATOP/SAK/SED

items.title: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift 'seriously mistaken'
items.description: Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a shift in US policy was “seriously mistaken”, hours after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. “Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website. Democrats seized control of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, reflecting anger over living costs , tariffs and the US war against Iran , which has sent fuel prices soaring . Khamenei’s remarks come with diplomatic efforts underway to avert renewed fighting in the war, which broke out on February 28 . US and Israeli leaders have in recent days threatened to resume attacks against Iran. “Should such aggressions be repeated, the war’s scope will become much wider,” said Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since he took power in March. Earlier, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Americans had voted against war. “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X. “If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said. Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. “We will certainly inflict further defeats on him,” he added.

items.title: Uno de cada 10 hombres admite haber cometido algún tipo de abuso sexual contra menores en España: “Es un problema estructural”
items.description: Tres datos arrojan luz sobre un panorama oscuro, por lo que implica y por lo poco estudiado hasta ahora. El primero, que uno de cada 10 hombres en España admite haber llevado a cabo algún tipo de abuso sexual contra niños o adolescentes durante su vida adulta. El segundo, que un 2,8% afirma haberlo hecho contra algún menor de 15 años, es decir, por debajo de la edad de consentimiento legal. El tercero, que uno de cada cinco asegura haber sentido algún grado de atracción sexual hacia menores de 16 años desde que cumplió los 18. Son los principales resultados del estudio que este miércoles ha presentado en Madrid el Grupo de Investigación en Victimización Infantil y Adolescente de la Universidad de Barcelona. El primero de este tipo realizado en España, enfatizan los autores, que insisten en que su trabajo parte de una perspectiva de prevención. “Poner el foco del abuso sexual infantil únicamente en los menores no funciona”, explica Pablo Romero-Seseña, autor del informe. “Si no llegamos a comprender cuáles son los factores de riesgo, esos caminos que recorren las personas que sienten atracción, difícilmente vamos a ser capaces de implementar medidas de prevención efectivas”, apunta. Canadian Prime Minister commends Mahama for leadership in Ghana and global affairs
items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has commended President John Dramani Mahama for his leadership in driving reforms in Ghana and contributing to efforts to address pressing global challenges. Mr Carney made the remarks during an engagement with President Mahama on the sidelines of the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda. The meeting provided an opportunity for the two leaders to discuss issues of mutual interest, including developments in Ghana and the country’s contribution to international discussions on governance and global cooperation. Mr Carney’s commendation recognised President Mahama’s leadership at both the national and international levels, particularly his efforts to advance reforms and contribute to addressing challenges affecting the wider global community. “We just had your Foreign Minister in Canada, and we’re working towards an MOU on other aspects. You’ve helped to lead a reset, both domestically and within the system as a whole,” he said. The engagement formed part of President Mahama’s diplomatic activities at the Commonwealth summit, which brought together leaders from member countries to discuss shared priorities and strengthen cooperation. Meanwhile, President Mahama has called for a stronger partnership between Ghana and the United Kingdom following Britain’s acknowledgement of the atrocities committed during the Transatlantic Slave Trade and its openness to a formal apology and structured dialogue on reparatory justice. During a separate engagement with the UK Prime Minister, President Mahama described Britain’s position as an opportunity for affected countries and the UK to work together to address the painful legacy of slavery and colonialism. He said the changing dynamics of global affairs made it necessary for both countries to strengthen their relationship and pursue areas of mutual interest. President Mahama has consistently advocated international recognition of the historical injustices associated with the Transatlantic Slave Trade and meaningful discussions on reparatory justice.

items.title: NAIMOS, Navy immobilise illegal mining equipment on River Offin amid armed resistance
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), supported by personnel from the Ghana Navy Special Boat Squadron, has returned to the River Offin in the Central Region, immobilising equipment allegedly used for illegal mining and polluting the waterbody. The operation took place at Nipanekro in the Upper Denkyira West District, following an earlier attempt by NAIMOS to stop illegal mining activities along the river that was reportedly met with stiff resistance from Changfan operators. In a report by JoyNews’ Erastus Asare Donkor, the Navy personnel deployed an inflatable boat to cross the river and reach the opposite bank, where the mining equipment was located. The miners were seen abandoning their rafts and fleeing as the security personnel advanced towards their operations. The team subsequently pursued some of the operators into areas leading towards Manso Tontokrom and immobilised equipment found in and around the river. The operation reportedly encountered another challenge when a group of suspected illegal miners began mobilising from surrounding communities. According to the JoyNews report, drone footage showed a group gathering about two miles from the operation site, with some individuals allegedly carrying pump-action guns. The group was said to have threatened to confront the security personnel. NAIMOS reportedly maintained its position but exercised restraint and opted not to engage the group unless necessary. The gathering later dispersed without a confrontation. The latest operation follows an earlier attempt to clear illegal mining activities from the River Offin, which reportedly faced resistance from Changfan operators who challenged the security personnel to cross the river. NAIMOS Commander, Colonel S.K. Appiah, said the team intended to sustain its operations to rid the river of illegal mining activities. The operation forms part of efforts to curb illegal mining and protect water bodies from further pollution.

items.title: La Tunisie ambitionne de faire décoller son secteur aéronautique à l’horizon 2030
items.description: La filiere aeronautique tunisienne se porterait plutot bien, selon les declarations de Hatem Soussi, directeur central a l'Agence de promotion de l'investissement exterieur (FIPA). Il a souligne sur les ondes de la Radio nationale, le 3 novembre, les atouts de la Tunisie, pays strategiquement situe sur le plan geographique, disposant d'un tissu industriel interconnecte, d'un bon partenariat public-prive ainsi que d'un vivier de talents et d'ingenieurs qualifies. Les chiffres communiques par le ministere de l'economie et de la Planification lors de la la cinquieme edition des Aerospace Meetings Tunisia 2026 , qui s'etaient tenus du 7 au 9 juillet dernier, font etat de 85 entreprises etrangeres operant dans le secteur des composants aeronautiques, comptant un total de 20 000 employes directs. Le pays mise, selon Soussi, sur le developpement de la filiere en matiere de creation d'emplois, d'integration et de renforcement des exportations, a l'horizon 2030, pour un secteur resolument tourne vers les marches internationaux. Creer 10 000 emplois et hisser l'integration locale a plus de 50 % La FIPA viseraient l'objectif de 10 000 emplois directs supplementaires qui viendraient renforcer les effectifs existants d'ici a 2030. Elle voudrait aussi porter le taux d'integration a plus de 50 %, et ce, en donnant plus de poids a la participation des entreprises tunisiennes aux differentes etapes de la chaîne de valeur du secteur aeronautique. Un tel objectif suppose plus d'investissements dans les activites industrielles deja en place, mais aussi dans les autres capacites locales de production de composants, de services specialises et de sous-traitance, entre autres domaines connexes. Il faut cependant preciser que les objectifs restent a confirmer institutionnellement et ne doivent donc pas etre consideres comme des engagements officiels des autorites. Doubler les exportations Pour l'heure, il n'existe pas de chiffre clairement defini pour la valeur des exportations du secteur. Une communication de la FIPA datant du 6 octobre avance une valeur totale des exportations du secteur aeronautique tunisien a plus de 650 millions d'euros (plus de 728 millions de dollars), alors que les chiffres du site d'information local des Journalistes tunisiens a Sfax indiquent un montant de 1,74 milliard de dinars (soit plus de 580 millions de dollars) en 2025. Le second chiffre ne se base cependant pas sur des sources statistiques officielles et ne tient pas compte des memes parametres que ceux de la FIPA, mais il permet tout de meme d'offrir une fourchette, certes large mais interessante, pour estimer le potentiel de la croissance de la filiere. Le secteur affiche une croissance annuelle de 20,4 % en moyenne sur les quatre dernieres annees, avec une progression estimee a 12 % en 2026. Du cote des flux d'investissements etrangers, ils auraient augmente de 30 % sur un an. Si les donnees ne suffisent pas a elles seules a determiner les capacites de production qui seront reellement mises en place, ni leur rendement, elles sont neanmoins percues comme des signaux favorables qui laissent esperer un doublement de la valeur des exportations a l'horizon 2030. Bien qu'il soit presente comme un relais important de croissance economique nationale en Tunisie, le secteur aeronautique devra relever une multitude de defis pour concretiser ses visees d'integration industrielle locale, de creation d'emplois et de haute valeur ajoutee.

items.title: Mastercard renforce l’offre de paiement mobile au Maroc avec l’arrivée de Samsung Pay
items.description: Mastercard accompagne le lancement de Samsung Pay au Maroc, élargissant le choix des consommateurs grâce à des paiements mobiles sécurisés et pratiques. Avec la technologie de tokenisation de Mastercard, les titulaires de cartes Mastercard éligibles auprès des banques participantes peuvent utiliser des appareils Samsung compatibles pour effectuer leurs paiements, alliant la praticité du quotidien à une protection des paiements intégrée. Ce lancement s’inscrit dans la continuité du travail mené par Mastercard avec les institutions financières et les partenaires technologiques pour faire progresser l’écosystème des paiements numériques au Maroc. En rendant ses capacités compatibles à Samsung Pay, Mastercard offre aux consommateurs davantage de solutions de paiement et contribue à ancrer le paiement numérique dans leurs achats du quotidien. Samsung Pay s’appuie sur les capacités de tokenisation déjà déployées par Mastercard au Maroc. La technologie qui sous-tend ces paiements remplace les données sensibles de la carte par un jeton numérique unique, contribuant ainsi à protéger les identifiants de paiement lors des transactions. Les dispositifs d’authentification et de protection fondés sur l’analyse des risques offrent des niveaux de sécurité supplémentaires, permettant aux consommateurs de payer facilement et en toute confiance. Ce lancement reflète également l’ambition mondiale de Mastercard de tokeniser 100 % des transactions en ligne d’ici 2030. En collaboration avec l’ensemble des partenaires technologiques, Mastercard continue de rendre les paiements numériques à la fois plus sûrs et plus simples à utiliser. A ce propos, Mohamed Benomar, Country Manager pour l’Afrique du Nord-Ouest, Mastercard, a que « chez Mastercard, nous croyons en un avenir des paiements qui offre à chacun plus de choix, plus de simplicité et davantage de confiance à chaque transaction ». « Accompagner Samsung Pay au Maroc constitue une nouvelle étape importante pour élargir l’accès à des expériences de paiement numérique sécurisées, grâce à notre technologie de tokenisation : Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES). Au-delà de l’introduction d’un nouveau moyen de paiement, notre ambition est de rendre les paiements numériques plus rapides, plus simples et plus sûrs » , a-t-il ajouté. Pour les consommateurs, Samsung Pay permet de payer avec un appareil Samsung compatible, sans avoir besoin de carte physique pour les transactions prises en charge. Les institutions financières participantes peuvent proposer une expérience de paiement numérique supplémentaire à leurs titulaires de cartes éligibles, tandis que les commerçants équipés pour le paiement sans contact peuvent accepter cette nouvelle option de paiement. Ensemble, ces capacités élargissent le choix dans l’ensemble de l’écosystème des paiements. « Avec Samsung Pay, nous voulons que payer devienne aussi naturel qu’utiliser son smartphone ou sa montre connectée. Ce lancement marque une nouvelle étape dans notre engagement à offrir aux utilisateurs Galaxy des innovations simples, sécurisées et réellement utiles au quotidien. Nous tenons à remercier les banques participantes et Mastercard pour leur confiance et leur collaboration, et nous sommes fiers de contribuer à cette transformation digitale », a pour sa part relevé Hongseok Lee, Président de Samsung Electronics Maghreb Arab. Mastercard et Samsung déploieront également une campagne conjointe au Maroc pour accélérer l’adoption de Samsung Pay au quotidien. Elle associera des opérations promotionnelles à des actions de sensibilisation des consommateurs à la manière de payer simplement et en toute sécurité avec des appareils Samsung compatibles. Cette initiative vise à soutenir la croissance durable des paiements numériques dans le pays. items.title: 'Clear message' by Americans: US politicians react to Democratic win in US midterms
items.description: In a sweeping midterm rout , Democrats won control of the US Congress, with a series of upsets delivering a major rebuke to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. Many politicians, Democrats and Republicans alike, reacted as news of America’s choice broke, with the former rejoicing countrywide. Former US president Bill Clinton said Democrats will lower costs, protect healthcare, end senseless wars, while also stopping tariffs that make life more expensive. “You deserve a government that works as hard for you as you do for your family,” Clinton posted on X. “It’s high time we put people first again!” Former US president Barack Obama said the results were a “clear message” from the Americans. “They want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face,” Obama said on X. “These results were only possible because outstanding candidates stepped forward in every region of the country,” he added. “While this administration has another two years in office, our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future,” Obama further asserted. President Trump, meanwhile, in comments to Fox News , said, “Congratulations to the Democrats — they did a good job. They’ve been looking for this one for 11 years and they finally got it.” He added, “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” US Senator Bernie Sanders called the news “great” on X. “At a time of massive income and wealth inequality, we must do more. We must aggressively fight for working families. No more excuses,” he wrote. Former US vice president Kamala Harris reacted to the news with a video of herself saying, “Hallelujah!” Democratic Representative Robert Garcia, now expected to lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, in a post on X warned Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run from sea to shining sea”. Jeffries could become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January. Former secretary of transportation Pete Buttigieg, in the wake of a number of Republican strongholds flipping blue, said, “Tonight proves it: there is no such thing as a permanently red seat.” Senate Majority Leader John Thune, in a post on X, vowed: “As we head into 2027, Senate Republicans will not stand idly by as the far-left, socialist wing of the Democratic Party attempts to unwind everything we’ve done.” He expressed gratitude that Trump was still in the White House, hoping that the Republicans will “work with him to stop the worst impulses of Democrat extremism. We cannot let their fringe positions become the mainstream”. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis pointed out that it was “unlikely” Republicans would recapture Congress in 2028, looking at the Senate map and given the “massive” margin in the House. “Might not have a shot at Senate control until 2032,” he added. CNN cited DeSantis as saying that Republicans underemphasised the impact of high gas prices due to the Iran war, although he did not name Trump specifically. “Listen, we’ve just got to be honest. Gas is higher. It hurts people, working-class people, and it’s higher because of the Iran conflict […] If you can’t admit that to voters, then you’re gaslighting them,” DeSantis said on Stephen A. Smith’s podcast “Straight Shooter” on Monday, according to CNN . Former US Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene, reacting to the development, said it was a “total referendum” for Trump, accusing the US president of “covering up the Epstein files, protecting rapists and paedophiles” and starting the US-Iran war. She said Trump “killed a school full of kids, put his rich elite donors before the struggling Americans who put him in office, made life unaffordable with his tariffs, and caused gas and diesel prices to skyrocket while he played the market and sold crypto.” “And Republicans stood behind him silently clapping like trained baby seals,” she said. “And tonight they sent him a clear message,” she added, warning that Republicans “need to learn the lesson and drastically change course”. “And I’m not sure if they’re capable of that.”

items.title: L’UE réclame des fonds supplémentaires à ses alliés après une nouvelle demande de 70 milliards d’euros de Kiev
items.description: L'Union europeenne demande au Canada, au Royaume-Uni, au Japon et a la Norvege de participer davantage au financement de l'Ukraine. Selon Politico, Bruxelles cherche a mobiliser de nouveaux fonds apres que Volodymyr Zelensky a reclame 70 milliards d'euros supplementaires pour 2027, malgre les montants deja accordes a Kiev. Cette nouvelle demande vient s'ajouter au pret europeen de 90 milliards d'euros approuve pour 2026 et 2027. Sur cette enveloppe, 60 milliards doivent financer l'armement ukrainien et 30 milliards soutenir le budget de Kiev. Le pret devait initialement couvrir environ deux tiers des besoins estimes pour cette periode, le reste devant provenir d'autres partenaires internationaux. Or, selon Politico, une part importante des contributions attendues n'a toujours pas ete engagee. Bruxelles doit ainsi rechercher de nouveaux financements alors que les besoins annonces par Kiev continuent d'augmenter. Les 500 millions du Canada provoquent une divergence Les discussions avec les partenaires de l'UE revelent egalement des desaccords sur l'affectation des fonds. a l'issue d'un sommet UE-Canada, le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney a annonce une contribution de 500 millions d'euros, presentee comme un premier apport au pret europeen de 90 milliards. Mais un haut responsable europeen a precise a Politico que cet argent devait couvrir une partie du deficit budgetaire supplementaire de l'Ukraine en 2027, et non alimenter le pret deja approuve. Le Canada devra conclure un accord distinct avec Bruxelles pour participer a ce mecanisme. La Commission europeenne a accueilli favorablement cette annonce, sans renoncer a demander davantage de contributions. Son porte-parole, cite par Politico, a insiste sur la necessite de repartir la charge financiere entre les partenaires internationaux, compte tenu des besoins de financement de Kiev. Le financement de Kiev suscite des critiques en Europe Bruxelles prepare desormais une nouvelle proposition de financement pour le sommet du 26 novembre, ou seront notamment examines le budget a long terme de l'UE et les besoins ukrainiens. La Commission souhaite connaître avant cette date les montants que ses partenaires sont prets a engager. Ces nouvelles depenses font deja l'objet de contestations au sein de l'UE. Le 21 octobre, l'eurodepute slovaque Milan Uhrík avait denonce les 70 milliards supplementaires demandes par Kiev, accusant Bruxelles de vouloir faire supporter cette charge aux Europeens, alors que les menages subissent la hausse des prix et que les entreprises sont confrontees a des coûts energetiques eleves. Moscou denonce pour sa part la poursuite de l'aide financiere et militaire occidentale a Kiev. Les autorites russes estiment que ces financements prolongent le conflit et soulignent les depenses croissantes supportees par les citoyens europeens pour maintenir le soutien a l'Ukraine.

items.title: CAF Awards 2026: dix joueuses africaines se disputent le sacre continental
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a levé le voile, le mardi 3 novembre 2026, sur les nominées dans quatre catégories féminines des CAF Awards 2026. Dix joueuses sont notamment en course pour le prestigieux trophée de Joueuse africaine de l’année, dans une sélection qui fait la part belle aux talents du continent. La course au titre de Joueuse africaine de l’année s’annonce particulièrement disputée. Trois Camerounaises, Marie Ngah Manga, Michaely Bihina et Monique Ngock, figurent parmi les prétendantes, après leur sacre à la Coupe d’Afrique des nations féminine 2026 avec les Lionnes indomptables. Elles devront notamment faire face à l’Algérienne Marine Dafeur, à la Ghanéenne Portia Boakye, aux Malawites Tabitha et Temwa Chawinga, à la Marocaine Hanan Ait El Haj, à la Sud-Africaine Thembi Kgatlana et à la Zambienne Barbra Banda. Dans la catégorie Gardienne de but de l’année, le Sénégal sera représenté par Adji Ndiaye. La portière figure sur une liste de dix nominées aux côtés de l’Algérienne Chloé N’Gazi, de la Camerounaise Michaely Bihina, de la Ghanéenne Cynthia Konlan, de la Malawite Mercy Sikelo, de la Malienne Fatoumata Karantao, de la Marocaine Khadija El-Rmichi, de la Nigériane Christiana Uzoma, de la Sud-Africaine Kaylin Swart et de la Zambienne Hazel Nali. Le Sénégal peut également compter sur Adji Ndiaye dans la catégorie Jeune joueuse de l’année. Elle y retrouvera la Béninoise Romaine Gandonou, la Camerounaise Maeva Nyadjou, les Ivoiriennes Grace-Ruth Sery et N’Sira Ouédraogo, la Malawite Rose Kadzere, la Marocaine Kautar Azraf, les Nigérianes Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei et Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, ainsi que la Tanzanienne Winfrida Gerald. Au niveau des sélections, dix équipes nationales sont en compétition pour le trophée d’Équipe nationale féminine de l’année. Il s’agit de l’Algérie, du Cabo Verde, du Cameroun, de la Côte d’Ivoire, du Ghana, du Malawi, du Mali, du Maroc, du Nigéria et de l’Afrique du Sud. Parmi ces nations en lice, le Cameroun, champion d’Afrique en titre, et le Malawi, finaliste de la dernière CAN féminine, figurent en bonne place. L’Algérie, qui a terminé à la troisième position de cette compétition continentale, fait également partie des sélections retenues. Pour les autres distinctions féminines, notamment celles de Joueuse interclubs de l’année, d’Entraîneure de l’année et de Club féminin de l’année, il faudra patienter. La CAF a annoncé que les nominations dans ces catégories seront dévoilées à l’issue de la Ligue des champions féminine, programmée en Égypte en 2026. Les regards sont désormais tournés vers Lagos, au Nigéria, où se déroulera, le 7 décembre 2026, la cérémonie des CAF Awards. Une soirée au cours de laquelle les meilleures individualités et formations du football africain seront mises à l’honneur. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article CAF Awards 2026: dix joueuses africaines se disputent le sacre continental est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: AMA gives traders at unauthorised bus stops 48 hours to vacate
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has given traders occupying unauthorised bus stops across the metropolis 48 hours to cease trading and vacate the locations ahead of an enforcement exercise. In a statement issued on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Assembly said the directive followed concerns raised by commercial drivers over the obstruction of designated bus stops by hawkers and other traders. The AMA said the practice obstructed the movement of vehicles and pedestrians, contributed to traffic congestion and forced commuters to board and alight from vehicles at unsafe locations, increasing the risk of road accidents. The Assembly said the Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, had already initiated enforcement measures, including the removal of traders occupying unauthorised spaces at the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange, Achimota and parts of the Central Business District. It has urged hawkers and traders to immediately vacate designated bus stops and desist from trading in areas reserved for the movement of vehicles and pedestrians. “The Assembly will intensify enforcement and take the necessary action against persons who disregard this directive in accordance with the Assembly’s by-laws,” the statement said. The AMA also cautioned traders against returning to locations that have been cleared, warning that reoccupation of bus stops could result in further enforcement action, including prosecution. The Assembly said the exercise formed part of its efforts to restore order in public spaces, improve road safety and ensure that designated bus stops were used for their intended purpose. Traders who fail to comply with the directive could face enforcement action after the 48-hour deadline.
