items.title: Hammouchi au chevet du policier percuté à Agadir
items.description: Le Directeur général du pôle DGST-DGSN, Abdellatif Hammouchi, s’est rendu, ce mercredi 4 novembre, au Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) Mohammed VI d’Agadir pour s’enquérir de l’état de santé de l’officier de police grièvement blessé après avoir été délibérément percuté par un usager de la route. Sur place, le patron du pôle sécuritaire s'est informé de l'évolution clinique du fonctionnaire de police et de sa réponse aux soins médicaux prodigués. Abdellatif Hammouchi a ainsi tenu à lui apporter un soutien direct, saluant son professionnalisme et son sens aigu du devoir face à cette violente agression. À cette occasion, il a réaffirmé l'engagement indéfectible de la Direction générale de la Sûreté nationale (DGSN) à défendre ses effectifs et à les protéger contre toute atteinte survenue dans l'exercice de leurs missions régaliennes de préservation de l'ordre public et de protection des personnes et des biens. En amont de ce déplacement, le responsable sécuritaire avait d'ores et déjà accordé une promotion exceptionnelle au policier victime, tout en ordonnant aux services sociaux et médicaux de la DGSN de prendre intégralement en charge l'ensemble des frais d'hospitalisation et de traitement requis par son état de santé. Une commission conjointe avait également été dépêchée à son chevet par Abdellatif Hammouchi. Composée du directeur de la Fondation Mohammed VI pour les œuvres sociales des fonctionnaires de la sûreté nationale, de l'inspecteur des services de santé de la sûreté et du préfet de police d'Agadir, cette délégation s'était assurée de la mise en place de toutes les mesures d'accompagnement nécessaires. Cette visite illustre l'attention portée par le pôle sécuritaire à ses agents blessés en service commandé et consacre la mise en œuvre effective de la protection de l'État garantie aux personnels de la sûreté nationale, tout en renforçant les dispositifs d'assistance et de motivation au profit des forces de l'ordre. The post Hammouchi au chevet du policier percuté à Agadir appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mamadou Thug interpelle le ministère de la Culture : « L’autonomie des artistes nécessite un véritable accompagnement de l’État »
items.description: Rachat des billets de concerts, financement des spectacles et avenir de l’industrie culturelle guinéenne : l’ancien conseiller national et entrepreneur culturel Mamadou Thug appelle à repenser les mécanismes d’accompagnement de l’État. Pour lui, la responsabilisation des artistes est indispensable, mais elle ne doit pas devenir un prétexte au désengagement des pouvoirs publics. Le débat autour du rachat des billets de concerts par l’État continue de susciter des réactions dans le milieu culturel guinéen. Face à cette problématique, Mamadou Thug, artiste comédien, entrepreneur culturel et ancien membre du Conseil national de la Transition (CNT), apporte sa contribution au débat et invite à une réflexion plus large sur le modèle économique de la culture en Guinée. D’entrée de jeu, il tient à faire une distinction importante : les propos du ministre de la Culture ne constituent pas nécessairement, à ce stade, une décision administrative définitive. Il les interprète plutôt comme un appel à la prise de conscience et à la responsabilisation des artistes et des promoteurs de spectacles. Selon lui, les professionnels doivent désormais accorder une attention particulière à la qualité de leurs productions, à leurs stratégies de communication et à leur capacité à mobiliser un public prêt à payer pour assister aux événements. Pour Mamadou Thug, l’argent du contribuable ne devrait pas systématiquement servir à compenser les difficultés de commercialisation des spectacles. L’État peut accompagner les initiatives culturelles, mais la réussite économique d’un événement doit également reposer sur le travail, le professionnalisme et la capacité commerciale de ses organisateurs. Une autonomie financière qui ne doit pas se construire dans la précipitation Si Mamadou Thug partage le principe d’une plus grande autonomie financière des acteurs culturels, il met néanmoins en garde contre toute mesure qui ne tiendrait pas compte des réalités économiques du secteur. Le faible pouvoir d’achat des populations, les charges importantes liées à la production, les difficultés de communication et l’insuffisance des financements constituent autant de défis auxquels les artistes et les promoteurs sont confrontés. Dans ces conditions, il estime qu’une éventuelle réduction des mécanismes d’accompagnement public devrait nécessairement être accompagnée de solutions alternatives. « L’autonomie financière des acteurs culturels est un objectif à encourager, mais elle doit se construire progressivement, avec un environnement favorable, des mécanismes de financement adaptés et un véritable partenariat entre l’État, le secteur privé et les professionnels de la culture », défend-il. Des subventions transparentes et un véritable partenariat public-privé Pour sortir de cette dépendance économique, l’ancien conseiller national propose une nouvelle approche du financement culturel. Il plaide notamment pour la mise en place d’un mécanisme transparent de subventions destiné aux initiatives culturelles portées par des structures légalement constituées et répondant aux exigences administratives. Il appelle également à faciliter les relations entre les promoteurs, les entreprises privées, les banques et les institutions financières, afin de faire de la culture un véritable secteur d’investissement et de création de richesses. Mamadou Thug insiste particulièrement sur l’équité dans l’attribution des soutiens publics. À ses yeux, aucun artiste ou promoteur ne devrait être privilégié au détriment d’un autre sur la base de considérations opaques. Les critères de financement doivent être clairement définis, accessibles et applicables à tous. Il souhaite, par ailleurs, que l’expérience du financement public de la presse puisse inspirer une politique de soutien mieux structurée en faveur de l’ensemble des métiers de la culture. Ne pas réduire la culture à la seule musique Autre point essentiel de son intervention : la nécessité d’élargir le champ de la réflexion. Pour Mamadou Thug, l’industrie culturelle guinéenne ne se limite pas à la musique. Elle englobe également le théâtre, le cinéma, l’humour, la danse, la production audiovisuelle, les métiers techniques et l’organisation des spectacles. Tous ces professionnels participent à la vitalité culturelle et économique du pays et méritent, selon lui, une attention institutionnelle adaptée à leurs réalités. Un appel à une nouvelle vision de la politique culturelle En définitive, Mamadou Thug considère que le véritable enjeu dépasse largement la question du rachat des billets. Il s’agit plutôt de définir un modèle de financement capable de responsabiliser les acteurs, de stimuler l’investissement privé et de garantir un accompagnement public durable. Son message au département de la Culture est sans ambiguïté : l’État ne doit pas uniquement intervenir pour acheter des billets, mais surtout créer les conditions nécessaires à l’émergence d’entreprises culturelles solides et à la professionnalisation des métiers artistiques. Si une décision officielle venait à mettre fin au rachat des billets, cela ne devrait donc pas signifier la fin du soutien public à la culture. L’ambition, selon lui, doit être de bâtir une industrie culturelle guinéenne autonome, structurée, compétitive et économiquement viable, capable de créer des emplois, de générer des revenus et de porter le rayonnement de la Guinée au-delà de ses frontières. items.title: New Mining Act to transform mining communities, end licence speculation and boost Ghana’s royalties – Lands Minister
items.description: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has outlined major reforms in the new Mining Act currently before Parliament, which he says will transform mining communities, stop licence speculation and significantly increase Ghana’s mineral revenues. Speaking at a seminar organised by Geological Engineering Students of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) under the theme “From rocks to resources to results – leading Ghana’s extractive future,” the Minister said communities where mining has gone on for years have seen no visible impact. He said the government is changing that by making Community Development Agreements mandatory as part of the larger mining lease agreement to be signed by the Government of Ghana, where mining companies will sit down with communities to agree on development projects. To the Minister, communities will no longer be told they cannot be employed because they lack qualifications, as companies will be required to help produce the next professionals in the field within a specified number of years. “Don’t come back and tell the communities they can’t be employed here because they don’t have the qualifications. Let’s have an agreement with the communities that in the next ten years, the mine is going to help us produce the next geologists and engineers from this village or mining community,” he said. Mr. Buah said the government is also introducing District Mining Committees to curb the practice where miners show up in communities with licences from the Minerals Commission without the knowledge of chiefs and without verifying the use of the land at the time. Illegal mining is among the biggest challenges of the country’s mining sector, threatening lives and communities. Statistics from the Ministry show that Ghana has 288 Forest Reserves, with almost 50 of them completely impacted by illegal mining. This amounts to almost nine thousand hectares destroyed, equivalent to twelve thousand five hundred football fields. This has further affected air quality and water sources, as almost 60 percent of the country’s water comes from forest reserves. Research shows turbidity levels of river bodies are now between five thousand and twelve thousand, against the acceptable level of 0 to 500, making water treatment almost impossible. “Two weeks ago I was with the NAIMOS. Today, I can tell you that this issue of illegal mining must be our collective responsibility,” he said. He called on students to lead the fight against the canker, stressing the need for collective action to preserve the environment for future generations. A key focus of the new law, which seeks to revamp the 2014 mining policy, is ending licence speculation where individuals acquire reconnaissance licences and hold on to large tracts of land for years, waiting for investors without doing any work. “The new law is to provide a five-year exploration mining licence. Two years with conditions; if you meet those conditions, we expand it for five years. After five years, if you can’t find the gold, let’s give the land back to the community to start farming,” he said. The Minister also disclosed a major shift from the decades-old flat royalty regime, where a production cost of around 1800 dollars per ounce was used as a benchmark even when gold prices soared to 4000 and 5000 dollars, allowing companies to claim excess profit. “For decades, we had a flat regime of royalties, so a mining company will negotiate with Ghana that the cost of producing an ounce of gold will be around 1800 dollars; that becomes a benchmark. Gold prices may go all the way to 4000 dollars, and they are claiming the profit, and we’ve locked it up,” he said. He said the government has now introduced a sliding scale from 5 to 12 percent that rises when prices go up and drops when they come down, ensuring a reasonable return on investment for companies and higher royalties for the state. According to the Minerals Income Investment Fund, Ghana received 7.82 billion cedis as royalties between January and September this year, compared to 3 billion cedis under the previous regime, saving Ghana over four billion cedis. Meanwhile, the Minister encouraged students to work hard to attain the necessary academic heights as the government makes efforts to improve local content in the mining industry.

items.title: Ejisu to celebrate maiden Yaa Asantewaa I festival to rebuild burnt museum
items.description: The Ejisu Traditional Area is set to celebrate the maiden Nana Yaa Asantewaa I festival from December 24 to 27, in honour of the legacy of the brave female warrior of the Asante kingdom. The festival, launched by the Paramount Queen Mother of Ejisu, Nana Yaa Asantewaa II, seeks to raise funds for the reconstruction of the museum built in commemoration of the legend. The museum, which held some of the traditional relics of the queen mother, was destroyed by fire about 15 years ago, but has since not seen any major facelift to restore its glory. Speaking at the launch, Nana Yaa Asantewaa II said this year’s celebration would focus on rebuilding and recommissioning the museum to preserve the historical legacy of the renowned queen mother. She said the festival would serve as an annual platform to reflect on Nana Yaa Asantewaa I’s contributions to Asante history while mobilising support for the restoration of the museum. “This is the maiden festival in honour of our first queen mother, Nana Yaa Asantewaa I, and it will be celebrated every year to reflect on her history. This year’s event is, however, targeted at rebuilding the Nana Yaa Asantewaa Museum, which was burnt down 15 years ago,” she said. The Paramount Queen Mother revealed that the festival had received the approval of the Asantehene as she called on natives of the community and well-wishers to participate in the celebration. Regional Director of the Kumasi Cultural Centre, Peter Kofi Marfo, outlined activities planned for the three-day festival. He noted that activities on the first day, December 24 would include a community clean-up exercise, health screening and traditional games, while December 25 would feature traditional cooking competitions among various groups and churches in the area. The celebrations will climax on December 26 with a grand durbar, during which funds will be raised to support the reconstruction of the museum. Mr. Marfo called on various stakeholders and members of the public to turn up in their numbers to support the festival and contribute to preserving the historical heritage of Ejisu.

items.description: Le ministre roumain des Affaires étrangères, Dan Neculăescu, a réaffirmé la position de son pays à l'égard du plan d’autonomie présenté par le Maroc, et qui constitue « la base la plus adéquate, sérieuse, crédible et réaliste » pour parvenir à une solution juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable à la question du Sahara marocain. A l’occasion d’un entretien téléphonique mardi avec le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Nasser Bourita, le chef de la diplomatie roumaine a salué, à cet égard, l’engagement constructif du Maroc. Cet entretien a également permis aux deux ministres de réaffirmer leur volonté de renforcer les relations bilatérales, dans la continuité des liens historiques d’amitié et de coopération unissant les deux pays. Les échanges ont, par ailleurs, porté sur les prochaines échéances de la Francophonie, notamment le prochain Sommet et la candidature roumaine au poste de Secrétaire général de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). The post Sahara : la Roumanie réaffirme son soutien au plan d’autonomie marocain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Espagne: démission du ministre des Transports après deux catastrophes ferroviaires ayant fait 115 morts
items.description: Près d'une semaine après la catastrophe ferroviaire d'Urda, qui a fait au moins 69 morts le 28 octobre 2026, le ministre espagnol des Transports, Óscar Puente, a officiellement annoncé sa démission, le mardi 3 novembre, à l'issue d'une longue audition devant la Chambre des députés. Il renonce également à figurer sur les listes du Parti socialiste (PSOE) pour les élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre 2026. Le gouvernement espagnol de Pedro Sánchez est confronté à une nouvelle secousse politique. Mis sous pression après deux graves accidents ferroviaires survenus en moins d'un an, le ministre des Transports, Óscar Puente, a choisi de quitter ses fonctions. Son annonce, faite le mardi 3 novembre 2026, intervient dans un contexte de vive émotion nationale et de fortes critiques sur la gestion de la sécurité ferroviaire dans le pays. Pour justifier son départ, le désormais ex-ministre a invoqué un impératif de «dignité politique, de cohérence et d’empathie envers les victimes». Au-delà de son départ du gouvernement, il a également annoncé son retrait des listes électorales du Parti socialiste (PSOE), en vue des législatives anticipées du 29 novembre 2026. Cette démission intervient après le terrible accident ferroviaire du 28 octobre à Urda, dans la province de Tolède, au sud de Madrid. Le drame a coûté la vie à au moins 69 personnes et fait plus d'une centaine de blessés. Il s'agit du deuxième accident ferroviaire majeur à grande vitesse enregistré sous lui, après la collision survenue à Adamuz, en Andalousie, en janvier 2026, qui avait fait 46 morts. Une succession de défaillances au cœur de l'enquête Lors de sa comparution devant les députés, Óscar Puente a présenté les premiers éléments de l'enquête sur les circonstances de la catastrophe d'Urda. Selon ses explications, le drame serait lié à une «erreur humaine» survenue dans un centre de contrôle ferroviaire de Madrid, à la suite d'une panne informatique. Le dysfonctionnement aurait provoqué l'arrêt du système de signalisation automatique LZB, entraînant l'immobilisation de plusieurs trains par mesure de sécurité. Mais la situation aurait ensuite basculé lorsqu'un opérateur du centre de contrôle aurait ordonné manuellement à un train de la compagnie publique Renfe de reprendre sa circulation à vitesse normale. Le train ainsi remis en marche a alors violemment percuté par l'arrière un convoi de la compagnie privée Iryo, immobilisé sur la même voie. Un enchaînement de défaillances dont les conséquences humaines ont plongé l'Espagne dans le deuil. Une démission aux lourdes conséquences politiques Óscar Puente a indiqué avoir pris sa décision dans les minutes qui ont suivi le drame. Il aurait toutefois attendu le lancement des premières mesures d'urgence, des dispositifs d'indemnisation des victimes et d'un «plan extraordinaire de sécurité» avant de rendre sa démission publique. Cette nouvelle tragédie ferroviaire accentue les difficultés du gouvernement de gauche de Pedro Sánchez, déjà fragilisé par des sondages défavorables à quelques semaines des élections législatives anticipées. L'opposition de droite n'a pas tardé à réagir. Ester Muñoz, porte-parole du Parti populaire (PP), a, notamment, estimé que cette démission intervenait bien «trop tard», pointant le bilan cumulé des deux catastrophes, qu'elle a évalué à «116 vies» fauchées. En quittant le gouvernement et en renonçant à briguer un nouveau mandat parlementaire, Óscar Puente tente ainsi de tirer les conséquences politiques de deux drames ferroviaires successifs. Mais son départ ne devrait pas suffire à éteindre la polémique car, au-delà des responsabilités individuelles, c'est désormais toute la question de la sécurité du réseau ferroviaire espagnol qui se retrouve au cœur du débat public. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Espagne: démission du ministre des Transports après deux catastrophes ferroviaires ayant fait 115 morts est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: GPRTU, GRTCC call off planned sit-down strike after meeting with ministers
items.description: The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) and the Ghana Road Transport Coordinating Council (GRTCC) have called off their planned sit-down strike following assurances from government to address concerns over trading activities on road corridors. The two transport groups announced the planned sit-down strike on November 2, 2026, protesting what they described as the authorities’ failure to clear roadways of trading activities. The proposed action was expected to disrupt commercial transport services across the country. The latest decision means transport services will continue without the disruption that would have resulted from the planned strike. In a joint statement issued on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the two transport groups said the decision followed a meeting held on Tuesday, November 3, with the Ministers of the Interior, Transport, and Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs. The unions said the ministers had committed to addressing their concerns, which also include the provision of adequate road signage, sustained public education and continued engagement with transport operators. “The Ministers assured us of their firm commitments to address our concerns, including the trading activities on road corridors, adequate signage, sustained public education and continued engagement with transport operators,” the statement said. The meeting also resulted in the formation of a committee to identify areas affected by roadside trading and recommend measures to address the situation. Although the planned industrial action has been called off, the unions say they expect the government to address all the concerns raised within 30 days. They warned that failure to meet the deadline would leave them with no option but to proceed with the sit-down strike. “It is our expectation that all our concerns raised during the meeting will be addressed within 30 days, failure of which we would have no option than to embark on the sit-down strike,” the statement said. The GPRTU and GRTCC thanked the ministers for what they described as their prompt engagement and apologised to commuters and the general public for the inconvenience the planned strike could have caused.

items.title: La journée mondiale « Une seule santé » célébrée à Sédhiou
items.description: Réunis pour célébrer la journée mondiale « Une seule santé » (One health en anglais), les acteurs de la région de Sédhiou ont insisté sur la nécessité de préserver l'environnement. Ils ont aussi profité de cette rencontre pour présenter l'impact du projet « Une seule santé » mis en œuvre dans le département de Sédhiou. Sédhiou – La question de l'eau et de l'assainissement, la dégradation de l'environnement, la pollution, les maladies hydriques, zoonoses, les systèmes d'alertes précoces, toutes ces thématiques ont été abordées hier mardi 3 novembre par les acteurs régionaux, lors de la célébration de la journée mondiale « One Health », dans la région de Sédhiou. « Les acteurs ont posé les problématiques et identifié les défis auxquels ils sont confrontés », a expliqué Abdoulaye Sambou, expert en sécurité sanitaire au programme « One Health », assurant que des solutions ont été proposées pour mettre en œuvre l'approche « One Health » dans la région. Cette rencontre a permis de persister sur le lien réel entre la santé humaine et celle animale, mais aussi sur l'importance de préserver un environnement de qualité. A lire aussi : Programme « Une seule santé » : l’organisation Solthis évalue les points positifs « Les effets du changement climatique, les maladies zoonotiques, la gestion des déchets et la préservation des ressources naturelles constituent des défis qui interpellent collectivement », a fait remarquer Ba Ousmane Danfakha, adjoint au gouverneur de la région de Sédhiou. Il faut préciser que la journée a été tenue sous le signe du « renforcement de la collaboration multisectorielle pour une meilleure santé animale, humaine, environnementale dans un contexte de changement climatique ». Au cours des travaux, les échanges ont mis en évidence la nécessité de renforcer la collaboration entre les différents services de la santé, de l'élevage, de l'agriculture, de la pêche et de l'environnement, mais aussi des collectivités territoriales et de la communauté. « Trois principales orientations ont été déclinées pour rendre efficaces les interventions : le renforcement de la collaboration multisectorielle, la promotion d'une gestion intégrée, mais surtout la promotion et l'implication des communautés en traduisant les engagements en action concrète », a résumé Ba Ousmane Danfakha. Pour rappel, le projet « One Health » s'articule sur quatre axes majeurs : « la sensibilisation pour susciter la prise de conscience et l'engagement communautaire. Le renforcement de capacité des acteurs communautaires et des professionnels des trois santés pour une compréhension du changement climatique. Mais aussi un volet résilience climatique des postes de santé ». Il a permis de doter des postes de santé de Sédhiou, de Djirédji, d'équipements de climatisation solaire, et de mini-forages », a confié Philippe Corréa, coordonnateur du projet Senaya au sein de l'organisation Solthis. Tout cela permet de rendre le service accessible aux populations. Rappelant l'impact des interventions, les activités de M. Correa ont affirmé que près de 8000 personnes dans les quartiers et les villages de la région de Sédhiou ont été touchées, tous ces individus peuvent comprendre le concept « One Health ». Dans la lutte contre le changement climatique, plus de 20 hectares ont été reboisés à Djirédji et à Bouno. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (Correspondant)

items.title: Forécariah : le grand marché de Famoréah, englouti par la boue et les ordures
items.description: Considéré comme l’un des plus grands marchés hebdomadaires de la Basse-Côte, le marché de Famoreah, dans la préfecture de Forécariah, accueille chaque semaine des commerçants et des acheteurs venus de plusieurs localités de la Guinée et de pays voisins. Malgré son importance économique et commerciale, ce centre d’échanges est confronté à un manque d’infrastructures et surtout à un sérieux problème d’insalubrité. Une situation qui suscite l’inquiétude des usagers. Chaque dimanche, le marché hebdomadaire de Famoreah connaît une forte affluence. Commerçants, vendeuses et acheteurs s’y donnent rendez-vous pour vendre et acheter une diversité de produits. Huile rouge, denrées alimentaires, produits agricoles, bananes et articles divers sont exposés dans les différents espaces du marché. La réputation de ce centre commercial dépasse les frontières de la préfecture de Forécariah. Des commerçants et acheteurs viennent notamment de la Sierra Leone, du Liberia et du Mali, mais aussi de plusieurs villes guinéennes, dont Dubréka, Kindia, Conakry et Kamsar. L’administrateur du marché, Ibrahima Sory Touré, souligne l’importance de ce lieu de commerce, tout en déplorant les difficultés auxquelles ses usagers sont confrontés. « Presque toute la Guinée fréquente ce marché. Même des commerçants venus de la Sierra Leone s’y rendent avec différentes marchandises, notamment des bananes et d’autres produits. Cependant, nous sommes confrontés à un sérieux problème de boue et d’insalubrité », explique-t-il. Derrière cette importante activité commerciale se cachent pourtant des conditions difficiles. La boue, les eaux stagnantes et les tas d’ordures occupent plusieurs endroits du marché, compliquant la circulation des personnes et le déroulement des activités commerciales. Pour les vendeuses et les acheteurs, cette situation constitue un véritable calvaire. Fatoumata 5 Sily Bangoura, vendeuse au marché, dénonce également ces conditions d'hygiène qu'elle juge inacceptables. « Ici, il y a beaucoup de boue et d’ordures. Pourtant, aucun être humain ne devrait vivre dans un environnement aussi insalubre », déplore-t-elle. Face à cette situation, les autorités communales reconnaissent les difficultés auxquelles le marché est confronté. Le maire de la commune Elhadj Konko Sankon a déploré cet état de fait avant d'annoncer des mesures d'accompagnement ainsi que des dispositions visant à améliorer la propreté de cet espace commercial dans les prochains jours. En attendant la concrétisation de ces annonces, les commerçants et les acheteurs interpellent les autorités locales et les pouvoirs publics sur la nécessité d'engager des actions urgentes pour assainir et aménager ce grand centre commercial.

items.title: Federal cabinet ratifies defence agreement with Kuwait
items.description: The federal cabinet on Wednesday ratified the defence cooperation agreement between Pakistan and Kuwait, according to a handout by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). “The federal cabinet ratified a defence cooperation agreement between Pakistan and Kuwait. This agreement, which aims to foster cooperation in the defence sector between the two brotherly nations, was concluded on June 11, 2023. The Kuwaiti government had ratified the agreement on July 19,” the handout said. In 2023, Pakistan and Kuwait signed a defence pact to further strengthen defe­nce cooperation and institutional linkages between the armed forces of the two countries. The statement also said that the cabinet approved the transfer of powers delegated to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to the province’s governor. The Centre declared an emergency and governor’s rule in the province on Oct 11. It said the powers included “the conduct of day-to-day affairs during the period of emergency in the province, to facilitate the smooth handling of administrative matters in KP and further improve governance”. “The KP governor will submit a review report to the federal government every month regarding the exercise of all such powers,” the statement said. It stated that the federal cabinet welcomed the decision and expressed the hope that the KP Advisory Council , under the leadership of the Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, would make full efforts for the welfare and prosperity of the people of the province and for establishing peace and security. Moreover, the federal cabinet, on the recommendation of the Ministry of Finance, approved the design of new currency notes, the statement added. “The cabinet was given a detailed briefing on the new currency notes. The briefing stated that proposals were solicited from artists and designers across the country for the design of the new currency notes and a cabinet committee established by the prime minister conducted detailed consultations on it with all stakeholders,” the handout said. According to the statement, the meeting was informed that, along with enhancing security features to prevent counterfeit notes, modern materials would be used, which would also extend the lifespan of the notes. The federal cabinet also approved the introduction of a Rs10 coin in place of the Rs10 banknote, the PMO statement said. ‘Pakistan continuing efforts for peace in Middle East’ Addressing the federal cabinet during televised remarks, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif noted that global oil prices had “skyrocketed” due to the instability in the region. “Pakistan is playing its role as before in restoring peace in the region,” he said, recalling Pakistan’s recent engagements with Tehran and other regional actors in the matter, as well as engagements under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Last month, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, visited Iran as part of Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between Washington and Tehran. In another meeting in October, held under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, CDF Munir, the Saudi defence minister, and the Turkish spymaster met top Iranian officials in Tehran. Last week, the military’s spokesman said Pakistan remained “cautiously optimistic” about its mediation between the US and Iran. On Tuesday, PM Shehbaz also recalled that the government had planned to hike fuel prices by Rs15 on Friday. “Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik [..] talked to the refineries to bear the burden in their windfall profits. We will not let a common man bear this burden,” he added. Speaking about the fuel subsidy scheme, launched in September, the premier said it would run till the end of December. “Rs28 billion has been spent so far,” he said, adding that the scheme was running “successfully and transparently” and that the Intelligence Bureau (IB) continued to monitor it. On liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), the prime minister said that the “era of mafiaa” was over and it was now being arranged transparently. “Now when LPG is imported, competition will be promoted and it will be auctioned in lots. The government will take the profits and subsidise it for the common man,” he said. He also stressed that the federal government was holding meetings “day and night” to meet LPG, liquefied natural gas (LNG), petrol and gas requirements ahead of winter despite challenges arising from the closure of maritime routes. LPG supply has been disrupted in the country due to the closure of Iranian border crossings, resulting in gas cylinders being sold at twice the official rate in the open market. PM Shehbaz also said that the federal government had finalised a proposed Rs160bn package for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “Security is our number one, two and three priority in KP,” the premier remarked. He further noted that counterterrorism efforts continued in the region. With the efforts of law enforcement agencies, the new government in KP and the support of the federal government, we will crush terrorism,” he said.

items.title: Government explores light rail network on four major Accra routes – Mahama Ayariga
items.description: The government is exploring the possibility of introducing a light rail network along four major routes in Accra as part of efforts to develop a more sustainable solution to the capital’s growing transportation challenges. The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, said President John Dramani Mahama had directed him to initiate discussions on the feasibility of introducing light rail services along routes serving large numbers of commuters travelling into and out of the capital. The proposed network is being considered as a more permanent mass transportation option alongside the existing Aayalolo bus contra-flow system, which allows designated buses to travel against the normal direction of traffic on selected corridors to ease congestion and reduce journey times. Speaking on Accra-based Citi FM on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, Mr Ayariga said the current arrangement had significantly improved journey times for commuters, but the President wanted a more sustainable solution for the future. He said he had been tasked with engaging the relevant authorities, particularly the Railway Authority, to explore the possibility of developing light rail infrastructure along the four major routes. “The President said, ‘contra-flow is good, but look at light rail as your more permanent solution going into the future,’ and so I am commencing conversations with the Railway Authority for us to see how we can begin to look at light rail along the four major routes that bring in a lot of the people in and out of the city.” The Aayalolo contra-flow system was introduced to improve public transport efficiency along some of Accra’s busiest road corridors, particularly during peak periods when commuters face lengthy delays travelling into and out of the city. Under the arrangement, designated buses are permitted to use selected lanes in the opposite direction of normal traffic, allowing them to bypass congestion and provide faster journeys for passengers. The intervention is intended to make public transport more efficient and reliable, particularly for residents travelling from surrounding communities to major commercial and employment centres in the capital. However, the system remains dependent on existing road infrastructure, effective traffic management and the availability of buses and personnel to sustain its operations. The proposed light rail initiative signals the government’s intention to explore a more permanent mass transportation option to address Accra’s growing commuter traffic and improve movement along major routes into and out of the city.

items.title: Les majestueuses chutes d’eau de Lélou et de Goumbouroun à Lélouma : immersion dans un paysage à couper le souffle
items.description: A seulement quelques kilomètres du centre urbain de Lélouma, dans un décor naturel d’une beauté saisissante se dressent deux impressionnantes chutes d’eau. Celle de Lélou et de Goumbouroun à quelques dizaines de mètres l’une de l’autre. Autour d’elles, d’autres petites cascades prolongent le spectacle. Le tout dans un décor de formation rocheuse et de blocs de pierres qui donnent au site un aspect particulier. Sur ces hauteurs, une forêt dense et verdoyante enveloppe le paysage. La végétation offre à l’endroit un magnifique décor plein de promesses touristiques. Made with LogoLicious Add Your Logo App Les deux principales cascades situées dans ce même arc montagneux à environ 50 mètres constituent les pièces maîtresses du paysage. Leurs eaux se jettent dans le vide à plusieurs dizaines de maîtres de hauteur. Pendant que des petites chutes secondaires complètent le tableau. En amont, dans différents endroits, l’eau contourne des blocs de pierres sur des surfaces rocheuses formant ainsi une succession de petites cascades et de bassins naturels. Dans les alentours, les arbres, arbustes et feuillages d’une verdure exceptionnelle habillent les hauteurs et donnent au paysage un aspect presque sauvage. Made with LogoLicious Add Your Logo App Au delà de cette beauté, ce site représente un potentiel important et très intéressant pour le développement du tourisme local. Mais tout d’abord, pour transformer cette richesse naturelle en véritable destination touristique des efforts considérables liés à l’accès et à l’aménagement sont nécessaires.

items.title: NPP’s GH¢5,000 parliamentary application fee could sideline women, youth – GenCED
items.description: The Gender Centre for Empowering Development (GenCED) has warned that the reported GH¢5,000 parliamentary candidate application fee introduced by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) could deepen financial barriers to political participation, particularly for women, young people and persons with disabilities. The NPP recently announced a GH¢5,000 application fee for parliamentary aspirants, alongside a GH¢2,000 fee for declaring interest. The party has defended the charges as necessary to ensure that only serious candidates proceed to the nomination stage. In a statement issued on Friday, October 30, 2026, the organisation said although political parties had legitimate administrative and organisational costs, their candidate selection requirements should not unnecessarily disadvantage qualified individuals from groups historically underrepresented in political leadership. It questioned whether the growing cost of competing for political office was making access to leadership increasingly dependent on financial resources rather than candidates’ competence and commitment to public service. “For GenCED, this development raises a fundamental question about Ghana’s democracy: Does every qualified citizen have a fair opportunity to compete for political office, or is access to leadership increasingly determined by financial capacity?” the statement said. GenCED said women aspiring to parliamentary office often faced additional challenges in mobilising the resources required to contest elections. These include unequal economic opportunities, limited access to influential political networks and sponsorship, as well as the disproportionate burden of unpaid care and domestic responsibilities. It warned that the GH¢5,000 application fee could discourage qualified women who lacked wealthy sponsors or established financial networks from entering the political contest. The organisation added that the application fee was only one part of the financial demands candidates faced, with aspiring MPs also expected to mobilise resources for transportation, campaign activities, constituency engagement and internal party elections. “When the ability to pay becomes a significant determinant of who enters the political contest, Ghana risks narrowing the pool of potential leaders and perpetuating women’s underrepresentation in Parliament,” it said. The organisation also raised concerns about the implications for young people and persons with disabilities (PWDs), who may have the qualifications and ideas to contribute to national development but lack the financial resources and backing available to more established political figures. It said substantial financial requirements at the initial stages of the candidate selection process could prevent emerging leaders from competing, regardless of their capacity to serve. GenCED called on the NPP to review the application fee and assess its potential impact on women, young people and economically disadvantaged aspiring candidates. It also recommended that the party: Introduce transparent fee reductions or waivers for eligible candidates facing structural financial barriers. Clearly communicate how application fees are determined and how the funds collected are managed. Strengthen practical support for underrepresented groups seeking to participate in internal party elections and political leadership. The organisation further urged other political parties to review their candidate selection and financing arrangements to ensure that financial requirements did not unnecessarily restrict inclusive political participation.

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.description: South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhage of votes for the country’s biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC). This year’s voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes. Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa’s nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994, when the racist apartheid system ended. Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime. At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later, its share dropped to 40%. Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections, but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral. “What I’m seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers,” he told supporters at the party’s final election rally on Sunday. In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support. The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard. We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so. They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services. But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change. “We face many challenges in Alexandra. There’s rubbish everywhere, and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues,” he said. Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties. On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road. The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn’t vote, even though she is registered to do so. The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision. “It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years,” she said. Alex, as the township is known, is a stone’s throw away from Sandton, Africa’s richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker. Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads, but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it. The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships. South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery. Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life, and he told the BBC about the community’s daily struggles with accessing water and electricity. “Every Monday we know we won’t have water after 2 pm,” he said. Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the “arrogance” he says local leaders have towards residents and “change the status quo”. These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa’s local governance. Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa’s 257 municipalities. A recent report only gave 39 clean audits – the highest ranking a public entity can achieve – between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng’s three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list. Earlier this year, Auditor-General Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg “needs ongoing attention”. “If we don’t do that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living,” she told lawmakers. The city has been labelled “effectively bankrupt” due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years. Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa’s wealthiest city as well as the country’s seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in. Of South Africa’s eight metros, only three are governed by a single party. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party. But that might change. Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a “verdict … and judgment” on the ANC. “And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it’s ever done,” she said. Several polls point to a continued decline in support for the party in Wednesday’s election, contested by over 500 political parties. One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC’s support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021. The same poll, along with others, points to a slight increase in electoral support for the Democratic Alliance (DA), especially in Johannesburg. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time. DA leader Helen Zille has been vying for the mayoral chain in the city, and her unusual campaign has attracted a lot of attention. The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a “Gusheshe”. She believes the DA is the country’s best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that “towns and cities that work best are under DA governance”. Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa’s ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue to be the order of the day across Gauteng. These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level, and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities. Verwoerd said that, in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power. Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country’s best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC. Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a “different story”, Verwoerd said. The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area, but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won’t and will need partners to form a government. The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election. Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be “very messy” given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA. A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections. Another political analyst, Dr Levy Ndou, echoed Verwoerd’s assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros. “We’re not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run,” he said. Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa’s elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline. Ndou attributed this to the “calibre” of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns. South Africa’s electoral commission has seven days to announce the results, but parties have 14 days to form a governing structure.

items.title: Cameroun : Nourane Fotsing annonce l’adhésion de 128 nouveaux militants au PSG
items.description: © DR Son annonce fait suite à la publication d’une lettre de démission commune de 128 militants du PCRN pour plusieurs motifs, dont une « opposition de façade » du président national du parti. Une démission considérée comme fausse par d’autres militants du parti. Une nouvelle vague de démission présumée survient au Parti camerounais pour la réconciliation nationale. 128 militants du parti présidé par Cabral Libii et membre de la base militante dans la région du Nord signent leur départ de la formation politique. Dans une lettre commune en date du 03 novembre et adressée au président du parti, ils invoquent plusieurs motifs à savoir : l’éloignement de l’objectif du changement fixé dans le Mouvement 11 millions de citoyens ; le refus de collaborer avec les forces vives de l’opposition lors la présidentielle de 2025, son soutien au régime en faveur de la nomination d’un vice-président ; le démenti de la possession de 21 000 procès-verbaux par un ancien conseiller du président du PCRN, un parti sous couvert d’une opposition de façade au lieu d’une alliance assumée avec le régime. Pour ces motifs, ils décident d’aller voir ailleurs. Sur la toile, d’autres militants et cadres du PCRN démentent cette démission et dénoncent une manipulation de l’opinion. Dans une vidéo, un militant prend ses distances au vu de la liste de militants démissionnaire. Il déclare que certains noms de démissionnaires lui sont inconnus dans la localité de Lagdo. Sa sortie amène à questionner la véracité de la démission et surtout du nombre de démissionnaires. Cependant, Nourane Fotsing, députée et responsable des femmes du Parti social pour la gouvernance (PSG), annonce ce 04 novembre, l’accueil par son nouveau parti politique de 128 nouveaux militants dans la région du Nord. Le timing de l’annonce et le chiffre coïncident avec la publication de la lettre de démission ayant la liste de démissionnaires en annexes. Analysant la déclaration de la députée, il s’agit ainsi d’une nouvelle vague de militants qui quittent le PCRN comme elle pour aller grossir les rangs du PSG. Le 26 septembre dernier, Nourane Fotsing et 65 militants et cadres du Parti camerounais pour la réconciliation nationale quittaient le PCRN . Cet article Cameroun : Nourane Fotsing annonce l’adhésion de 128 nouveaux militants au PSG est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Gender Data Ghana calls for increased funding for healthcare and child protection in 2027 budget
items.description: Gender Data Ghana (GDG) is calling for increased and predictable funding for healthcare and child protection in the 2027 National Budget, urging the government to address persistent inequalities affecting women, children and other vulnerable groups. The independent, non-profit and non-partisan think tank says greater investment in primary healthcare, maternal and reproductive health services and child protection institutions is needed to translate government policy commitments into tangible improvements in people’s lives. In a statement issued on Wednesday, November 4, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on November 12, GDG said the national budget must reflect the government’s constitutional obligations and commitment to the well-being and dignity of citizens. “The national budget is a powerful expression of the Government’s priorities, constitutional obligations and commitment to the well-being and dignity of its people, especially populations that have been left behind,” portions of the statement read. On healthcare, GDG expressed concern about persistent shortages of essential medical supplies, inadequate hospital infrastructure, disparities in access to healthcare and high maternal mortality. It cited an estimated maternal mortality rate of 243 deaths per 100,000 live births, saying Ghana remained considerably behind the Sustainable Development Goal target of fewer than 70 deaths by 2030. The organisation is therefore calling for “increased allocations to primary healthcare, maternal and reproductive health services, essential medicines, hospital beds, oxygen supplies, personal protective equipment and emergency referral systems, particularly in underserved communities.” It also urged the government to explore local manufacturing of essential medical supplies to create employment opportunities for young people and strengthen national health security. On child protection, GDG referenced the recent sexual abuse allegations involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, saying the case had exposed weaknesses in Ghana’s child protection and institutional accountability systems. “The protection of children cannot be left to institutional goodwill, internal investigations or the courage of individual whistleblowers. It requires properly resourced, independent and accessible protection mechanisms,” the statement said. Press Release on the 2027 Budget Reading 11 3 2026 Download GDG urged the Ministry of Finance to prioritise funding for the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, its Department of Social Welfare and the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) of the Ghana Police Service. It further recommended the progressive deployment of professionally trained social welfare officers to public educational institutions across the country. According to the organisation, the officers should operate independently of the Ghana Education Service, with clear reporting and referral arrangements, to ensure that children’s welfare takes precedence over institutional reputation or the interests of alleged perpetrators. The statement also called for adequate budgetary support for professional training, survivor-centred services, psychosocial care, investigations and access to justice. On infrastructure development, GDG urged the Ministry of Finance to institutionalise gender and human rights impact assessments in the planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring of major infrastructure projects. It said poor roads and prolonged construction works affect women’s access to healthcare, markets and livelihoods, while exposing schoolchildren to safety risks and making it difficult for pregnant women to access emergency obstetric care. “Public investment must deliver equitable social and economic returns, not merely physical infrastructure,” it stated. GDG also called for gender-responsive budgeting to be institutionalised across Ministries, Departments and Agencies, supported by gender budget statements, measurable expenditure indicators and periodic reporting on actual expenditure and outcomes. It urged the Ministry to support the generation and use of gender statistics, including the proposed SDG 5+ Gender Equality Index, in national development planning and budget monitoring. The organisation stressed that healthcare, gender equality and child protection should not be treated as peripheral or competing priorities. “They are fundamental to productivity, social stability, human capital development and sustainable economic growth,” it added.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : volontaires, les visages d’une aventure historique
items.description: Sur les différents sites de Dakar 2026, ils seront parmi les premiers visages rencontrés par le public. Venus de l’événementiel, de la création ou d’autres horizons, les volontaires se préparent à accueillir, orienter et accompagner les participants. Au-delà de la mission, ils veulent vivre une expérience humaine, acquérir de nouvelles compétences et inscrire leur nom dans une aventure appelée à compter pour le Sénégal. Sur les sites des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse « Dakar 2026 », ils sont déjà là. Ils orientent, accueillent, renseignent, accompagnent. Au cœur battant des compétitions, les volontaires prennent progressivement possession de leurs espaces de travail et découvrent l’ampleur d’un rendez-vous qui dépasse leurs parcours personnels. Au site du Cto, installé au niveau du Tour de l’œuf, dans l’ancienne piscine olympique, Ibrahima Sall se prépare à entrer dans le bain des Joj. Photographe et vidéaste, il connaît déjà les coulisses des événements. Son expérience de quatre ans dans le volontariat, notamment comme ambassadeur volontaire au « Festival Game International », l’a conduit naturellement vers Dakar 2026. « J’aime servir, partager mon énergie et apporter ma contribution à la communauté », dit-il. Chez lui, le volontariat ne ressemble donc pas à une découverte. Il est devenu une manière de participer à la vie collective, de donner de son temps et de mettre son énergie au service des autres. Mais les Joj changent d’échelle. Ibrahima dit s’être préparé « mentalement et humainement », avec motivation et esprit d’équipe. Son principal défi est désormais de répondre aux attentes liées à sa mission et de contribuer au bon déroulement des Jeux. Derrière cette volonté, il y a aussi une ambition personnelle, celle d’apprendre, de développer son réseau et d’enrichir son expérience professionnelle et humaine. Cette envie d’apprendre traverse aussi le parcours d’un autre volontaire rencontré dans le dispositif. Il s’appelle Fallou Mbaye. Lui aussi arrive avec une expérience déjà construite dans l’événementiel. A lire aussi : [Datajournalisme]-JOJ Dakar 2026 : les chiffres clés d’un rendez-vous historique Pendant trois ans, il a participé au Festival des Games, où il a appris à accueillir le public, à travailler en équipe, à organiser et surtout à composer avec les imprévus. Des réflexes qui trouvent aujourd’hui un nouveau terrain d’expression avec les Joj. Il sait pourtant que le changement d’échelle est considérable. « Ce que j’appréhende le plus, c’est l’ampleur d’un événement international comme les Joj », reconnaît-il. La préparation passe alors par l’expérience accumulée, mais aussi par une disposition à apprendre encore. Il veut donner le meilleur de lui-même et transformer ces quelques jours en véritable expérience professionnelle et humaine. Son regard se porte déjà sur l’après-JOJ. Il espère gagner en confiance, renforcer son leadership, améliorer sa communication et son esprit d’équipe. Les rencontres comptent aussi beaucoup. Mais au-delà des compétences et du réseau, une image revient dans son discours, celle d’un jeune qui pourra un jour raconter qu’il a participé à un événement qui aura marqué le Sénégal et l’Afrique. Cette même fierté apparaît sous une autre forme chez Aminata Diawara, entrepreneuse et créatrice, volontaire sur le site de la Corniche Ouest. Son profil rappelle que le volontariat rassemble des parcours différents et des motivations qui ne se ressemblent pas forcément. Entrepreneurs, artistes, professionnels de l’événementiel ou jeunes désireux de vivre une expérience nouvelle, tous se retrouvent désormais dans les mêmes espaces, avec une responsabilité commune. Du Tour de l’Œuf à la Corniche Ouest, les visages changent, les parcours aussi, mais une même énergie circule. Celle de jeunes qui veulent être utiles, apprendre et participer à un moment qui dépasse leur propre histoire. Leur présence se mesurera dans les détails. Un spectateur renseigné, un visiteur orienté, un problème rapidement pris en charge, une équipe qui fonctionne. Derrière ces services du quotidien, il y aura des volontaires qui auront choisi de donner de leur temps pour accompagner les Jeux. Pour Ibrahima Sall, cette aventure prolonge quatre années d’engagement. Pour son collègue Fallou, elle constitue un nouveau chapitre après plusieurs expériences dans l’événementiel. Pour Aminata Diawara, vient s'inscrire son parcours d’entrepreneuse et de créatrice dans une aventure collective. Des itinéraires différents, réunis le temps des Joj par une même envie, celle de pouvoir dire, au terme des compétitions, « j’y étais ». Par Amadou KEBE

items.title: Sam George calls for dismissal of military officer over alleged misconduct in Ningo-Prampram
items.description: The Minister of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has called on the Chief of Defence Staff to take disciplinary action against a military officer he accuses of leading an operation involving the seizure of trucks in the Ningo-Prampram Constituency. The minister identified the officer as Lieutenant Albert Goh and accused him and other soldiers of entering the constituency heavily armed, seizing trucks belonging to residents without lawful authority, and mistreating local people. “And to Lieutenant Albert Goh, who came here yesterday with his men, this is a warning to you. It should be your last time because you are a disgrace to the Ghana Armed Forces. Albert Goh, your official number, your Ghana Army number, is 5666.” “And I’m saying that Lieutenant Albert Goh, you are a disgrace to the uniform that you wear. And I expect the Chief of Defence Staff, the CDS, to dismiss you from the Armed Forces for bringing disgrace to the Army. What you did yesterday was akin to armed robbery,” he said. Describing the alleged conduct as akin to armed robbery, Sam George said the military personnel had no justification for taking citizens’ property. “What you did yesterday was akin to armed robbery,” he said, directly addressing the lieutenant. “Picking weapons from the Ghana Armed Forces armory, coming here, seizing the trucks of citizens without any lawful order, driving that truck for two weeks, somebody’s property. You are a thief.” He maintained that the people of Ningo-Prampram deserved justice, adding that the matter would be pursued through the appropriate military disciplinary channels. “And I’m going to have a conversation with my colleague, the Minister of Defence, to make sure that he insists that the Army disciplines you, Albert Goh. He also warned soldiers against returning to the constituency to brutalise residents, saying they would be held accountable under the law. “Any soldier who comes to Ningo-Prampram to brutalise the people of Ningo-Prampram again, you will face the law of the streets,” he said. The minister further alleged that the soldiers had taken trucks belonging to residents and used them for about two weeks without lawful authorisation. He said he would raise the matter with the Minister of Defence to ensure that the military authorities investigated the incident and held those involved accountable. Sam George also accused the lieutenant of disrespecting a police commander who had attempted to engage him over the operation. According to the minister, the commander, a Chief Superintendent, was disrespected, while some of the soldiers allegedly cocked their weapons at him. He questioned the conduct of the personnel, saying their actions were inconsistent with the standards expected of members of the Ghana Armed Forces. The minister said he had obtained the names of the soldiers involved and would pursue the matter through the appropriate military disciplinary channels. He maintained that residents of Ningo-Prampram deserved justice and that the incident would not be allowed to go unaddressed. For you to issue a public warning to a soldier and instruct the military to respect the police in your constituency takes some balls. Sam George gotta be the hardest guy! Fearless! https://t.co/BzjkXm4OhV — BONGO IDEAS (@BongoIdeasHQ) November 3, 2026

items.title: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
items.description: US President Donald Trump asked voters to pretend he was on the ballot in the midterm elections and handpicked Republican candidates in some of the country’s most consequential Senate races. By Tuesday night, voters had rejected them . Trump-backed candidates in South Carolina, North Carolina and Texas all lost, while the president’s preferred pick trailed in early results in Michigan. The defeats handed Democrats control of the chamber and exposed the limits of Trump’s political power. Trump has spent more than a decade reshaping the Republican Party around his ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) movement, dictating primary matchups and pushing aside conservative figures he felt were insufficiently loyal or not aligned with his vision. Trump repeatedly favoured loyalists and ideological allies over more established Republicans with stronger statewide networks and proven electoral track records, betting that his endorsement could overcome their political liabilities. Tuesday’s results revealed he was unable to persuade the broader electorate to back his choices. People react at a US midterms elections night watch party hosted by the Congressional Progressive Staff Association (CPSA) and Metro DC Democratic Socialists of America (MDC DSA), in Washington, DC, the US on November 3, 2026. — Reuters One of the most stunning repudiations came in South Carolina, which had not elected a Democratic senator since 1998 and which Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024. Trump backed Darline Graham, the sister of late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham . But Democrat Annie Andrews won the seat in a stunning upset. In North Carolina, Trump endorsed former national Republican campaign official Michael Whatley, who lost in a rout to former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper. In Texas , Trump intervened in a messy Republican primary election to promote scandal-plagued Attorney General Ken Paxton over Senator John Cornyn, a Trump ally who some in the party considered a safer pick in the general election. Democrat James Talarico glided to a victory on Tuesday night, delivering Democrats a seat the party had not won since 1988. Republican senatorial candidate Ken Paxton addresses supporters after his defeat in the Texas US Senate race at The Westin Galleria Dallas in Dallas, Texas, on November 3, 2026. — AFP Former US Representative Mike Rogers , Trump’s choice in Michigan, trailed Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in an uncalled race. El-Sayed would be the first Muslim to serve in the Senate. The losses came as Trump’s popularity was lower heading into Tuesday’s vote than in the aftermath of the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol, according to Reuters/Ipsos polls. That helped fuel concerns among Republicans that the president had become a drag on the party he remade around himself. This is a “Trump Quake”, said Doug Heye, a veteran Republican strategist, pointing to voter frustration over high prices caused by tariffs and the war in Iran. “Trump spent the year telling voters what was important to him, not to them.” Trump struck a defiant tone as election returns arrived. “I wasn’t on the ballot, and if I was, we would have won in a landslide!” Trump wrote in a Tuesday night social media post . One White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves. A senior White House official, also speaking anonymously, told Reuters the administration had polling data as far back as six weeks ago showing Republicans would lose both the House of Representatives and Senate, and Trump embarked on a month-long nationwide campaign to try to salvage Republicans’ prospects. ‘Gave that seat away’ Some independent analysts said the Senate losses bore Trump’s fingerprints specifically. Thomas Kahn, a professor at American University, said the president’s intervention in the Texas Republican primary had cost his party a safe seat, arguing that a nomination for Senator John Cornyn “would have been a slam dunk for Republicans to win.” North Carolina, Kahn said, was another clear case. The Republican incumbent senator, Thom Tillis, said he would not seek re-election last year after a public split with Trump, who threatened to back a primary challenger against him after Tillis baulked at Medicaid cuts in the president’s tax-and-spending bill. “He essentially gave that seat away to Democrats,” Kahn said. “Roy Cooper would not have run if Thom Tillis had run for re-election.” Former North Carolina Governor Pat McCrory, a Republican, said Trump’s interventions in his party’s primaries had divided Republicans in state after state. Democrat senatorial candidate Roy Cooper and his wife Kristin Cooper celebrate victory during an election night event in Raleigh, North Carolina, the US on November 3, 2026. — AFP In South Carolina, McCrory said, the president went against two local congressmen, a fight that “really divided the party”, an example, in his telling, of a president spending his political capital against his own side. McCrory’s sharpest criticism was aimed at Trump’s connection with the voters who built his coalition. “I think President Trump’s greatest strength was that he had a common touch with the working-class people,” McCrory said. “He lost that skill. He better regain that skill for the good of the country.”

items.title: Asif says Chaudhry Salik's remarks about corruption in Punjab 'beyond my understanding'
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”. During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader had lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi. However, he had also criticised the present provincial administration, headed by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption. On Tuesday, CM Maryam had sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to the minister, demanding that he retract his remarks. In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own. “His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding. Corruption is the biggest issue in our society and it is the collective responsibility of the political leadership, both at the central and provincial levels, to rid the country of this curse,” he said. He went on to say that Salik was a part of “both the federal and provincial governments and the leadership of both these governments lies with the PML-N”. “If this statement is part of some future political agenda — to target Maryam Nawaz’s government and carve out space for himself in Punjab and at the Centre to secure his political future — then it starts to make sense,” he said. He also praised Maryam’s performance, saying her work across Punjab’s cities and villages and the service standards being set by her government would pose a “very difficult challenge” for its opponents. What did Salik say? During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending , particularly the use of official aircraft , arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips. He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance. The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote. While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab. On Tuesday, CM Maryam said the PML-Q leader’s anger stemmed neither from corruption nor progress. She said the issue was that she had changed the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days earlier, whereas Salik wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed. The defamation notice — sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman — said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province. The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question. It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages. Meanwhile, responding to Maryam’s remarks, Salik said he stood by his statement and had responded honestly to a question during the interview. The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request to appoint a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.
